headline: 21 is the new political age: Revanth Reddy seeks lower age to contest MLA, MP polls
full_text:
21 is the new political age: Revanth Reddy seeks lower age to contest MLA, MP polls
A Revanth Reddy said Telangana will move a resolution to lower the minimum age for contesting Assembly and Lok Sabha elections to 21. He presented it as a push for stronger youth representation and wider student participation in national politics.
In a major political pitch aimed at empowering India's youth, Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Saturday announced that his government would move a resolution in the State Assembly urging the Centre to reduce the minimum age to contest Assembly and Lok Sabha elections from 25 years to 21 years.
Addressing a massive Gen Z rally in Hyderabad, Revanth Reddy said the time had come to give young Indians a greater role in shaping the country's future. "If a 21-year-old can become an IAS officer, contest local body elections, and even serve the nation through the civil services, why can't they contest Assembly and Parliament elections?" he asked.
The Chief Minister said the Telangana government would convene a special session of the Assembly and Legislative Council in the first week of August to pass a resolution seeking the constitutional amendment. He added that Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge would pursue the issue in Parliament.
Making a strong case for lowering the age limit, Revanth Reddy cited former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's decision to reduce the voting age from 21 to 18 through the 61st Constitutional Amendment and PV Narasimha Rao's 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, which enabled 21-year-olds to contest local body elections. He also referred to countries such as Germany, the United Kingdom and Singapore, where younger leaders are allowed to contest elections at an earlier age.
The Chief Minister said Gen Z accounts for nearly 30 per cent of India's population but has less than one per cent representation in Parliament. "India's future lies in the hands of its youth. The country's legislatures must reflect that reality," he said.
Revanth Reddy also praised the nationwide Gen Z movement over the alleged NEET paper leak, claiming it had compelled the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. He demanded that the Centre withdraw cases filed against protesting students and provide compensation to the families of students who allegedly died by suicide in connection with the controversy.
Calling the movement a victory for India's youth rather than any political party, the Chief Minister urged young people to continue their fight for justice and greater representation. "This tsunami of youth must not stop here. The voice of Gen Z should be heard from Jantar Mantar to Parliament," he said.

headline: Dharmendra Pradhan steps down, Gen Z steps up
full_text:
Dharmendra Pradhan steps down, Gen Z steps up
Minister Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of education, BJP leaders rally behind Pradhan after he resigns.
A 36-day stir by students achieved a landmark victory on Saturday as education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of sweeping protests that brought central Delhi to a halt, energised a moribund Opposition, and heralded the entry of a new generation of young people into politics.
The sprawling sit-in in Delhi’s historic Jantar Mantar was called off hours after the resignation was announced by the minister on X with leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) saying the government had accepted two other demands – compensation of ₹1 crore to the kin of every student who died by suicide following irregularities in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test, and the withdrawal of all first information reports against students who undertook a massive march to Parliament earlier this week.
“We have won. Gandhi has won. Ambedkar has won,” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said from the makeshift stage in Jantar Mantar as news trickled into the heavily barricaded site.
This is the first time that a popular street protest has forced the resignation of a Union minister in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government’s three terms. Union consumer affairs minister Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the education ministry.
Also read: Fear of losing Gen Z, poll math forced BJP's hand in Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Celebrations erupted soon after as young men and women – many of them Gen Z -- waved the Tricolour, climbed barricades and broke into impromptu jigs as makeshift loudspeakers belted out Bollywood favourites. Many briefly interrupted festivities to stand in attention and loudly sing along to the national anthem and Saare Jahan Se Acha, before unfurling their banners and posters featuring memes and slogans hitting out at the government.
“Our generation did it. We showed them that you cannot call us terrorists, hit us, and go scot free,” said Nachiket Malhotra, 22.
Pradhan – one of the seniormost ministers in the Cabinet who was a part of the council of ministers since Prime Minister Narendra Modi swept to power in 2014 and the longest serving education minister in almost two decades – announced his dramatic resignation on X.
In his two-page note in Hindi, the minister said he was disturbed to see the events of the past 10 days, and said he had resolved to not let the youth get ensnared in the web of confusion.
“Considering the situation at Jantar Mantar and across the country-with the aim of preventing anti-national forces from exploiting it, preserving national unity, ensuring that not a single Indian student’s future gets entangled in legal complexities, and allowing our children to devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers-I have submitted my resignation to prime minister,” he said.
“It is not a matter of individual prestige for me,” he added.
Rashtrapati Bhavan accepted his resignation even as senior ministers and Bharatiya Janata Party leaders rallied behind him. “His contribution to public service has been inclusive, future-ready, and aligned with the aspirations of a New India,” defence minister Rajnath Singh said on X.
Hours later, CJP representatives Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das met Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh – for the third time in as many days – and announced later that the government had accepted all their demands. The two sides will again meet after four weeks to discuss broader reforms in the examination system, the CJP said.
Also read: NEET can’t continue as a make-or-break exam
“The CJP declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith and understanding that the agreed-upon terms will be executed within the agreed-upon timeline,” Das said at a joint press conference with Nadda and Singh.
“As the government accepted all our demands after 36 days of protests, we appeal to everyone to peacefully withdraw from protest sites and go home,” Ranka said.
Das said they have shared a draft of the demands with the government and the government will share a written guarantee by Tuesday. There was no word on the demand for an apology from the government over clashes on July 20.
Nadda said the CJP representatives came to the meeting with a written draft on cases filed during the July 20 agitation. Delhi Police have filed at least 15 FIRs in connection with the protest when tens of thousands of young people broke barricades, braved tear gas shells and batons to march to Parliament.
Nadda said the government also discussed demands of no retaliatory measures against agitators, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died, and a five-point CJP charter.
Also read: New paper leak bill prescribes 2-month window for probes, speedy trials
“After the discussion, the first point was that no action should be taken and no FIRs should be filed. If any FIRs have already been registered, whether by the Delhi Police or in BJP-ruled states, it will be withdrawn,” Nadda said, adding that the government agreed to give “honourable compensation within the rules” to the families of NEET suicide victims.
“All our demands have been accepted by the government,” Das said. Nadda said the government will provide to CJP copies of FIRs registered.
The announcements drew a dramatic denouement to the sweeping protests that were birthed by a controversial comment by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant describing unemployed people and dubious degree holders earlier this year.
“I thank CJI Surya Kant ji for calling us cockroaches. If you had not called us cockroaches, I would not have returned to India. If you hadn’t called us cockroaches, the youth would not have been on the roads,” Dipke said at Jantar Mantar to cheers.
The CJP first garnered millions of followers on social media before launching an indefinite sit-in protest on June 20 demanding the resignation of Pradhan over repeated question paper leaks – including one earlier this year. After days of tepid crowds, the movement was galvanised by the hunger strike and forcible removal of activist Sonam Wangchuk last week.
Crowds swelled through the weekend and by Monday morning, columns of people –– many of them students, first-time agitators and young professionals –– had defied a steady drizzle and police barricading to join what became the largest street protests in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s third term. Over 100 protesters and 129 security personnel were injured. One protester remains in the ICU.
Over the past week, crowds swelled and spilled beyond the confines of Jantar Mantar as thousands of young people poured into central Delhi, despite the longest spells of internet shutdown and metro station closure in Delhi, scores of barricades that sparked traffic snarls across the Capital, and controversial police detention from roads over protesters carrying posters or pepper spray. Tensions sporadically flared at the site, most dramatically on Wednesday night when clashes between protesters and police led to injuries to five agitators and five police personnel.
As the storm of Gen Z protesters grew, the government’s efforts to break the impasse kicked into overdrive. Nadda and Singh convinced Wangchuk to break his fast, Modi made a rare personal appeal to young people on Instagram and promised a stringent new bill – which will come before Parliament on Monday – to tackle paper leaks, and the National Testing Agency fired top officials. The police continues to be under fire over allegations of excess force used to scatter crowds on July 20; the Supreme Court is set to hear two appeals on Monday even as four people have alleged that the security forces used pellet guns on them – an unprecedented occurrence in the Capital.
But on Saturday afternoon, as an avalanche of people – many of them school students, many first-time protesters who had never stepped outside campuses before, many who travelled a night or more to be there – thronged Jantar Mantar, the jubilation around their achievement had washed away the bitterness. “Everyone thought we were lazy, we don’t know anything beyond Instagram or our phones,” said Nikita Joshi, 19. “Today, our generation raised its voice.”

headline: New Delhi: The Rajya Sabha Wednesday passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amid a heated debate, with the Opposition questioning the intent of the Bill and maintaining that reverence to the national song doesn’t ...
full_text:
New Delhi: The Rajya Sabha Wednesday passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amid a heated debate, with the Opposition questioning the intent of the Bill and maintaining that reverence to the national song doesn’t come through legislation. The government said that opposing the national song Vande Mataram amounts to boosting the morale of the “Bharat tere tukde honge gang”.
The Act penalises insults to the national flag, the Constitution of India, and the national anthem. The Bill would give Vande Mataram the same statutory protection as the national anthem. The Bill was discussed amid Opposition staging protest and shouting slogans demanding a response from Union Home Minister Amit Shah over police action against protesters last week. Opposition members later staged a walkout in the middle of the debate.
During the debate on the Bill, RJD MP Prof Manoj Kumar Jha asked, “I am seeing for the first time that my national anthem and national song are being pitted against each other. Subhash Babu is being pitted against Nehru ji. What are we doing?”
He asserted that “reverence cannot be legislated”, and asked whether the slogan, “Vande Mataram. Kar le thodi sharam” will be considered an insult. Saying that during his student days, they used to raise this slogan, he asserted that he was asking this question on behalf of the youth of the country.
BJP MP Dr Radha Mohan Das Agrawal alleged that Vande Mataram was being insulted for the past 123 years, and claimed that the national song was never discussed in the Constituent Assembly. He alleged that “not just today’s Congress, but even the Congress of the time of Independence struggle” consistently insulted the national song.
Quoting several revolutionaries who sang Vande Mataram, he said, “Because revolutionaries drew inspiration from this song, members of the Congress felt inferior because of the song, they used to feel a sense of their own smallness.”
Agrawal referred to the 1923 Kakinada session of the Congress, whose president Muhammad Ali Jauhar protested when the singer Vishnu Digambar Paluskar rose to render the song.
He said, “In the 1923 session of the Indian National Congress, when the then-Congress president insulted Vande Mataram and said the song won’t be sung in the Congress session, they didn’t have the courage to remove that president, that Muslim League’s dalal, that anti-Indian who allowed Afghan attack on India, from the Congress…They laid the foundation for the Partition during the Non-Cooperation Movement.”
AAP MP Sanjay Singh said it was “laughable that such a bill is being brought by a party which didn’t have the Indian flag at the RSS headquarters for 52 years”.
“Today, people are talking about bringing in a strict law against (insult of) Vande Mataram. There is a patrika called Organiser which wrote in 1949 that the national anthem is an item of entertainment. You insulted that national anthem, there should be proceedings against such organisations, who insulted the national anthem and the national flag,” Singh added.
The AAP MP asked, “Why don’t you unfurl the flag at Sangh Shakhas?”, urging for a Bill for proceedings against people who have insulted the national flag and the national anthem as well.
In his response, Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai said the Bill was not just a legislative change but a “collective commitment to the soul of India, national consciousness, cultural heritage, and the ideals of the freedom struggle”.
“I don’t know why these 1-2 people are opposed to Vande Mataram. I don’t understand what opposition the Congress has towards Vande Mataram,” he added.
Nityanand Rai further said that the original 1971 law punishes insults to the national flag, the Constitution, and the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana. The amendment, he said, ensures the same respect and punishment for insult of the national song as well.
Rai then asserted, “Being against Vande Mataram means that the Congress always adopts the policy of polarisation to undermine the pride of the nation…Why is the Opposition against Vande Mataram? Opposing the Vande Mataram amounts to boosting the morale of ‘Bharat tere tukde honge’ gang. But the country’s youth, farmers, women and workers, won’t tolerate the slogan, Bharat tere tukde honge. Such people will be taught a lesson.”
He said that Swami Vivekananda had made a prediction that the 21st century would be India’s. “Swami Vivekananda’s childhood name was Narendra. One Narendra made a prediction, and it is being fulfilled by the world’s most popular leader, the messiah of the poor, the bringer of development, honorable Shri Narendra Modi ji.”
Respect of national symbols should be above any politics, he said, asserting that this Bill isn’t against any person or ideology, and is in the interest of the nation’s dignity and “our shared national consciousness”.
(Edited by Gitanjali Das)

headline: PM Modi forgives students amid abusive video row: 'Let's guide the misguided'
full_text:
PM Modi forgives students amid abusive video row: 'Let's guide the misguided'
In a video message, PM Modi said the language used by some protesters was unfit for a civilised society, but urged people to reform, not punish, the students.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said he was forgiving students who hurled abuses at him and his late mother during the Jantar Mantar protest, describing them as "misguided children" who deserve guidance rather than punishment or prolonged legal action.
In a video message shared on his social media handles, the Prime Minister said the language used by some protesters "would not suit any civilised society", but appealed to people to help reform the students instead of seeking retribution.
Also Read | 'When will BJP face cases?': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke on FIR against woman over anti-Modi remarks
"Some mischievous children used very filthy abuses... Abuses were directed at me, and abuses were directed at my late mother as well."
Modi said that while society's anger was understandable, particularly over the language allegedly used by young women, the focus should be on showing them the right path rather than pushing them into legal battles.
"These are misguided children, and showing them the way is our duty; we will not be able to change circumstances by punishing them, making them run around the courts, or harassing them in society."
The Prime Minister said he wanted to forgive the students and urged society to do the same. Drawing an analogy, he said that just as people do not break their teeth after accidentally biting their tongue, society should not abandon its own children for their mistakes.
"Sometimes our tongue comes under our teeth and blood comes out, but we do not break our teeth—because the teeth are ours, and the tongue is ours too. The children are also ours."
Calling on the students to move on from the episode, Modi invited them to contribute to nation-building.
"Children, come, let us move forward together for the country. Let us learn something new, let us learn even from mistakes... I live for you, I toil for your bright future, so come, let us together take the country forward."
The Prime Minister's remarks comes on the same day a Zero FIR was registered over a viral video showing a woman allegedly using abusive language against him during the recent Jantar Mantar protest.
The FIR, initially lodged in Noida on July 29 based on a complaint, was transferred to the Delhi Police on Friday as the alleged offence occurred within the national capital's jurisdiction. Police officials said they will first examine the contents of the Zero FIR before deciding the next course of action.

headline: New Delhi: One of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s most visible faces on social media and TV channels, Shehzad Poonawalla on Friday removed all reference to the BJP from his X bio, triggering speculation about his resignation from the party.
full_text:
New Delhi: One of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s most visible faces on social media and TV channels, Shehzad Poonawalla on Friday removed all reference to the BJP from his X bio, triggering speculation about his resignation from the party.
However, there has been no official confirmation of the BJP spokesperson quitting the party. Poonawalla didn’t respond to calls and messages from ThePrint.
His updated bio now reads, “Religion, Islam, Culture, Hindu, ideology-Bhartiya, Author: GST ki Yatra; Lifelong follower of PM Narendra Modi.”
Poonawalla also shared a screenshot of the revised bio on X. In his updated bio, Poonawalla describes himself as a “lifelong follower” of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
However, his current bio on Instagram still mentions “BJP Spokesperson”.
Poonawalla had joined the BJP after he quit the Congress in December 2017.
The change in his bio has raised eyebrows as he had hinted a few days back that the time had come to move on from active politics.
On Friday, he reposted videos of interviews in which he had made those remarks.
— Shehzad Jai Hind (@Shehzad_Ind) July 30, 2026
— Shehzad Jai Hind (@Shehzad_Ind) July 30, 2026
A lawyer by training, Poonawalla grabbed headlines in 2017 when he termed the Congress presidential election process as rigged and claimed it was rigged in favour of Rahul Gandhi to elevate him to the post of party president. He had quit the party following this controversy.
ThePrint had reported that at the time of his quitting, he alleged that Congress leaders treated him very shabbily despite his repeated attempts to get in touch with Rahul’s office before his public outburst.
PM Modi used his claims to hit out at the Congress and the rival party’s presidential elections.
Shehzad is the brother of political analyst Tehseen Poonawalla, and they had a very public split, when Shehzad openly criticized the Congress leadership’s internal elections, which led to Tehseen distancing himself from him.
The BJP spokesperson is from Pune and comes from a well-off Aga Khan Muslim family. He started working for the Congress in 2008. Poonawalla studied law and interned with Congress leader Suresh Kalmadi before joining the All India Congress Committee (AICC) as a volunteer. After completing his course in 2008, he interned with the Congress’ media research team in Delhi.
He had been the vice-president of the Pune wing of the National Students Union of India and also worked in the AICC’s media cell. After quitting the Congress, he joined the BJP wherein he was first given responsibility at the state level and was later elevated to the position of the national spokesperson.

headline: Six dead as heavy rain batters Kerala, rescue operations continue
full_text:
Six dead as heavy rain batters Kerala, rescue operations continue
Four of the deaths occurred in separate landslides in Idukki and Kottayam districts, where several others were rescued.
Heavy rains lashed several parts of Kerala on Saturday, triggering landslides, inundating low-lying areas, swelling rivers and dams, and prompting authorities to launch large-scale rescue and evacuation operations in affected regions.
A statement from the CMO said six people were killed in rain-related incidents across the state.
Four of the deaths occurred in separate landslides in Idukki and Kottayam districts, where several others were rescued.
Search operations for the six missing persons continued with personnel from the National Disaster Response Force, Fire and Rescue Services, police, the Coast Guard, the local administration, public representatives and residents participating in the efforts, the statement said.
The statement said 65 relief camps had been opened across the state, providing shelter to 1,465 people.
Chief Minister V D Satheesan said 17 houses had been destroyed and another 127 had suffered partial damage in rain-related incidents.
Two separate fatal landslides were reported in Idukki district.
The deceased was identified as Sumathi (65), a resident of Adoormala near Kudayathoor in Idukki district.
Her husband, Ravi, and their son, Ratheesh, were rescued and admitted to hospital, officials said.
In another incident, Prabhakaran Nair (77) of Vaikom died after a landslide hit the house of his relative in the Vagamon area of Idukki district.
A youth died, and his mother was trapped under debris after a landslide at Payyanithottam in Poonjar in Kottayam district.
The deceased was identified as Josephine, son of Johny. His mother, Rejina Johny (46), was trapped under debris, officials said.
Following the landslides and flooding, Satheesan directed ministers in charge of rain-hit districts to camp in their respective districts and coordinate rescue and relief operations as heavy rain continued across the state.
He reviewed the situation with ministers and district collectors.
Landslides and flooding hit several parts of Idukki district.
At Upputhara, a parked police jeep was damaged in a landslide. Heavy rain disrupted traffic at multiple locations.
Vehicle movement on the Kochi-Dhanushkodi National Highway was affected following a landslide near Cheeyapara.
Rising water levels in the Chottupara stream at Vandiperiyar led to waterlogging on National Highway 183.
In neighbouring Kottayam district, heavy rain triggered widespread flooding in Erattupetta, Kanjirappally, Koottickal, Erumeli and Pala, inundating commercial and residential areas, disrupting traffic and prompting rescue operations.
Four houses were damaged in a landslide at Teekoy village, but residents escaped unhurt, officials said.
Around 2,500 chickens died after floodwaters entered a poultry farm at Pala in Kottayam.
The poultry farm, owned by Jineesh Alex of Mulaykkal House, has been operating for the past 18 years.
More landslides were reported from the hilly areas of Pathanamthitta district.
Ranni MLA Pazhakulam Madhu, in a social media post, said heavy flooding had been reported in Ranni and adjoining areas.
As water entered shops and houses, people were shifted to relief camps.
Several parts of Ranni, Kozhencherry and Aranmula, located along the banks of the Pampa river, were cut off due to flooding.
The district administration deployed boats to rescue people trapped in their houses, officials said.
Besides the central Kerala districts, floods and minor landslides were reported in Ernakulam, Thrissur, Kozhikode, Malappuram, Kannur, Kasaragod and Palakkad districts.
Engapuzha town in Kozhikode was completely inundated after river water entered the area following heavy rain.
Landslides were reported from several high-range areas of Kozhikode and Kannur districts, officials said.
Traffic on ghat roads in Wayanad and Idukki was regulated following minor landslides in those areas.
Kerala Revenue Minister A P Anilkumar said the government was fully prepared to deal with landslides, flooding and other rain-related emergencies.
"We have already opened relief camps wherever required. Even if the intensity of the rain decreases, people living in high-risk areas will be shifted to camps as a precautionary measure," he said.
Shutters of dams in Thiruvananthapuram, Pathanamthitta, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur and Kannur districts were opened following rising water levels.
The shutters of the Thottappally spillway and barrages in Alappuzha district were also opened to prevent flooding.
Sea incursion affected coastal areas of Ernakulam, Alappuzha, Kozhikode, Kannur and Kasaragod districts, officials said.
The India Meteorological Department had issued a 'red alert' forecasting very heavy rainfall in Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.
An 'orange alert' was issued for Ernakulam, Thrissur and Palakkad districts.
Kerala State Disaster Management Authority member secretary Sekhar Lukose Kuriakos said exceptionally heavy rainfall in central Kerala had triggered landslides, mudslides and flooding across several districts.
A 'red alert' indicates extremely heavy rainfall of over 204 mm in 24 hours, while an 'orange alert' means very heavy rainfall of 115 mm to 204 mm.

headline: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday (August 1, 2026) assured exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin of security in the State, saying the “days of threats are over”.
full_text:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday (August 1, 2026) assured exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin of security in the State, saying the “days of threats are over”.
Sharing the stage with Ms. Nasrin at Kolkata’s Rabindra Sadan at an event that marked the writer’s return to the city after 19 years, Ms. Adhikari said: “You are most welcome to Bengal. Please come here whenever you want and as many times as you wish. Your safety is my responsibility.”
Ms. Nasrin was exiled from Bangladesh in 1994 over her writings after which she started living in Europe and then in Kolkata. But she had to leave Kolkata in November 2007, when violence erupted in the city after some organisations called for action against the author over her books. The violence reached such alarming proportions that the Army had to be deployed in the city to contain the situation. She had blamed the Left Front government and the Trinamool Congress government for not allowing her to return to the city.
She reached Kolkata on Friday (July 31, 2026) to attend the event at Rabindra Sadan.
The Chief Minister said Ms. Nasrin’s return indicated that not only had the face of the government changed but the entire system too. “This Bengal is free from any barriers and chains. Every single pillar of the Constitution is safe here. We all have the righteous opportunity for freedom of speech,” said Mr. Adhikari, welcoming the writer with a portrait of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, the writer of national song Vande Mataram.
Veteran BJP leader and former Tripura Governor Tathagata Roy also shared the stage with the writer. The audience comprised a number of State Ministers, including Swapan Dasgupta, Agnimitra Paul, and Kalyan Chakrabarti.
Thanks CM
“I have always questioned this city. Did I ever harm you [Kolkata]? I haven’t come for any answer today. I have come back to Kolkata with tears in my eyes and also immense love in my heart. This was my dream for the last 19 years. History remembers who shut this door. Now, history will also remember who opened this door again,” said Ms. Nasrin, expressing gratitude to the West Bengal Chief Minister for facilitating her return.
“It is still painful that a writer had to return to the city of her own language with such high security. I am thankful to the government. But my gratitude is not my allegiance to any party. I have not come here for any political party. I came here to express my voice over women’s liberty and freedom of speech,” the 63-year-old writer said at the event.

headline: DMK moves SC seeking immediate release of Cauvery water from Karnataka to Tamil Nadu
full_text:
DMK moves SC seeking immediate release of Cauvery water from Karnataka to Tamil Nadu
Edited by: Vijaya Srivastava / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 01, 2026, 20:48 IST
Comments
Share

Responding to the growing protests in Karnataka, chief minister DK Shivakumar appealed on Saturday to organisations opposing the release of water to withdraw their proposed agitation.
NEW DELHI: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday moved the Supreme Court seeking directions to the Karnataka government to immediately release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, arguing that Karnataka must comply with the apex court's 2018 verdict and the recent directions issued by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA).The plea seeks an order directing Karnataka to implement the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's recommendation, upheld by the CWMA on Thursday, to release 3,500 cusecs of water per day for 15 days to Tamil Nadu at the inter-state border point of Biligundlu."Direct the State of Karnataka / Respondent No. 1 to forthwith and fully implement the direction of the CWRC dated July 28, 2026, as affirmed by the CWMA on July 30, 2026, by ensuring a flow of 3,500 cusecs per day at Biligundlu for the period of 15 days commencing from date of the order passed by this Hon'ble Court, and to make good the shortfall in compliance from July 29, 2026 onwards," the DMK said in its plea.The party also sought a direction to Karnataka to clear the accumulated shortfall in water releases. It asked the court to direct the state to "make good the accumulated backlog of about 9.46 TMC due at Biligundlu as on July 26, 2026, computed on the pro-rata/distress-sharing basis, by ensuring releases such that about 7,000 cusecs per day is realised at Biligundlu over a period of 15 days".In addition, the DMK urged the Supreme Court to direct the CWMA to monitor reservoir releases in Karnataka and the flows realised at Biligundlu on a day-to-day basis and submit compliance reports.
The move comes amid renewed tensions between the two southern states over the sharing of Cauvery waters during the current monsoon season. On Thursday, the CWMA upheld the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's recommendation that Karnataka release 3,500 cusecs of water daily for the next 15 days to Tamil Nadu.Responding to the growing protests in Karnataka, chief minister DK Shivakumar appealed on Saturday to organisations opposing the release of water to withdraw their proposed agitation. The farmer groups and pro-Kannada organisations staged demonstrations across the Cauvery basin, arguing that the state could not spare even a drop of water for Tamil Nadu because major reservoirs did not have enough water even for drinking.Shivakumar said the Kabini reservoir was rapidly filling up and warned that water could not be retained once the reservoir reached full capacity."Kabini reservoir is filling up. Once a dam is full, water has to be released. It is impossible to hold it back. I humbly appeal to those planning to agitate against the release of water to withdraw their decision," he said.Shivakumar also cautioned protesters against approaching water release points, saying, "Even if we decide not to release water, once the reservoir is full, it is impossible to hold it back. Protesters should not go near the points where water is being released. The force of the water can sweep you away. No one should lie down in the path of flowing water."The Karnataka CM said the state would protect the interests of its farmers while respecting judicial orders. "There is an order to release 177 TMC of water to Tamil Nadu, and the Supreme Court has upheld it. We must respect the court's order while also protecting the interests of our farmers. Our government is committed to safeguarding the welfare of Karnataka's farmers," he said.
He also accused the BJP of "politicising" the issue and said an all-party meeting would be held to consult former chief ministers, political leaders and legal experts before deciding the state's next course of action. According to Shivakumar, Tamil Nadu had sought 9,000 cusecs, but the Authority had directed Karnataka to release only 3,500 cusecs.The Cauvery Water Management Authority was constituted by the Centre in 2018 following the Supreme Court's final verdict on the decades-old Cauvery river water dispute among Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala and Puducherry. The Authority includes representatives of the riparian states as well as a nominee of the central government and is responsible for overseeing implementation of the court-mandated water-sharing arrangement.

Watch: Pro-Channi sloganeering draws Congress' ire amid Punjab leadership tussle

NEW DELHI: Congress' internal rift in Punjab showed no signs of easing on Saturday after supporters of former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi disrupted two party programmes by raising slogans in his favour, prompting AICC general secretary in charge of Punjab Bhupesh Baghel to warn that anyone indulging in indiscipline would be expelled from the party.The slogan shouting took place during the Congress' 'Har Booth, Congress Mazboot' programmes in Patiala and Sangrur, where Baghel, Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and several senior leaders were present.Despite the disruption, Baghel reiterated that the Congress high command would decide the party's chief ministerial face only after the Punjab Assembly elections, due early next year.
Channi supporters disrupt Congress meetings
The disruption began in Patiala soon after Warring started addressing party workers. Channi's supporters raised slogans including "Charanjit Singh Channi Zindabad", "Channi Teri Soch Te Pehra Deyange Thok Ke" and "Channi Liyao, Punjab Bachao", briefly bringing the programme to a halt.
A visibly upset Warring repeatedly appealed to workers to maintain discipline and allow the meeting to continue but the slogan shouting persisted for some time before proceedings resumed.Senior Congress leaders, including Baghel, MP Amar Singh and Brahm Mohindra, witnessed the developments while other leaders attempted to calm the workers.
Similar scenes unfolded later in Sangrur, where another group of Channi supporters raised slogans in favour of the former chief minister and against Baghel. Tensions escalated after some of Channi's supporters clashed verbally with other Congress workers.
One supporter demanded that the Jalandhar MP be declared the Congress' chief ministerial face, claiming it reflected the wishes of party workers.However, Warring dismissed suggestions that Channi had orchestrated the protests."Channi did not send these people. He is our crown," Warring said in Sangrur, while alleging that the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) had sent people to disrupt the Congress programme.
Baghel says CM face will be decided after polls
Addressing party workers, Baghel urged leaders to remain united and focus on defeating the ruling AAP, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal instead of engaging in internal rivalries.He made it clear that the Congress leadership, including party president Mallikarjun Kharge and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, would decide the chief ministerial candidate and ministers only after the Assembly elections."Smaller differences are part of every party which can be sorted out for the bigger battle that the Congress has to fight against AAP, BJP and Akalis," Baghel said.He expressed confidence that the Congress would emerge stronger in the Assembly elections because everyone shared the common objective of bringing the party back to power in Punjab.Baghel also underlined the importance of strengthening the party at the booth level, saying a strong grassroots organisation would be key to electoral success.
Warning on indiscipline
Later, speaking to reporters in Patiala, Baghel issued a stern warning against indiscipline."Whosoever indulges in indiscipline will be shown the door from the party irrespective of the position one holds," he said, citing the earlier expulsion of Navjot Kaur Sidhu as an example.
When asked whether the party would initiate action against Channi, Baghel responded by asking what mistake the former chief minister had committed.Warring, meanwhile, announced that former MLA Madan Lal Jalalpur had been suspended for remarks against senior Congress leaders.Rejecting reports that some leaders had stayed away from district committee meetings, Baghel said all leaders had been informed about the programmes and were participating as their schedules permitted.
Warring stresses organisation over individuals
In his address, Warring stressed that no leader, regardless of popularity, could win elections without a strong organisational structure.He cited the example of late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala, saying that despite his immense popularity, he lost the 2022 Assembly election by over 60,000 votes because of inadequate booth-level management.Warring also said his only wish was to see a Congress chief minister and ministers taking oath after the next Assembly elections, adding that he would be happy to watch the swearing-in ceremony from the audience.He described senior leaders including Channi, Partap Singh Bajwa, Rajinder Kaur Bhattal and Brahm Mohindra as more experienced and capable than himself, and assured workers that all senior leaders would soon be seen sharing one platform ahead of the polls.
The latest developments indicate continuing factionalism within the Punjab Congress despite repeated assurances from the party leadership that organisational unity is being strengthened ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Baghel is currently touring the poll-bound state as part of the 'Har Booth, Congress Mazboot' campaign, meeting district and block-level leaders after launching the initiative in Fatehgarh Sahib and Mohali on Friday.Baghel had earlier dismissed reports of factionalism, claiming that the media and a few individuals were creating a perception of infighting.However, discontent within the state unit has continued since the Congress retained Amarinder Singh Raja Warring as Punjab Congress president while appointing Channi as chairman of the campaign committee.A section of leaders led by Channi and Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa had opposed Warring's continuation as state chief and sought his removal.

headline: Karnataka cabinet expansion likely next week, Congress govt to finalise list by Sunday
full_text:
Karnataka cabinet expansion likely next week, Congress govt to finalise list by Sunday
Congress set to finalize the Karnataka Cabinet expansion. Discussions focused on ensuring representation across various communities and balancing young leaders.
The Congress high command is expected to settle the long delayed expansion of the Karnataka Cabinet by Sunday night, clearing the way for a swearing in ceremony likely to be held on Monday, state Congress leaders said after a series of discussions in New Delhi.
The final list of ministers is expected to reflect the party’s calculations on caste, religion, regional representation and the balance between younger leaders, major communities and groups that remain underrepresented. Congress leaders also discussed whether to leave three or four ministerial positions vacant until the completion of Gram Panchayat and other local body elections.
‘Waiting for results’
Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee president BK Hariprasad said the consultations were effectively complete and that the party was now awaiting a decision from the central leadership. “We have written the exam, and now we are waiting for the results,” Hariprasad, a KPCC president and MLC, told reporters.
Also Read | 'Leak double, trauma triple': Raghav Chadha targets Congress over Karnataka exam paper leaks
He said chief minister DK Shivakumar, former chief minister Siddaramaiah and senior Congress leaders had held several rounds of discussions on the expansion.
Shivakumar, Hariprasad said, would decide the timing of the swearing in after considering the almanac and what he described as auspicious hours.
Kharge, Rahul Gandhi's meet with Shivakumar, Siddaramaiah
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi held a detailed hour-long meeting with Shivakumar, Siddaramaiah, Hariprasad, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal and Karnataka in charge general secretary Randeep Surjewala. State leaders presented a list of legislators being considered for ministerial positions, and the central leadership discussed the names individually.
Siddaramaiah argued that the selection should give priority to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and minority communities. Shivakumar sought what party leaders described as a broader balance, including younger legislators, major communities and groups that have had less representation.
Also Read | Saini says Congress ‘misleading’ youth on paper leaks
The chief minister also argued that the composition of the ministry should be considered with the 2028 Assembly election in mind.
After the meeting, Gandhi asked the Karnataka leaders to return to Bengaluru and said the final list would be sent on Sunday night. Shivakumar indicated that he preferred the swearing in ceremony to be held Monday. Basavaraj Rayareddy, a former minister and a close aide of Siddaramaiah, said the talks had ended positively and that Monday was the most likely date for the ceremony.
The leadership also considered appointments to the posts of Assembly Speaker, Legislative Council chairman and chief whips in both Houses. The nomination of five seats in the Legislative Council was discussed as well. The Karnataka council of ministers can have 34 members, including the chief minister. Only 14 ministers are currently in place, leaving 20 positions unfilled. The prolonged vacancy has led to sustained lobbying by Congress legislators seeking induction into the government.

headline: Dipke questions PM Modi after his message to students who hurled abuses: ‘Is this forgiveness only for the reel?’
full_text:
Dipke questions PM Modi after his message to students who hurled abuses: ‘Is this forgiveness only for the reel?’
PM Modi in a video said he was forgiving students who hurled abuses at him and his late mother during the Jantar Mantar protest, saying they were “misguided”
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke responded to an Instagram video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi about the students who had abused him, questioning whether the Prime Minister's message was "only for the camera."
In the video, PM Modi said he was forgiving students who hurled abuses at him and his late mother during the Jantar Mantar protest, saying they were “misguided” and deserve guidance rather than punishment. Dipke commented on the video, asking whether the government would also withdrawn cases against the student protesters.
“Sirf reel par hi maaf karoge ya cases bhi vapas loge? (Will you forgive them only in a reel/on camera, or will you also withdraw the cases)” Dipke asked.
The Prime Minister's video came on the same day a girl was booked for allegedly using abusive and objectionable language against him during the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar on July 23. The girl, who was identified as a 25-year-old in the FIR, has reportedly apologised for her remarks in a video message, wherein she said she was just 15.
“I came under the influence of some people at the protest and said a lot of bad things against the Prime Minister,” she said, according to NDTV, India Today and several other media outlets.
In the video, she said the incident was her “first and last mistake”, and extended an apology to the entire country. HT could not independently verify the authenticity of the video.
‘Let’s guide the misguided': PM Modi
In his video on his official Instagram account, PM Modi said the language used by some protesters “would not suit any civilised society”, but urged people to help reform those students. “Abuses never solve anything. Let’s guide the misguided. Let’s work together. Let’s work for Bharat,” the caption for the video said.
PM Modi said “some mischievous children” had directed abuses towards him and his late mother. The Prime Minister said that while society's anger was understandable, particularly over the language allegedly used by young women, the focus should be on showing them the right path rather than pushing them into legal battles.
The Prime Minister said he wanted to forgive the students and urged society to do the same. “These are misguided children, and showing them the way is our duty; we will not be able to change circumstances by punishing them, making them run around the courts, or harassing them in society,” PM Modi said.
‘When will cases be registered against BJP IT cell people?’: Dipke
Reacting to the FIR against the a woman for allegedly using abusive language against PM Modi, CJP convenor Dipke questioned whether there were “two laws” in the country. In a video shared by CJP on X, Dipke asked why similar action had not been taken in other cases.
“If you are registering cases for abusing, when will cases be registered against those BJP IT cell people who have been using abusive language for women online for years?” Dipke said. In the video, Dipke further cited alleged remarks by BJP leaders in the past.
“Their Member of Parliament, Ramesh Bidhuri ji, what words did he use for a fellow Member of Parliament, everyone remembers that,” he said. He further added, “The CM of UP... even had a video, where he had abused a camera person. So, what is going on? Are there two laws in this country?”

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh's Vizianagaram district, a nearly Rs 5,000 crore project that the state government says will transform North Andhra into a major economic and industrial hub. Calling the airport a key milestone in the state's growth story, the PM said the NDA government was working at "double speed"for the state's development.During his address, the Prime Minister also took a veiled swipe at the Gandhi family, saying airports in the past were often named after "a single family". He said the NDA government had instead chosen to honour national icons by naming airports after figures such as Valmiki, Sant Ravidas and Alluri Sitarama Raju.
The PM was accorded a grand ceremonial welcome, with around 13,500 tribal women performing the traditional Dhimsa dance. The airport premises were adorned with displays celebrating Andhra Pradesh's rich cultural heritage, including Etikoppaka artwork and motifs depicting the state's geographical identity.
PM Modi was received by Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu, deputy chief minister Pawan Kalyan, and union civil aviation minister K Ram Mohan Naidu.
He later witnessed the Dhimsa performance before formally inaugurating the airport.Developed by the GMR Group, the airport has been named after freedom fighter Alluri Sitarama Raju. It has been designed to handle six million passengers annually in its first phase, with a long-term expansion plan to increase capacity to 40 million passengers a year. Commercial flight operations are scheduled to begin on August 17.

While addressing a public gathering in Bhogapuram after the airport's inaugural ceremony, PM Modi said Andhra would emerge as a manufacturing hub under Naidu's leadership. He said the NDA government was working at "double speed" for the state's development, highlighted railway projects worth around Rs 1 lakh crore, noted that the number of airports in India had increased from 74 to 166 over the past 12 years.
The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stone for Andhra Pradesh's first semiconductor manufacturing facility under the India Semiconductor Mission, which is expected to produce around 96 million semiconductor chips annually. In addition, he launched power transmission projects worth over Rs 9,900 crore to strengthen the National Grid and facilitate renewable energy integration from Kurnool and Ananthapuram.He further dedicated to the nation and laid the foundation stone for National Highway projects worth over Rs 1,880 crore, including stretches of NH-365BG, the Tadipatri Bypass on NH-67, and a high-level bridge at Lingasamudram on NH-565. According to the government, these projects will improve regional connectivity, reduce travel time between Visakhapatnam and Hyderabad, ease congestion and enhance road safety.

headline: PM Modi inaugurates Andhra Pradesh’s Bhogapuram international airport
full_text:
PM Modi inaugurates Andhra Pradesh’s Bhogapuram international airport
The airport has been designed to handle six million passengers annually in the first phase, with a master plan to expand capacity to 40 million passengers annually
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the Visakhapatnam Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram and announced that the Centre will extend all its support to the upcoming Visakhapatnam Economic Region, which will play a pivotal role in Andhra Pradesh’s development journey and evolve into one of Asia’s most significant economic hubs.
Modi said it was a matter of pride that the Bhogapuram airport had been named after freedom fighter Alluri Sitarama Raju, who sacrificed his life for the rights of tribal communities.
Modi also said the Centre is committed to creating the necessary infrastructure and ecosystem to transform the region into a major investment and employment destination. He said the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government’s development strategy was centred on attracting investments that would generate employment, increase production, boost exports, and ultimately improve the quality of life for people.
“Investment leads to production, production leads to exports, exports create employment, and employment transforms people’s lives. This is the development model the NDA government is pursuing,” the Prime Minister said.
He described the day as a landmark in Andhra Pradesh’s march towards achieving the ‘Swarna Andhra Vision’, and said projects worth nearly ₹18,000 crore, including the inauguration of the new international airport, were launched.
Calling the airport a “runway and launch pad” for the aspirations of North Andhra’s youth, Modi said it would significantly enhance employment opportunities and regional development.
Modi said the country had only 74 airports before the NDA government came to power, but that number had now increased to 166. “Air connectivity had expanded to smaller towns, while the UDAN regional connectivity scheme had enabled millions of first-time passengers to travel by air,” he said.
He also referred to the expansion of the “Smart Airport” model from Kashi to Amritsar, saying it had strengthened international air connectivity to 25 countries.
He also said people had blessed Andhra Pradesh with a “double-engine government,” enabling the NDA administration under Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan to accelerate development.
Gateway to north Andhra
Described as the “Gateway to North Andhra,” the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram was built at a cost of nearly ₹4,727 crore in a record time of 31 months.
The airport has been designed to handle six million passengers annually in the first phase, with a master plan to expand capacity to 40 million passengers annually in the future.
The project is expected to play a pivotal role in boosting economic growth, tourism, industrial investments, exports, logistics, aerospace and defence sectors across the erstwhile Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts.
The airport has been developed by GMR Visakhapatnam International Airport Limited (GVIAL) under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model using the Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) framework.
The integrated project spans 2,703.26 acres, and includes comprehensive airside infrastructure, commercial development, residential zones and approach roads.
A key highlight is its 3,800-metre Code-E runway, capable of handling wide-body aircraft such as the Boeing 777, Boeing 787 Dreamliner, Airbus A330 and Airbus A340. The airport is also equipped with advanced airfield lighting, navigation aids and CNS/ATM infrastructure to support both domestic and international operations.
Bhogapuram Airport is expected to significantly strengthen North Andhra’s export ecosystem through a 25,000 metric tonne annual capacity cargo terminal.

headline: CBI case against Anil Ambani, Reliance Capital over Rs 1,816 crore EPFO loss
full_text:
CBI case against Anil Ambani, Reliance Capital over Rs 1,816 crore EPFO loss
The CBI has filed an FIR against Reliance Capital and former chairman Anil Ambani over alleged EPFO losses.
The CBI has registered an FIR against Reliance Capital Limited (RCL) and its former chairman Anil D Ambani over allegations that the company caused a loss of Rs 1,816.22 crore to the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).
The case follows a complaint dated July 21 from the Union Ministry of Labour and Employment, which alleged cheating, criminal conspiracy and wrongful loss to the EPFO. Ambani has denied any wrongdoing through his spokesperson.
According to the complaint, now part of the CBI FIR, RCL issued secured non-convertible debentures during 2013 and 2014. The complaint said investments totalling Rs 2,500 crore were made by portfolio managers on behalf of the EPFO in these debentures, with maturity in 2023 and 2024.
The complaint alleged, "The present complaint is being lodged on behalf of EPFO through its authorised officer pursuant to the approval of the competent authority in relation to the substantial loss suffered by the EPFO arising out of its investment in the secured Non-Convertible Debentures issued by Reliance Capital Limited and the subsequently discovered material indicating fraudulent conduct connected with such investment."
It said the Ministry of Labour and Employment sent the complaint after being informed by the Enforcement Directorate that it had found documentary evidence and that a transaction audit by BDO India LLP showed, prima facie, a number of fraudulent transactions by RCL and those in charge of its management between December 7, 2019, and December 6, 2021.
The complaint further alleged, "In addition, during an earlier period as well, various fraudulent transactions have been found which also led to ultimate failure of RCL as a consequence of siphoning off of money of RCL." It said the ED probe prima facie pointed to a series of transactions involving irregular lending, diversion of funds, impairment of security and other acts by RCL that require investigation.
The complaint added, "If established upon investigation, such conduct may have materially contributed to the financial deterioration of RCL, its inability to honour its obligation towards Debenture Holders, and the consequent loss of Rs 1,816.22 crore suffered by EPFO."
Responding to the complaint, Ambani's spokesperson said, "The FIR registered by the CBI pertains to Reliance Capital Limited. Mr. Ambani served as a Non-Executive Director/Chairman of the Board of Reliance Capital Limited from 2005 until November 2021, when the Reserve Bank of India superseded the Board of Directors of the company and appointed an administrator." The spokesperson added, "Anil Ambani denies any wrongdoing, whatsoever, and reserves all rights available to him in law."

âEPFO administered the Employeesâ Provident Fund, Pension Scheme and Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme. NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for compassion towards students accused of abusing him at the Jantar Mantar protest has triggered a fresh response, with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke questioning whether the message of forgiveness would extend beyond words.Reacting to the Prime Minister's selfie-style Instagram video, Dipke wrote, "Fraand, sirf reel par hi maaf karoge ya cases bhi wapas loge?(Friend, will you forgive them only through reels, or will you also withdraw the cases?)"The Prime Minister's video, shared on his official Instagram and X handles on Friday, came after a 15-year old protester from Noida was booked for allegedly using derogatory language against him during at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.In the video, PM Modi said, "Today I just feel like talking to you. The country and the world have witnessed what happened at Jantar Mantar. Some mischievous children used very crude and abusive language, words that do not befit any civilized society. I was personally abused, and even my late mother was subjected to abuse. It was a truly ugly spectacle."Acknowledging the public outrage over the incident, the Prime Minister urged people to view the matter through the lens of reform rather than punishment.
He said that while the students' remarks had understandably outraged society, mistakes are part of growing up. He urged people to forgive them, guide them in the right direction, and help them reform, saying the students had "lost their way" but deserved an opportunity to correct themselves.
The Prime Minister further argued against prolonged legal action and social ostracisation."Punishing them, dragging them through court proceedings, and harassing them in society, none of this will change the situation. I want to forgive them. Society, too, should accept this," PM Modi said, while urging the students to learn from their mistakes and move forward.Earlier, Dipke had questioned the police action and alleged selective enforcement of the law.In a video shared by CJP on X, he said, "If you are registering cases for abusing, when will cases be registered against those BJP IT Cell people who have been using abusive language for women online for years?"He further alleged that several social media users identifying themselves with the BJP had routinely targeted women online."They have been using all kinds of words, not respecting women from any angle. And they proudly wrote in their bio, 'Followed by PM Modi'. Such people have abused girls. When will the case be filed on them?" Dipke said.
Questioning the criminal proceedings, Dipke argued that abusive language, while objectionable, should not automatically attract criminal prosecution.
"If cases are to be filed for abusing, highest number of cases will be filed against the BJP's IT Cell, because they are the ones who have abused women the most. And it will be against BJP's leaders, who have used bad language for years, even inside the Parliament," he said.In a post accompanying the video, CJP asked, "Will an FIR be filed against all those IT Cell members who have been abusing women for the last several years?"This is not the first time Dipke has publicly reacted to one of the Prime Minister's social media videos. Earlier on Thursday, after PM Modi released a video message highlighting the recently passed anti-paper leak legislation, Dipke commented on Instagram, "Your skin is brighter than the country's future."The Prime Minister had described the legislation as a key reform aimed at strengthening the examination system.

The price of commercial LPG reportedly stands at ₹2,738 per cylinder in Delhi and ₹2,872 per cylinder in Kolkata as of Sunday, August 1.
The prices of 19kg commercial LPG has been reduced by in Delhi and Kolkata, with no change in rates of domestic LPG, news agency ANI reported on Sunday citing sources.

The last time commercial LPG rates saw a drop was on July 1, when oil marketing companies brought down rates by ₹183.50, bringing the retail price in Delhi down to ₹2,930 per cylinder.
Vendors reacts to price drop
Shop owners and vendors welcomed the further reduction in commercial LPG rates on Sunday. A street food vendor, Jhandu in North 24 Parganas told news agency ANI, "Yes, the price has come down by ₹209...We are facing a little difficulty, it is good that the price has come down but it should be further reduced."
A shop owner in Uttar Pradesh's Ayodhya also praised the price drop and said it would make a difference. “It would be better if it became a bit cheaper. Similarly, a tea seller in Delhi also said that the price reduction would help, adding that rates should further drop.
Concerns over LPG prices
LPG prices saw a big jump after the US-Iran war began, triggering disruptions in passage through the Strait of Hormuz, an important waterway for vessels carrying oil to different countries. As the government moved to prioritise domestic LPG, restaurants and hotels saw a commercial LPG crunch in March this year and took up measures like limiting menu options to limit LPG usage.
In June, the government restored commercial LPG supplies to pre-crisis levels, withdrawing temporary restrictions imposed during supply disruptions linked to the recent Middle East crisis.
The government has maintained that petroleum product prices in India are linked to corresponding international market prices.

How did Abhijeet Dipke's father fund US education? RTI activist seeks probe
RTI activist Amit Tiwari questioned the status of the Cockroach Janta Party and whether it could receive funds while operating under the name of a political party.
A Surat-based Right to Information (RTI) activist has sought a probe into the finances of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's father, questioning how the retired Maharashtra government employee funded his son's education abroad.
The activist, Amit Tiwari, has also written to the Election Commission of India and tax authorities seeking scrutiny of the Rs 1 crore legal defence fund announced by senior advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal for CJP protesters facing police cases.
Tiwari sought an examination of the financial status of Dipke's father, Bhagwanrao Dipke, citing his status as a retired government employee and his son's higher education abroad.
Separately, Tiwari questioned the status of the CJP and whether it could receive funds while operating under the name of a political party.
"The Cockroach Janta Party is an unregistered entity but is operating as a political party. If Rs 1 crore has been pledged to it as a legal defence fund, then the EC should verify whether the CJP is registered with it under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951," Tiwari said.
"If not registered, then its operation under the name of a political party and collection/receipt of funds may require examination," he added.
Tiwari also approached the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, asking it to examine whether GST would apply to Sibal's proposed contribution to the legal defence fund.
Sibal had on Monday announced a Rs 1 crore contribution to a fund set up by the CJP to provide legal assistance to protesters arrested by Delhi Police during the agitation over the NEET paper leak controversy.

headline: A joint operation by the Army’s Intelligence units and the Rajasthan Police has uncovered a counterfeit military combat uniform racket in Rajasthan’s Sriganganagar district, leading to the seizure of nearly 1,000 metres of unauthorised Army-pattern c...
full_text:
A joint operation by the Army’s Intelligence units and the Rajasthan Police has uncovered a counterfeit military combat uniform racket in Rajasthan’s Sriganganagar district, leading to the seizure of nearly 1,000 metres of unauthorised Army-pattern combat cloth.
According to the Army, the operation was launched after a consignment of counterfeit combat cloth was seized in Bareilly in June this year. Investigators traced the material to a manufacturing source in Sriganganagar, prompting the Army’s Intelligence units to carry out a discreet probe.
The investigation identified a local firm as a key link in the supply chain, allegedly distributing counterfeit Army-pattern combat cloth to shops in Sriganganagar town as well as Lalgarh Jattan, Suratgarh, and other nearby markets.
Based on the Army’s interim investigation report shared with the Rajasthan Police in mid-July, a coordinated operation was carried out on July 30. Joint teams searched multiple shops across the district and seized around 1,000 metres of unauthorised new-pattern combat cloth.
Security risk
Officials said the unauthorised possession, sale or use of military-pattern combat cloth is a punishable offence and poses a significant security risk by potentially facilitating the impersonation of armed forces personnel.
The investigation is continuing to identify the manufacturers, suppliers, and distribution network behind the counterfeit military-pattern fabric.

'On Aug 4, at 12 pm': Kejriwal plans march to PM's residence with '100 who don't fear jail' over E20 concerns
The scheduled march marks the latest in a series of attacks by the AAP targeted towards the Centre's fuel-blending policy.
Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal has announced a march to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence in New Delhi on August 4 at 12 pm to submit a petition demanding three key changes in Centre's E20 fuel policy. According to Kejriwal, the petition has been digitally signed by more than two lakh people.
The announcement marks the latest move by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) to escalate its campaign against the Centre's mandatory ethanol-blending policy. The party has been amplifying concerns raised by several vehicle owners, who allege that E20 petrol is damaging engines and reducing fuel efficiency.
A 100-member march to the PM's residence
While addressing a townhall programme outside the Constitution Club in New Delhi on Saturday, Kejriwal revealed his bid to launch a march to the prime minister's residence in order to demand a more fair fuel policy.
“Earlier, I asked you to sign a petition addressed to the Prime Minister. More than 2,00,000 people have signed it online, and I have taken printouts of those signatures. On Tuesday, the 4th, at 12:00 PM, I will personally go to the Prime Minister's residence to hand over the petition,” he said in his address.

“There is no need for everyone to come along. I will take 100 people with me who are not afraid of police batons,” he said. “I will take 100 people with me who are not afraid of going to jail. Those who wish to join should write to me, tag me and send me a message. We will take 100 people with us, march toward the Prime Minister's residence, and then see what happens.”
What are Kejriwal's 3 demands?
During the run of the programme, Kejriwal put forth three key demands in front of the central government in relation to its current fuel policy: an option to pick between E20 and pure patrol at pumps, to make E20 cheaper than pure petrol, and to fix the price of petrol below the ₹84/litre mark.

This development is the latest in a series of attacks launched by the AAP towards the Centre for its fuel-blending policy. Kejriwal pointed out repeated inconsistencies in the statements given by Union ministers in response to concerns surrounding vehicle damage due to ethanol use.
"On one side they say E20 is good, on the other side they say E20 is bad. One ministry says there is a difference of 2 per cent to 5 per cent, while another ministry says 4 per cent. They haven't conducted any study; they are just forcing the policy onto the people... Vehicles are getting damaged and mileage is dropping. Why is the Government forcing this on people? What is the interest of Govt in this? E20 petrol is not good," Kejriwal told reporters, as per ANI.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, however, refuted “misleading claims” regarding E-20, insisting that there is "no verified evidence of widespread engine damage" linked to the fuel following years of scientific vetting and real-world usage across crores of vehicles.
The Centre further claimed that E-15 plus petrol had been in use for over three and a half years while E19-E20 fuel has been in circulation for more than two and a half years and over 20 crore two-wheelers and more than 3 crore petrol cars have operated on these fuel blends successfully without verified systemic failures.

headline: The Executive Officer of (EO) of Dalmianagar Municipal Council in Bihar was beaten to death on Saturday night (August 1, 2026). While the police have arrested the EO’s driver, his wife has alleged the hand of a Lok Janshakti Party (Ram-Vilas) MLA in ...
full_text:
The Executive Officer of (EO) of Dalmianagar Municipal Council in Bihar was beaten to death on Saturday night (August 1, 2026). While the police have arrested the EO’s driver, his wife has alleged the hand of a Lok Janshakti Party (Ram-Vilas) MLA in the murder.
The incident took place under Barun Police Station in Aurangabad district, whereas Dalmianagar falls under Rohtas district. Vimal Kumar, the EO, was on his way to Patna from Dehri-on-Sone in Rohtas district when he was attacked in a deserted area.
After the attack, Vimal was rushed to Narayan Medical College and Hospital in Jamuhar, Rohtas district, where he died during treatment.
The police arrested his driver Mithilesh Kumar in the case. According to police sources, the driver has admitted to his involvement in the murder during interrogation. On Sunday (August 2, 2026), Magadh Range Inspector-General (I-G) Vikas Vaibhav inspected the crime scene and confirmed the arrest of the driver. He added that the driver repeatedly changed his statement during questioning, which deepened the police’s suspicion.
Later, Aurangabad Police issued a press statement stating, “Police have arrested one accused individual (the driver) involved in the incident.”
Based on a complaint filed by Vimal’s family, a first information report (FIR) was registered under relevant sections at Barun Police Station (Case No. 312/26, dated August 2, 2026).
“Acting on the information provided by the arrested driver, a team of divers recovered the iron lever pipe used in the crime from the Patna-Barun-Baura canal located near the crime scene. The arrested accused is being sent to judicial custody. The investigation into the case is ongoing,” the Aurangabad Police said in the statement.
Rohtas District Magistrate Deepak Kumar Mishra said that though the incident had taken place in Aurangabad, the investigation was being conducted in coordination with Rohtas Police.
Wife’s allegation
Vimal’s family members and relatives gathered at his apartment in Gola Road in Danapur, Patna. He is survived by his wife, Babita Kumari, and their two minor children — Vaibhavi, 7, and Vivan, 5.
Vimal’s wife has accused Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Sonu Singh, Lok Janshakti Party (Ram-Vilas) MLA of Dehri-on-Sone, of having a hand in the murder. Ms. Kumari said that the MLA used to call her husband every day and demand ₹25 lakh to ₹50 lakh.
“Dehri MLA used to repeatedly call and demand ₹25 lakh to ₹50 lakh. He used to ask my husband to visit his home; last time he had called my husband on July 29, 2026 as well. My husband used to say that he had not done anything wrong, so from where would he get that much money? Whenever the MLA spoke, my husband would simply say, “Yes, sir; yes, sir.” He kept pressuring him to pay ₹50 lakh, and now he has been murdered,” Mr. Kumari said.
Leader of Opposition in the State Assembly Tejashwi Yadav spoke to Vimal’s wife over the phone and assured her that the Opposition would raise its voice against the incident. He slammed Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, alleging that law and order had collapsed in the State.
