headline: Marriage not essential for domestic cruelty protection: SC on live-in relationships
full_text:
Marriage not essential for domestic cruelty protection: SC on live-in relationships
The Supreme Court has said women in long-term live-in relationships akin to marriage can invoke Section 498A. The ruling broadens protection against domestic cruelty but limits the interpretation to this provision alone.
In a significant ruling reflecting changing social realities, the Supreme Court has held that the protection against cruelty under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) will also be available to women in long-term live-in relationships that are "in the nature of marriage", even if the couple was not legally married. The top court, however, clarified that the expanded interpretation is confined to proceedings under Section 498A alone and will not automatically extend to other provisions of criminal or civil law.
The bench observed that Section 498A was enacted as a beneficial and protective provision to shield women from cruelty in a domestic setting, and its objective should not be defeated by insisting on the existence of a formal marriage. "When the objective of Section 498A was to provide protection against harassment by the husband or in-laws through wilful conduct causing mental or physical injury, then to say that such harassment can only occur after marriage would be an oversimplification," the court said.
It stressed that the law must evolve with society, noting that long-term live-in relationships have become an accepted reality, particularly in urban India. "Whether or not the woman is married does not have a proximate link to the objective of the provision, which is to prevent cruelty within a household," the court observed.
LIVE-IN RELATIONSHIPS CAN QUALIFY FOR PROTECTION
The Supreme Court held that Section 498A would apply to live-in relationships that qualify as "relationships in the nature of marriage", where the intent to marry forms an intrinsic part of the relationship.
The protection, the court clarified, is available only to relationships between two consenting adults and not to casual or purely romantic relationships lacking the characteristics of a marriage-like domestic arrangement.
At the same time, the court made it clear that the burden of proving that the relationship was "in the nature of marriage" and not merely a love affair or casual live-in arrangement would lie on the woman seeking protection under Section 498A.
'CRUELTY DOES NOT CHECK AT THE DOOR'
Emphasising the purpose behind the law, the Supreme Court remarked that cruelty does not distinguish between married and unmarried women living in a shared household. "If a woman is in a domestic setup even prior to marriage, which is increasingly a reality today, the protection given to a married woman should also be extended to her," the court said.
In one of the judgment's key observations, the bench stated: "Cruelty, any which way, does not check at the door whether the house it enters is that of a married woman or not. Once it enters, its propensity to destroy is aggravated."
RULING LIMITED TO SECTION 498A
The court clarified that its interpretation is restricted to Section 498A IPC and should not be treated as a precedent for extending similar meaning to other statutory provisions.
The judgment marks a notable expansion of legal protection against domestic cruelty, recognising that household relationships have evolved over the decades since Section 498A was enacted, while balancing that recognition by requiring proof that the live-in relationship was genuinely akin to marriage before the provision can be invoked.

headline: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar expands cabinet; 20 ministers inducted

Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar expands cabinet; 20 ministers inducted
Alongside the cabinet expansion, the Congress also announced appointments to senior legislative offices
The Karnataka cabinet expansion took place on Monday with the Congress inducting 20 legislators into the cabinet and filling key constitutional posts in the state legislature after months of internal consultations within the party.

Alongside the cabinet expansion, the Congress announced appointments to senior legislative offices.
GS Patil will serve as speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly, with AS Ponnanna as deputy speaker. Salem Ahmed has been named Chairperson of the Legislative Council, while Umashree will serve as deputy chairperson.
The appointments follow several months of discussions between the Karnataka leadership and the Congress leadership over the composition of the ministry. The exercise sought to accommodate competing political interests while distributing representation across regions and communities within the ruling party.
The expanded cabinet is likely to take oath on Monday evening.

headline: Glaw Lake becomes Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar site, India's 101st
full_text:
Glaw Lake becomes Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar site, India's 101st
Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance under the Ramsar Convention, an environmental treaty established in 1971.
The Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh, tucked in the wilderness of Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary, was designated as the state’s first Ramsar site and the 101st in India, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced on Monday.
Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance under the Ramsar Convention, an environmental treaty established in 1971 to conserve biodiversity, particularly waterfowl habitats.
In a post on X, Yadav said the “pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas is a biodiversity hotspot”. “Powered by 101. India continues Her journey beyond a century in designating Ramsar Sites. Delighted to announce Glaw Lake as Arunachal Pradesh’s first Ramsar Site — a significant milestone for biodiversity, water and climate security, and sustainable livelihoods,” he said.
“Fed by perennial mountain streams, it is surrounded by lush vegetation, with more than 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment,” he added.
The Union Minister also said India has emerged as a global leader in wetland conservation under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership. “From 26 Ramsar Sites in 2014 to 101 today, this remarkable journey reflects our unwavering commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development,” he said.
“Every new Ramsar Site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,” he added.
Ramsar sites are selected based on their international significance in terms of ecology, botany, zoology, limnology or hydrology. Applicant countries designate sites that meet at least one of nine criteria, such as supporting vulnerable species, maintaining biodiversity.
Such sites are also significant as they can serve as model examples of a nation’s commitment to conservation and management under internationally accepted frameworks. In designating a wetland as a Ramsar site, countries agree to establish and oversee a management framework aimed at conserving the wetland.

headline: 22 children die of Chandipura virus in Gujarat, 7 under treatment
full_text:
22 children die of Chandipura virus in Gujarat, 7 under treatment
Gujarat Health Minister Praful Panseriya said all confirmed patients are below the age of 15 and clarified that the infections are not concentrated in any one village or district.
The Chandipura virus has claimed the lives of 22 children in Gujarat this monsoon season, with 35 infections confirmed out of 184 suspected cases reported so far, state Health Minister Praful Panseriya said on Monday.
Test results of 11 samples are still awaited.
Seven children who tested positive are currently undergoing treatment at civil hospitals across the state, while six patients have recovered and been discharged. Children admitted to hospitals in Gandhinagar, Sabarkantha-Himmatnagar, Patan, Rajkot and Bhavnagar are receiving specialised treatment under the supervision of expert doctors, he said.
The minister said all confirmed patients are below the age of 15 and clarified that the infections are not concentrated in any one village or district. Cases have been reported from different parts of Gujarat, prompting health authorities to remain on high alert.
To curb the spread of the virus, health department teams have intensified surveillance and launched large-scale insecticide spraying, particularly in livestock-rearing areas where sandflies — the primary carriers of the virus — are commonly found. Residents have also been advised to seal cracks in mud houses and walls, which can serve as breeding spots for the insects.
The government has directed all government and private paediatric hospitals to immediately admit children showing symptoms such as high fever, vomiting, seizures or altered consciousness to intensive care units equipped with oxygen and ventilator support. Early treatment is crucial to prevent severe complications, including multiple organ failure, officials said.
There is currently no specific vaccine or antiviral treatment for the Chandipura virus.
Gujarat Health Minister Praful Panseriya urged people not to panic or pay attention to rumours and appealed to parents to seek immediate medical attention if children develop symptoms. He also asked citizens to cooperate with health teams conducting surveillance and preventive measures.
Chandipura encephalitis is a rare viral disease that primarily spreads through sandflies and causes inflammation of the brain. The virus was first identified in Chandipura village in Maharashtra's Nagpur district in 1965. It mainly affects children and can progress rapidly if not treated in time.

22 children dead in Gujarat's Chandipura virus outbreak; 35 infections confirmed

As many as 22 children have died due to Chandipura virus (CHPV) in Gujarat this monsoon season, with 35 cases testing positive out of 184 suspected infections, state health minister Praful Panseriya said on Monday.
Seven patients remain under treatment across civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Rajkot, and other districts, and government and private paediatric facilities have been instructed to immediately admit symptomatic patients to ICU beds to prevent organ failure, he said.
"A total of 184 suspected cases have been registered in the state so far, out of which 35 cases have tested positive and the results of 11 samples are still pending," Panseriya said.
Out of the cases reported so far, 22 children have died due to Chandipura virus, he said. All patients are under 15 years of age, he added.
Children under treatment, cases spread across districts
Children who are admitted to civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Sabarkantha-Himmatnagar, Patan, Rajkot and Bhavnagar are being provided the best and super-specialist treatment and doctors are monitoring their condition, Panseriya said.
He further noted that cases are being reported from different areas and not concentrated in a particular village.
State steps up surveillance, treatment
Health teams are spraying pesticides in areas where animal husbandry is practised to target sandflies, which are responsible for spreading the encephalitis virus, he said.
Government and private paediatric facilities have been instructed to admit patients with symptoms of the virus to ICU beds with oxygen and ventilator facilities and not delay treatment so that serious conditions like multiple organ failure can be prevented, he said.
What is Chandipura virus?
Chandipura encephalitis is a viral disease that spreads mainly by sandflies and other insects and causes inflammation of the brain. The virus was first isolated from a patient from Chandipura village in Nagpur district of Maharashtra in 1965.

headline: BJP MP files privilege notice against Pappu Yadav over 'sadhu' attire in Parliament
full_text:
BJP MP files privilege notice against Pappu Yadav over 'sadhu' attire in Parliament
The notice alleges that the Independent MP's enactment in Hindu Sadhu attire at Makar Dwar hurt religious sentiments and undermined the dignity of Parliament.
BJP Lok Sabha MP Sanjay Jaiswal has given a Notice of Breach of Privilege and Contempt of the House to the Lok Sabha Speaker against Lok Sabha MP Pappu Yadav for allegedly wearing Hindu Sadhu attire at Makar Dwar, within the Parliament complex on July 31, to ridicule religious sentiments and lower the dignity of the house.
In his privilege notice submitted to the Lok Sabha Speaker in terms of Rule 222 read with Rule 223 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha. "I request that the matter be admitted and, if you deem fit, referred to the Committee of Privileges under Rule 227 for detailed examination," stated Sanjay Jaiswal.
BJP Lok Sabha MP Jaiswal has mentioned grounds of the Motion and said, "Conduct unbecoming of a Member and lowering the dignity of the House. On 31st July, 2026, Pappu Yadav, MP, staged a scripted enactment at Makar Dwar, within the Parliament Complex, wearing attire associated with a Hindu Sadhu and carrying a photograph/idol of Lord Ram, portraying a temple priest collecting offerings from "devotees" and pocketing the money instead of depositing it in the donation box, while other Members and slogans accompanied the act. The said conduct has been widely perceived as a deliberate and theatrical act intended to ridicule, mock or trivialise Hindu religious symbols and sentiments, undertaken in connection with allegations concerning donation irregularities at Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, Ayodhya," said Jaiswal.
Also read: Slipper thrown at MP Pappu Yadav over Parliament Ram temple skit, two detained
Sanjay Jaiswal further added in Notice that Parliament House is not a venue for theatrical or symbolic provocation of this nature, and such conduct is not mere political expression but tends to lower the dignity, seriousness and moral authority of the House and of its Members collectively.
According to the complaint, the gravity of the hurt caused is further borne out by the fact that seers and members of the public in Varanasi and Delhi have since lodged police complaints against Pappu Yadav alleging that the enactment hurt the religious sentiments of the Hindu community, and that religious bodies have called for protests across the country in protest against the said conduct.
Jaiswal added that the rules themselves recognise that the dignity and discipline of the House are not confined to the floor of the Chamber but extend to the wider precincts of Parliament House.
This is reinforced by rule 232, which prohibits arrest within the precincts of the House, and by the corresponding prohibition on service of legal process within the precincts, both of which treat the precincts as continuous with the House for the purpose of extending its protections.
"Theatrics of the kind described above, though committed at Makar Dwar and not within the Chamber, therefore fall squarely within the mischief that the Rules of Procedure seek to guard against, and cannot be permitted to escape scrutiny merely on account of location within the larger precincts of Parliament House," he added.
Jaiswal further added that violation of the standard of conduct expected of a Member under Rule 349. Rule 349 requires every Member to maintain conduct befitting the dignity of the House. In particular, Rule 349(xiv) bars a Member from wearing or displaying badges of any kind in the House, and Rule 349(xvi) bars a Member from displaying flags, emblems or exhibits in the House.
" I submit this Notice not in a partisan spirit, but to preserve the sanctity of Parliament, uphold constitutional values, and protect the dignity of the House from conduct that may diminish its stature in the eyes of the nation. I remain available to furnish any further particulars, including video and photographic record of the conduct complained of, as may be required by the Chair or the Committee," he added.

headline: 'Not giving up': Vinesh Phogat says wrestlers to appeal against Brij Bhushan's acquittal in sexual harassment case
full_text:
'Not giving up': Vinesh Phogat says wrestlers to appeal against Brij Bhushan's acquittal in sexual harassment case
Vinesh Phogat's remarks came after Brij Bhushan was acquitted in the sexual harassment case lodged by six women wrestlers against him and secretary Vinod Tomar.
Wrestler Vinesh Phogat said that she was “deeply saddened” by the acquittal of Brij Bhushan Singh, former chief of the Wrestling Federation of India, by court in in sexual harassment case filed by female wrestlers and added that they will appeal against the decision “as soon as possible”.
Phogat said that they had to muster up a lot of courage to protest on the streets demanding an FIR against Brij Bhushan but he used “power and muscle” to scare girls and take back their names from the complaint.
Her remarks came after Brij Bhushan was acquitted in the sexual harassment case lodged by six women wrestlers against him and secretary Vinod Tomar on Monday. The decision came two years after the trial began.
The case against Bhushan was filed after a prolonged protest by wrestlers at Jantar Mantar in January 2023. They had accused Singh of sexual harassing several female wrestlers over the years and demanding him to be arrested and removed from the federation.
Looking back the protest, Phogat said that many wrestlers kept fighting against Bhushan even when the entire system was engaged in “saving” him.
“But many women wrestlers stood up and kept fighting against Brij Bhushan in the court. We are deeply saddened that the court has found Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh not guilty of the allegations of sexual violence made by female wrestlers,” Phogat said.
Also read: Delhi court clears Brij Bhushan Singh in sexual harassment case by six women wrestlers
“From the very beginning, the entire system, government and this system is engaged in saving Brij Bhushan. The women wrestlers have instructed their lawyers to appeal against this decision, and this will be done as soon as possible. We have not given up hope and the wrestlers will continue their fight,” she added.
‘Moment of happiness’ for Brij Bhushan
The former WFI chief, reacting to his acquittal, said that it was a “moment of happiness” for him.
"From the very first day, I had said that if even a single allegation against me was proved, I would be ready to face the harshest punishment,” he said.
“Today, the court has acquitted us with honour and it is a matter of happiness for me. What I had said on the first day has turned out to be true. I did not know what the other side was thinking, but my first reaction was that the truth would prevail. Today is a moment of happiness," he added.

headline: New Delhi: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor dealt a major blow to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) as he defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by almost 19,000 votes in his electoral debut in the Bankipur assembly bypolls.
full_text:
New Delhi: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor dealt a major blow to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) as he defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by almost 19,000 votes in his electoral debut in the Bankipur assembly bypolls.
According to data released by the Election Commission, Kishor bagged 63,203 votes, followed by Sinha, who managed 44,250 votes in the high-stakes battle. RJD’s Rekha Gupta is in the distant third.
JSP party workers celebrated across Patna. Kishor thanked the Bankipur voters and said victories and defeats keep happening. “I am grateful to the people…I sincerely thank everyone who placed their trust and faith in Jan Suraaj and me. I also want to thank those who voted for our political opponents and assure them that after the election, those who voted for us and those who did not are equally ours,” he told the media.
The Bankipur seat fell vacant after BJP national president Nitin Nabin resigned as MLA following his election to the Rajya Sabha in April. Polling was held 30 July.
The seat had witnessed drama as barely 24 hours after nominating Abhishek Bunty from Bankipur, the BJP had replaced him with Neeraj Kumar Sinha for the bypoll.
Kishor had also accused Patna Senior Superintendent of Police Kartikey Kumar Sharma of misusing police powers to intimidate voters and unlawfully detaining local workers. The JSP leader while addressing a press conference said that homes of several persons were also raided. Kishor claimed that his party had taken up the matter with the ECI.
For the BJP, Bankipur is a prestige fight. The seat, considered high-profile, is a BJP stronghold. It was earlier known as the Patna West assembly constituency. Nabin’s father Kishore Prasad Sinha won it multiple times from 1995 until his demise in 2006.
More than 25 percent of voters in the constituency are Kayasthas, a community that Nabin belongs to. The constituency also has a sizable upper-caste mix of Bhumihars.
Nabin entered electoral politics after his father’s demise, first winning the seat in a 2006 by-election. In the assembly polls last year, he had won for a fifth consecutive term, defeating the RJD candidate by a margin of nearly 50,000 votes.
In the last year’s Bihar election, Nabin had won the seat for a fifth consecutive term, defeating the RJD candidate by a margin of nearly 50,000. The BJP set a target of increasing the winning margin, with its party president holding several meetings and campaigning extensively in the constituency.
Kishor launched the Jan Suraaj Party on 2 October 2024 after a two-year pan-Bihar march, the Jan Suraaj Padyatra. This was after exiting a career in political consulting in 2021.
A JSP functionary explained how professionals managed the entire campaign and key workers of the party were given charge of four booths each and after submitting the reports for each of them. A review meeting used to take place every night with Kishor, he said.
“Booth committees were also made for this purpose and it was ensure that a section of these members were local representatives from the area. Everything was meticulously planned and we are hoping to win the seat.”
In the last year’s Bihar elections, Kishor fielded candidates in 238 of the 243 seats, but he himself did not contest. The party drew a blank, getting just 3.4 percent vote share.
(Edited by Tony Rai)

headline: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor scripted a major political upset in Bihar by defeating the Bharatiya Janata Party candidate in the Bankipur Assembly byelection, a constituency represented for five consecutive terms by the BJP’s nationa...
full_text:
Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor scripted a major political upset in Bihar by defeating the Bharatiya Janata Party candidate in the Bankipur Assembly byelection, a constituency represented for five consecutive terms by the BJP’s national president Nitin Nabin. The BJP retained Manjalpur in Gujarat while the Congress held on to Madhya Pradesh’s Datia in other Assembly byelections.
Mr. Kishor dedicated the victory to the people of Bankipur and appealed to the BJP’s central leadership to change the Chief Minister of Bihar. The Bankipur Assembly seat had fallen vacant after Mr. Nabin vacated the seat upon his election to the Rajya Sabha and elevation as BJP chief.
The political strategist-turned-politician clinched victory over BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by a margin of 19,324 votes. He bagged 64,151 votes while Mr. Sinha finished with 44,827 votes. Rashtriya Janata Dal nominee Rekha Kumari secured the third position with 14,273 votes. A total of 25 candidates contested the election, with 646 voters choosing the NOTA option.
In the 2025 Assembly election, Mr. Nabin had defeated Ms. Kumari by a margin of 51,936 votes. He had secured 98,299 votes while Ms. Kumari polled 46,363 votes. The JSP’s Vandana Kumari had received 7,717 votes.
Prashant Kishor: From election backrooms to Bihar Assembly
Throughout the 32 rounds of counting on Monday, Mr. Kishor, contesting an election for the first time, remained ahead in every round and held on to his lead until the final tally. Celebrations broke out at the JSP office in Patliputra Colony after the 10th round, when Mr. Kishor had established a lead of over 6,000 votes.
A JSP worker, celebrating the victory while dancing to Bhojpuri songs, said: “Bankipur is just a trailer; the whole of Bihar is still to come.”
After the 22nd round of counting, when Mr. Kishor was leading by a margin of around 13,000 votes, he and his wife Jahanvi Das walked to the counting centre at A.N. College to join the party workers and supporters in celebrations.
“The people have not only elected an MLA, but the people of Bankipur have given a message to the central leadership of the BJP to replace Samrat Choudhary with a better person. I expect that the BJP leadership will seriously think about it,” Mr. Kishor said.
He added that the time had come for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to not only care about the people of Gujarat but also pay attention to the people of Bihar.
“My only concern is that the young people of Bihar need to go to other States in search of jobs. Migration from Bihar should be stopped,” he said.
Read updates from the vote counting for Manjalpur Assembly bypoll in Gujarat
The Bihar Chief Minister congratulated Mr. Kishor on his victory on his X handle. “In the grand festival of democracy, the people have chosen Jan Suraaj in the Bankipur Assembly by-election. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to Prashant Kishor ji on his victory, while respecting the people’s decision,” said Mr. Choudhary.
In his statement, Bihar BJP State president Sanjay Saraogi said, “The Bharatiya Janata Party humbly accepts the mandate of the Bankipur by-election and respects the decision of the people. In a democratic process, the verdict of the people is above everything! We will seriously analyse why we did not secure the votes; we will identify our shortcomings and work diligently to rectify them.”
He added, “Unlike Opposition parties, we do not blame constitutional institutions, EVMs, or the Election Commission for our defeat. The Bharatiya Janata Party has complete faith in democracy and constitutional systems, and believes in addressing its shortcomings through introspection and review.”
BJP wins in Manjalpur
In Gujarat, the BJP retained the Manjalpur Assembly seat in Vadodara district, with its candidate Satish Govindbhai Patel defeating Congress nominee and former Minister Bhikhabhai Rabari by 30,630 votes. According to the Election Commission, Mr. Patel secured 55,481 votes against Mr. Rabari’s 24,851 after 20 rounds of counting at Bhavan’s School in Makarpura. The byelection, necessitated by the death of senior BJP MLA and former Minister Yogesh Patel, recorded a voter turnout of 37.5%.
With the victory, the BJP’s strength in the 182-member Gujarat Assembly has increased to 162 seats, while the Congress has 12 MLAs.
The Congress defended Madhya Pradesh’s Datia Assembly constituency, with its candidate Ghanshyam Singh winning against BJP’s Ashutosh Tiwari by 6,016 votes. Mr. Singh, a member of Datia’s erstwhile royal family, polled 66,757 votes against Mr. Tiwari’s 60,741. Mr. Tiwari was picked to contest the bypoll over former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra. Aazad Samaj Party candidate Damodar Yadav ‘Mandal’ finished third with 22,527 votes.

headline: BJP chief Nitin Nabin reacts as Prashant Kishor wrests his family seat: ‘Unexpected’

BJP chief Nitin Nabin reacts as Prashant Kishor wrests his family seat: ‘Unexpected’
BJP national president Nitin Nabin thanked voters in Gujarat for helping the party retain the Manjalpur Assembly seat and congratulated workers on the victory.
BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Monday accepted the verdict in the three Assembly bypolls and said the party would conduct a detailed review after losing the Bankipur seat in Bihar and Datia in Madhya Pradesh.
On X, Nabin thanked voters in Gujarat for helping the BJP retain the Manjalpur Assembly seat and congratulated party workers on the victory.
"We accept the mandate received in today's three assembly by-elections," he said. Thanking the people of Manjalpur, Nabin congratulated its workers and office-bearers for the win.

Referring to the defeats in Bankipur and Datia, Nabin admitted that the BJP had fallen short of expectations.
"In Bankipur and Datia, we did not receive the expected mandate. We will conduct a thorough introspection of the election results in both these areas with complete seriousness," he said.
He added that the BJP would return to the people "with renewed energy and determination" and continue working to further strengthen their trust.
ALSO READ | From Jan Suraaj's zero to Bankipur victory: What changed for Prashant Kishor in Bihar within months
Why Bankipur mattered for Nitin Nabin
The Bankipur bypoll carried high political stakes for the BJP because it was held in the party's traditional stronghold and a seat closely associated with Nitin Nabin.
The constituency has remained with the BJP since 1995. Nitin Nabin himself represented Bankipur for four consecutive terms and built it into one of the party's safest urban seats in Bihar.
The bypoll became necessary after he resigned as an MLA following his elevation as the BJP's national president.
The BJP fielded Neeraj Kumar to retain the seat, but Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor defeated him by 19,324 votes, handing the BJP one of its most significant electoral setbacks in Bihar in recent years.
Bankipur had long been considered a BJP bastion. In the 2025 Assembly election, the BJP won the seat by a margin of more than 50,000 votes.

‘We humbly accept’
After the results, Nabin told reporters that the Congress merely retained a seat it already held in Datia and pointed out that the BJP had increased its vote tally there by around 1,700 compared to the previous Assembly election.
“The public's trust in us in a democracy is evident - after the last Assembly election, winning all 29 out of 29 Lok Sabha seats was accomplished by the Bharatiya Janata Party for the first time since independence,” he said.
He also spoke of the party's recent electoral record, saying that the BJP won all 29 Lok Sabha seats in Madhya Pradesh, retained its Budhni Assembly seat in a bypoll and even wrested the Amarwara seat from the Congress.
"We presented our view, Congress presented their view, and whatever verdict the public gave, we humbly accept it," Nabin said and added that the BJP would return to the people with greater strength in the upcoming elections.

headline: WhatsApp puts multiple accounts in India under review, blocks app access for 24 hours
full_text:
WhatsApp puts multiple accounts in India under review, blocks app access for 24 hours
Affected users said they were unable to use the Meta-owned messaging app despite receiving no prior warning.
Multiple WhatsApp users, including several in India, reported on Monday evening that their accounts had been placed "under review" for up to 24 hours. The app temporarily blocked access to all features of the instant messaging platform, PTI reported.
The issue occured around 8 pm, Indian time. Affected users said they were unable to use the Meta-owned messaging app and hadn't received any prior warning.
What users saw
Users whose accounts were affected were shown the following message on the app: "Account in review. Date requested: 3 Aug 2026. Your account activity and device info is being checked to make sure it follows our terms of service. We will notify you of the result typically within 24 hours."
The review notice also included links to information on "How to use WhatsApp responsibly" and "About stolen phone and accounts."
During the review period, users reported being unable to access WhatsApp's messaging and calling features.

A user wrote on X, "WhatsApp has placed several accounts under investigation for 24 hours. WhatsApp suddenly put several users' accounts under investigation on Monday evening. As a result, they were unable to use the app's features for 24 hours. This step has left people frustrated in India and several other places, and they also lodged their complaints on social media."
Another user on X wrote, “WhatsApp has banned my account for absolutely no reason. Has anyone else experienced this? Any idea what the next steps are?”
WhatsApp's response
A WhatsApp spokesperson acknowledged that the company's automated systems could occasionally make mistakes while enforcing its policies.

"We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting," the spokesperson told PTI.
WhatsApp did not specify how many accounts were affected or whether the issue was linked to a technical glitch or an automated enforcement action. The company said it worked to correct cases where legitimate accounts are mistakenly flagged and restore access as quickly as possible.

headline: 2 losses, 1 win: BJP election scorecard days after Gen Z delivered a setback to Modi govt

2 losses, 1 win: BJP election scorecard days after Gen Z delivered a setback to Modi govt
The biggest setback for the BJP came from Bihar, where Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes in Bankipur.
The BJP had a mixed day, at best, in the assembly bypolls on Monday. The saffron party won only one of the three seats that went to polls, all of them in states it rules.
It lost the high-profile Bankipur seat in Bihar and failed to wrest Datia in Madhya Pradesh, though the BJP held on to Manjalpur in PM Narendra Modi's home state of Gujarat.
The results came days after the Centre was put under pressure -- and the education minister had to be replaced -- over protests that saw massive participation of youth in Delhi against repeated examination paper leaks. Track election results live here
Bankipur loss hands Prashant Kishor first win
The biggest setback for the BJP came from Bihar, where Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes in Bankipur.
The BJP had held the seat since 1995.
The bypoll was held after BJP national president Nitin Nabin resigned from the assembly upon moving to the Rajya Sabha.
This was Kishor's first election victory since entering politics and gave Jan Suraaj its first MLA. The party had failed to open its account in the 2025 Bihar elections.

During the campaign last week, Kishor said Jan Suraaj already changed Bihar's political debate despite not being in power.
RJD's vote share also dropped sharply. Its candidate, who had polled more than 46,000 votes in the last assembly election, got fewer than 15,000 votes this time.
BJP loses Datia
The BJP also lost the Datia assembly bypoll in Madhya Pradesh, with Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh defeating BJP's Ashutosh Tiwari by 6,016 votes.
The Congress retained the seat, which it had won in the 2023 elections.
BJP holds Manjalpur
The BJP's only win came from Gujarat, where it comfortably retained the Manjalpur Assembly seat.
BJP's Satendrabhai Patel defeated Congress candidate Bhikhabhai Rabari by a margin of over 30,000 votes.

Opposition steps up attack
The Opposition was quick to target the BJP after the results.
Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav linked the defeats to public anger over paper leaks, unemployment, inflation and corruption. Calling the verdict the “beginning of change”, he said it showed the “unity of the youth and the outrage of their guardians”.
He added that "even the BJP's safest and most traditional seats won't be able to save them from defeat now" and described the outcome as the “double defeat of the double-engine government”.
“Bhagwan ko nachane ka ahankaar rakhne walon ko Bhagwan ne hi nacha diya. (Those who believed they could make God dance have instead been humbled by God Himself),” the SP chief said.
AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal also took a swipe at the BJP over the bypoll results.
READ ALSO | 'BJP just lost its president's seat': Kejriwal on Prashant Kishor's big debut win in Bihar's Bankipur
Congratulating Prashant Kishor on his debut win, Kejriwal said, “The BJP has lost even the seat of its national president.”
He claimed the BJP's “ground has completely shifted” and blamed the result on issues such as “fund theft, paper leaks, E20” and growing public dissatisfaction with the Narendra Modi government.
"The arrogance is breaking down. The people of the country have given a signal of change," he added.
Results come after Jantar Mantar protests
The bypoll results came days after the Centre took a beating from non-stop GenZ-driven protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar over exam paper leaks and education reforms.
The agitation, led by the satirical digital front Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), began over the NEET paper leaks before ballooning into a mass movement on education, jobs and governance.
ALSO READ | 'Withdraw FIRs now': CJP to BJP after top court clarifies order on protest-linked cases
After over a month of protests and hunger strikes, the Centre opened talks with CJP leaders. Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan was forced to resign on June 25, and the government announced a series of measures, including examination reforms, discussions on preventing future paper leaks and compensation for families of students who died by suicide following exam paper leaks.
The CJP later ended its protest, saying the government accepted its key demands.
Kishor on CJP's impact
Last week, Kishor said the popularity of the CJP was an example of public frustration with the BJP growing day by day.
“The so-called party is being talked about because within no time of it hitting the Internet, nearly two crore people have signed up,” he told reporters.
“It must be understood that there is public distress which has led to so many people associating themselves with the party. Problems like unemployment, corruption, price rise and non-availability of gas and fertilisers have created a situation in which so many people are endorsing this campaign.”
Asked if the campaign could influence future elections, he said, “That remains to be seen. But the response to the campaign should have the government concerned. It is indicative of a trust in the system giving way to anxiety.”

headline: RSS chief Bhagwat to address Gen Z at Mumbai event, Aaditya Thackeray takes a ‘suddenly’ dig

RSS chief Bhagwat to address Gen Z at Mumbai event, Aaditya Thackeray takes a ‘suddenly’ dig
The interaction will take place in Mumbai during an event commemorating the 15th anniversary of India's International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN).
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat is scheduled to interact with Gen Z students from over 100 cities across the country on Thursday (August 6), days after the student protests at Jantar Mantar. The youth-led demonstrations forced the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as the Union education minister.
The interaction between the youth and RSS chief Bhagwat, 75, will take place in Mumbai during an event commemorating the 15th anniversary of India's International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN), according to a press release.
Over 2,000 high school students are expected to be present during the inaugural ceremony of IIMUN's Annual Championship Conference, which will be held at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC). Gen Z and Gen Alpha are demographic groups, segregated according to their birth years — those born from 1997 to 2012 come under the Gen Z umbrella, those from 2013 to 2025 are considered to be Gen Alpha. Gen Z made up a major part of the recent student protests.
Also Read | Nandan Nilekani to lead exam reforms: Amid Gen-Z ire, Modi taps all-season technocrat
Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray took a jibe at recent Gen Z interactions, questioning the legal action on the student protesters. He further asked why leaders had not “stepped in” during police action and complaints against them in the aftermath.
“Suddenly everyone who wants to interact with Gen Z and Gen Alpha, and some who have taken it on themselves to preach “culture” to them via social media, the simple question to all of them is…Where were you when they were facing AK-47s, lathis with rusted nails, electric shock guns and electric barricades, tear gas and when women were manhandled in the name of “law and order?”” Thackeray asked.
He added, “Where were you when they were detained at home while leaving for peaceful protests, or when they were arrested? Why didn’t you step in then?”
Mohan Bhagwat to address participants between 15-19 years of age
According to the press release, the participants at the event are between 15 and 19 years of age. Bhagwat's address will mark the beginning of flagship Annual Championship Conference under IIMUN, one of the largest youth-led congregations. The inaugural ceremony will be centred around the theme "The Role of Youth in Uniting the World, the Indian Way."
Student participants, representing their schools and colleges, will debate and deliberate on local, national and international issues during the conference.
Rishabh Shah, the founder of IIMUN, thanked Bhagwat for accepting the invite, saying this dialogue was needed “more than ever before.”
“Leadership is not only about guiding the next generation, but also listening to it. At this critical juncture in India's journey, we need this dialogue more than ever before. I am grateful to Mohan Bhagwat ji for accepting our invite to address this gathering at this critical juncture,” the release cited Shah as saying.

The IIMUN, founded by Rishabh Shah in 2011, organises 108 conferences and thousands of civic engagements and community interventions ever year, according to the press release. These are largely led entirely by youths aged 15-24 for students aged 11-19.

headline: Parliament panel summons Meta, X, Google, Snapchat over digital safety, meeting at 4pm today
full_text:
Parliament panel summons Meta, X, Google, Snapchat over digital safety, meeting at 4pm today
The panel will examine measures to protect women, children and citizens' data privacy, besides reviewing how social media platforms comply with government rules
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology summoned representatives of major social media platforms Meta, X, Snapchat, and Google to appear before the panel today at 4 PM.
The meeting of Parliament's Committee on Information Technology and communications was scheduled to convene to evaluate the broader framework of online safety. The discussions primarily focused on three core areas: ensuring the digital safety of women and children, safeguarding the data privacy of farmers, rural residents, laborers, and general citizens, and assessing how social media platforms comply with government rules governing law and order.
Also read: Govt summons Meta’s global head after PM Modi's Facebook reel removed
Announcing the summons earlier, BJP MP and chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee Nishikant Dubey outlined the specific areas of inquiry for the digital platforms.
"On 3 August 2026 at 4 PM, our Parliamentary Committee on IT and Communication has summoned Meta (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp), X (Twitter), Snapchat, and Google," Dubey stated.
"How will the privacy of women, children, farmers, rural folks, laborers, and the general public be protected? How do these companies ensure the government's public order?" he added.
The development follows an incident involving Meta, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook video addressing action against examination paper leaks was briefly removed from the platform before being restored.
In a statement, a Meta spokesperson said, "The content was removed in error and has since been restored," attributing the removal to a technical error.
Also read: ‘Removed in error’: Meta on blocking PM Modi's video on Facebook
The video, released on July 23, marked Prime Minister Modi's first direct address to Gen Z during the 36-day-long Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led agitation over the NEET-UG 2026 examination irregularities.
In the address, the Prime Minister assured students that the government would strengthen the legal framework against paper leaks, including setting up Special Fast-Track Courts and introducing stricter punishment through fresh legislation. The Centre subsequently introduced the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, proposing imprisonment of up to 10 years, enhanced monetary penalties and Special Fast-Track Courts for offences under the Act.
The student agitation was called off on July 25 after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. The Centre also reached an understanding with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and activist Sonam Wangchuk to withdraw cases against protesters, prevent police intimidation and bring stronger anti-paper leak legislation.

headline: Politics often comes wrapped in familiar assumptions. With the BJP, the ruling party at the Centre, now also in power in a majority of states, either alone or in alliance, one might expect a degree of sameness in the profiles of Indiaâs chief ministe...
full_text:
Politics often comes wrapped in familiar assumptions. With the BJP, the ruling party at the Centre, now also in power in a majority of states, either alone or in alliance, one might expect a degree of sameness in the profiles of Indiaâs chief ministers. Yet the Association for Democratic Reforms reports show a more varied picture. The countryâs CMs come from different social strata, age groups, educational backgrounds and economic profiles, even within their own parties. There is no single formula for political ascent.That is what makes the comparison between ADRâs 2025 and 2026 reports more revealing than either report viewed alone. The 2025 study examined 30 chief ministers, since Manipur was then under Presidentâs Rule. The 2026 report covers 31, after the return of a chief minister in the state. More importantly, the occupants of the chief ministerâs office changed in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar and West Bengal.
South pulls the wealth map
The combined assets declared by Indiaâs chief ministers rose from Rs 1,632 crore in the 2025 report to Rs 3,660 crore in 2026. Average assets more than doubled from Rs 54.42 crore to Rs 118.07 crore. The number of billionaire chief ministers rose from two to four.
In 2025, N Chandrababu Naidu, with assets of Rs 931.84 crore, and Pema Khandu, with Rs 332.57 crore, were the only billionaire chief ministers. Siddaramaiah was a distant third with Rs 51.94 crore. A year later, Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar is the clear number one with Rs 1,413.8 crore, while cine star and Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay declared assets of Rs 648.86 crore. Together, these four account for approximately Rs 3,327 crore, or 90.9% of the assets declared by all 31 chief ministers. The remaining 27 account for only around Rs 333 crore between them.
Analysing the assets held by CMs
A geographical cut makes the imbalance sharper. Using a broad four-zone grouping, not an ADR classification, the South has only six of the 31 CMs but accounts for roughly Rs 3,059 crore, or about 83.6% of all declared CM assets in 2026. That is because three of the four billionaire CMs, Shivakumar, Naidu and Vijay, are from southern states. So the South, in a way, lives up to the larger-than-life CM personalities. Naidu is a veteran politician who has survived many ebbs to rise again and regain his lost glory. D K Shivakumar finally got rewarded after a power tussle with Siddaramaiah, and Vijay was the new kid on the block who broke through the DMK-AIADMK binary, while also ticking the box of another cine star to become CM of Tamil Nadu. So the profiles of these billionaire CMs could not be more different.East and the Northeast together have the largest number of CMs in this grouping, 12, but account for about Rs 495 crore, helped substantially by Khanduâs declaration. North and Central India together have 10 CMs but only around Rs 75 crore in declared assets, while the West has three CMs and around Rs 31 crore.
Same party, different worlds
The party-wise picture is just as uneven. The BJP has 17 chief ministers in the 2026 list, but they are far from a single economic bloc. Its richest CM is Pema Khandu, with Rs 332.57 crore in declared assets. Its poorest is West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, with about Rs 85.88 lakh. That is a nearly 387-fold gap within the same party.The Congress spread is smaller in headcount but sharper in scale. Of its four CMs, Shivakumar alone accounts for Rs 1,413.8 crore. At the other end is Kerala CM V D Satheesan, with Rs 6.66 crore. Revanth Reddy, at Rs 30.05 crore, and Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhvinder Singh, at Rs 7.82 crore, sit far below Shivakumarâs level. In effect, Congressâs CM asset profile is overwhelmingly shaped by one leader.This is why the average can mislead. A calculation based on individual entries puts the 2026 median at only around Rs 8.23 crore, barely higher than the 2025 median of about Rs 8.02 crore.Total declared liabilities rose from roughly Rs 242 crore in 2025 to nearly Rs 505 crore in 2026, though the number of CMs declaring liabilities of Rs 1 crore or more remained unchanged at 11. Khandu led the 2025 liability table with Rs 180.28 crore. In 2026, Shivakumar moved to the top with Rs 265.07 crore, followed by Khandu and Himanta Biswa Sarma.
Younger leaders, uneven party trend
The leadership profile also became younger. In 2025, 12 of the 30 chief ministers were in the 51-60 group. By 2026, that number had risen to 17. The number aged 61 or above fell from 10 to six. The 41-50 category remained unchanged at eight.
India now has younger CMs
The average reported age declined from 58.8 to 56.7, though the median remained 56. The shift reflects the exit of several older CMs, including Siddaramaiah, Pinarayi Vijayan, Nitish Kumar, M K Stalin and Mamata Banerjee. The ages are those recorded when election affidavits were filed, not necessarily current ages. So the actual decline is much sharper because the 2025 calculation accounted for many outgoing CMsâ 2021 affidavits.Here again, parties differ internally. Congressâs four CMs are tightly bunched. Revanth Reddy is 56, Sukhvinder Singh 58, Shivakumar 60 and Satheesan 61. The BJPâs spread is wider. It has Pema Khandu at 44 and Manik Saha at 70, with several CMs clustered in their 50s. In other words, the Congress CM cohort is smaller and more middle-aged, while the BJPâs larger pool stretches from younger leadership to older veterans.There was a reversal on gender. The 2025 report listed two women among 30 chief ministers. The 2026 report lists only one among 31. Mamata Banerjeeâs exit from the CM roster left Delhiâs Rekha Gupta as the sole woman in the group.
Degrees stay broadly stable
Many of the politicians are products of student politics. They may not have worked professionally, but they still believed in the inherent importance of formal education. In 2025, 25 of the 30 CMs were graduates, professional graduates, postgraduates or doctorate holders. In 2026, the number remained 25, despite the larger group. The proportion with graduate-level qualification or higher slipped slightly, from about 83% to 81%.Within parties, the BJP shows the widest educational spread. Its CM list includes doctorate holders such as Mohan Yadav, Himanta Biswa Sarma and Samrat Choudhary, but also leaders listed as Class 10 pass, diploma holders, graduates, professional graduates and postgraduates. Congressâs four CMs are more compact educationally: Shivakumar and Sukhvinder Singh are postgraduates, Revanth Reddy is a graduate and Satheesan is a graduate professional.
Cases rise, but cluster in five names
The criminal-record figures worsened modestly. In 2025, 12 of 30 chief ministers, or 40%, had declared criminal cases; 10 had cases classified by ADR as serious. By 2026, 14 of 31, or 45%, had declared criminal cases; 11 had serious cases.The combined number of declared cases rose from 187 to 195. The burden remained concentrated. Revanth Reddy continued to head the list with 89 cases, followed by Suvendu Adhikari with 29, Shivakumar and Naidu with 19 each, and Keralaâs V D Satheesan with 18. Five chief ministers accounted for 174 of the 195 cases, or 89.2%.
Criminal cases against CMs
Three of Congressâs four CMs are among the top five by declared cases: Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar and Satheesan. Among BJP CMs, Adhikari carries the highest declared case load, while several BJP chief ministers have no declared criminal cases. Geography shows a similar concentration, though for different reasons. The six southern CMs together account for 147 declared cases, driven mainly by Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar, Naidu and Satheesan. East and the Northeast account for 38 cases, led by Adhikari. North and Central India account for six, while the West accounts for four. It is perhaps not a coincidence that many of the CMs with high case loads were opposition leaders for a significant time.
Thus, criminal cases need to be treated with caution. A low case count may not strictly be a virtue; it may just be a case of friendly police administration. Disclosures arenât the only way to understand the nature of a politician. But they are an important starting point, particularly when compared over the years, to understand how the seat of power remains the same, but the nature of those who occupy it changes, perhaps as an inevitable reflection of the realities of the times.

headline: CJP eyes next chapter after NEET agitation, announces nationwide listening tour
full_text:
CJP eyes next chapter after NEET agitation, announces nationwide listening tour
The Cockroach Janta Party will also hold a two-day strategy meeting in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Wednesday and Thursday to finalise its future roadmap. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, spokespersons and organisational leaders will be in attendance.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Monday unveiled plans for a nationwide listening tour to connect with young people across India as it looks to build on the momentum of its agitation against the NEET paper leak.
In a statement posted on X, the outfit announced a two-day strategy meeting in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Wednesday and Thursday to finalise its future roadmap. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, spokespersons and organisational leaders will be in attendance.
According to the party, the discussions come after days of consultations with a broad cross-section of stakeholders, including around 50 volunteers who played a key role in the Jantar Mantar agitation.
As part of the nationwide listening tour, the CJP said it would reach out to volunteers across the country to understand the aspirations and concerns of young people before deciding its next course of action.
It said the outreach programme is aimed at engaging with a generation that has become "hopeful and optimistic" following what it described as the success of its campaign, which led to the resignation of former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, ending the two-month agitation.
"The defeat of this arrogant government at the hands of the youth shows that when young people come together, they can achieve anything," CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said.
"Our team is working to put together the best possible path forward to channel the expectations of our youth into meaningful action," he added.
The party said it would announce further details, including the schedule and format of the nationwide listening tour, in the coming days.
The outreach is expected to shape CJP's organisational and political strategy as it seeks to build on the momentum generated by the anti-NEET movement.

headline: Continued political activities by deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from Indian territory “could harm” bilateral relations, the Government of Bangladesh conveyed to India on Monday (August 3, 2026) through Humayun Kobir, the Foreign Aff...
full_text:
Continued political activities by deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from Indian territory “could harm” bilateral relations, the Government of Bangladesh conveyed to India on Monday (August 3, 2026) through Humayun Kobir, the Foreign Affairs Adviser to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Mr. Kobir met with Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi in Dhaka after Ms. Hasina’s August 5 ‘homecoming’ media event was announced here by the Foreign Correspondents Club.
“Adviser Kobir mentioned that such activities could harm the positive progress of bilateral relations between the two countries. The Indian High Commissioner assured that the matter would be duly considered, necessary inquiries would be made and efforts would be made in this regard,” the official news agency of Bangladesh UNB reported.
The meeting took place in the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon, Dhaka, UNB said.
The report added that Dhaka expects India to ensure that no one, including Ms. Hasina, used “Indian territory to make political statements or conduct any activities aimed at creating instability within Bangladesh”.
The Indian High Commission, in a statement, said that the discussion between Mr. Trivedi and Mr. Kobir focused on “mutual interests” and “mutual benefits”.
“High Commissioner reiterated India’s intent to work positively with the Government of Bangladesh to advance the developmental aspirations of the peoples of India and Bangladesh,” said the Indian High Commission in a message.
Ms. Hasina, who has been based here since fleeing Dhaka on August 5, 2024, has given multiple telephonic and emailed interviews over the past three months expressing her desire to return to Bangladesh by the end of the year.
Earlier, on Sunday, the Foreign Correspondents Club announced that the media event featuring an audio message from Ms. Hasina would be held on August 5 and that the event titled ‘Sheikh Hasina’s Homecoming’ would also feature her son Sajeeb Wazed Joy and several top functionaries of the Awami League.
Waeil Awwad, the club’s president, told The Hindu on Monday (August 3, 2026) that the event remains on track.

Meta apologises before Parliament panel over removal of PM Modi's Facebook video
NEW DELHI: Parliamentary standing committee on communications and information technology chairman Nishikant Dubey on Monday said Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg should personally apologise over the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook video, warning that the social media giant could lose its safe harbour protection if it failed to do so.Dubey's remarks came after Meta apologised before the parliamentary panel, saying the PM Modi's video was removed due to an error. However, members of the committee said the issue went beyond an apology and demanded accountability for the incident.Addressing reporters after chairing the committee meeting, Dubey said, "...Understand the situation that has arisen within the algorithm. What Meta India did, what X did, and what YouTube did is a matter that the country should know. If you look at the viewership algorithm of the BJP, Congress, Samajwadi Party, and Aam Aadmi Party, the viewership is only 23 million. And those who are neither registered parties nor registered NGOs, their algorithm is 27 million. All political parties together are at 23-24 million. An anti-reservation forum has just been formed five or six days ago, and it reached 7 million. The reason for that is that they have a policy of giving preference to newcomers."
On the removal of the Prime Minister's video, he said, "The second question is that Meta India removed the Prime Minister's content. This is not the first time Meta India has done this. If you recall, Zuckerberg himself made a statement in January regarding the 2024 elections and later apologized. This shows that his intention is to destabilise the country. When a video of the Prime Minister of India can be removed, and they themselves admitted that the content was missing for five hours, from 12:30 am to 5:00 am, this is a very serious matter. Our committee has said two things and has clearly stated that the apology should come from Zuckerberg. If Zuckerberg does not give it, then the safe harbour protection under Section 79 should be withdrawn from him."Dubey also raised concerns over the handling of child sexual abuse material and other objectionable content on social media platforms.He said, "CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material) is another issue. YouTube also has that content. Meta also has that content, and they do not remove content related to child abuse. They do not remove content related to women. Both these rules of the Government of India are very strict, and on top of that, they do not listen to the Home Ministry. They do not listen to the IT Ministry either. So, we have said that in all these matters, and in many other matters, you know that the Chief Minister of the Congress government of Telangana has filed an FIR against Meta India. We have said that safe harbour should be removed in all these matters..."Earlier in the day, Meta apologised before the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology, saying the removal of PM Modi's Facebook video was the result of an error. According to ANI sources, several committee members questioned Meta officials and said the issue was not about an apology but about fixing accountability. Members also sought details on the company's action against controversial and objectionable content on its platforms.ANI sources said, "The Parliamentary Standing Committee on IT took a tough stance over the removal of PM Modiâs video from Facebook. During the committee meeting, several members posed tough questions to Meta officials. Meta officials apologized, stating that the PMâs video was removed due to an error. Several committee members said the issue was not about an apology, but about fixing accountability. Committee members also demanded legal action against the Meta official responsible for removing the video. Members further sought details from Meta on what action the company has taken regarding controversial and objectionable content present on its platforms. Meeting is still underway."The meeting, attended by representatives of Meta, Google, YouTube, X and Snapchat, along with officials from the Union home ministry and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), was convened to discuss the regulation of social and digital media platforms.
The controversy stems from the temporary restriction of Prime Minister Modi's Facebook post in which he addressed India's youth and promised stringent action against paper leaks. While Meta restored the content and attributed the removal to a technical error, the MeitY termed the explanation "inadequate", saying the issue also concerned national security and public order.
Separately, Hyderabad Cyber Crime Police has registered cases against Meta India head Arun Srinivas and certain Facebook and Instagram accounts over allegedly morphed and AI-generated posts targeting the Prime Minister.

headline: Zuckerberg apology sought over PM Modi video takedown, Meta faces panel heat
full_text:
Zuckerberg apology sought over PM Modi video takedown, Meta faces panel heat
A parliamentary panel has sought answers from Meta over why a PM Modi video disappeared from Facebook for hours. The episode has now raised questions over accountability, safe harbour and platform moderation.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg should personally apologise for the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video from Facebook, Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology chairman Nishikant Dubey said on Monday after a meeting with representatives of the social media giant.
Speaking after the more than three-hour meeting, Dubey said Meta had acknowledged that Modi's video remained unavailable on the platform for about five hours, from 12.30 am to 5 am.
"They themselves admitted that the video was taken down for five hours. This is a very serious matter and an apology must come from Zuckerberg's side," Dubey said, according to PTI.
He also warned that if Zuckerberg did not apologise, the government should consider withdrawing Meta's safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act.
The provision protects intermediaries from liability for third-party content under certain conditions.
WHY WAS PM MODI'S VIDEO REMOVED?
The meeting was convened after a Facebook post by Modi on action against paper leaks was briefly removed from the platform.
Meta had earlier attributed the incident to a technical glitch, apologised and restored the post. However, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology described the explanation as "inadequate".
Sources said the parliamentary panel has asked Meta to submit a written response within 10 days.
During the meeting, several BJP MPs questioned Meta representatives over who authorised the removal of the Prime Minister's video and sought clarity on who was responsible.
Members also raised concerns over alleged algorithmic bias, arguing that objectionable material remained available on the platform while "genuine" content was removed.
META OFFICIALS EXPRESS REGRET
According to sources, Meta representatives expressed regret over the incident and indicated that they were willing to apologise before the committee.
BJP members, however, argued that the matter went beyond an apology and called for accountability to be fixed, with legal action to be considered if warranted.
Opposition MPs on the committee took a different position, arguing that social media platforms must preserve space for dissent in a democracy.
They also cautioned against treating criticism of the government as anti-national content.
GOOGLE, X, YOUTUBE ALSO APPEAR
The meeting was part of the parliamentary panel's broader examination of the regulation of social and digital platforms.
Apart from Meta representatives, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, MeitY Secretary S Krishnan and officials from Google, X, YouTube and Snapchat also appeared before the committee.
The episode has put fresh focus on how major social media platforms moderate political content and the extent of accountability they should face when posts by public figures are removed, even temporarily.

headline: ‘Zuckerberg intends to destabilise India’: Parliament panel chief demands apology from Meta boss over PM post row
full_text:
‘Zuckerberg intends to destabilise India’: Parliament panel chief demands apology from Meta boss over PM post row
Highlighting the removal of PM Modi's content, Nishikant Dubey said this was “not the first time” Meta had done this.
BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on Monday questioned Meta chief executive officer (CEO) Mark Zuckerberg's “intention”, days after the brief removal of one of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's videos on Facebook. Dubey, who is also the chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications & IT, further demanded an apology from Zuckerberg himself after a meeting of the panel.
Highlighting the removal of PM Modi's content, Dubey said this was “not the first time” Meta had done this. “If you recall, Zuckerberg himself made a statement in January regarding the 2024 elections and later apologised. This shows that his intention is to destabilise the country,” Dubey said, according to a video by news agency ANI.
After chairing a meeting with representatives from Meta, Snapchat, Google, X and YouTube, Dubey told reporters that the removal of PM Modi's video for over five hours was a “serious matter”. While Meta during the meeting reportedly said it was ready to apologise, according to a report by PTI news agency, Dubey stated that the apology must come from the CEO himself.
“Our committee has said two things and has clearly stated that the apology should come from Zuckerberg. If Zuckerberg does not give it, then the safe harbour protection under Section 79 should be withdrawn from him,” the BJP MP from Godda said.
As for “not the first time”, Dubey was referring to a statement made by Zuckerberg in January 2025, wherein he claimed that after Covid people lost trust in information given by the governments because of which incumbent governments that went to polls in 2024 had lost. The Meta CEO also included India while listing out such countries — BJP lost majority on its own but its alliance remained in power in the 2024 polls — following which the tech giant had to issue an apology.
Dubey slams Meta's algorithm, raises concern over child sexual abuse material
Dubey also slammed Meta's algorithm, alleging the viewership of registered parties was around 23 million, while that of non-registered parties or NGOs was 27 million, ANI reported.
“What Meta India did, what X did, and what YouTube did is a matter that the country should know. If you look at the viewership algorithm of the BJP, Congress, Samajwadi Party, and Aam Aadmi Party, the viewership is only 23 million. And those who are neither registered parties nor registered NGOs, their algorithm is 27 million. All political parties together are at 23-24 million,” he said.
He further said that an anti-reservation forum, formed five to six days ago, already had a viewership of 7 million. “The reason for that is that they have a policy of giving preference to newcomers,” Dubey said.
Dubey said child sexual abuse material (CSAM) was another issue with the the platform. “YouTube also has that content. Meta also has that content, and they do not remove content related to child abuse,” Dubey alleged, adding that content “related to women” is not removed.
He pointed out compliance-related challenges with the home ministry and the IT ministry. “So, we have said that in all these matters, and in many other matters, you know that the Chief Minister of the Congress government of Telangana has filed an FIR against Meta India. We have said that safe harbour should be removed in all these matters...” he added.

headline: Congress retains Madhya Pradesh's Datia seat; BJP loses bypoll after candidate switch
full_text:
Congress retains Madhya Pradesh's Datia seat; BJP loses bypoll after candidate switch
At the end of all 15 rounds of counting, Singh secured 66,757 votes, while Tiwari polled 60,741 votes.
The Congress on Monday retained the Datia assembly seat in Madhya Pradesh, with the party candidate Ghanshyam Singh defeating his nearest rival Ashutosh Tiwari of the BJP by 6,016 votes in the byelection marked by differences in the saffron camp over the choice of candidate.
At the end of all 15 rounds of counting, Singh secured 66,757 votes, while Tiwari polled 60,741 votes. Azad Samaj Party candidate Damodar Yadav secured third position by bagging 22,527 votes, District Election Officer and Datia District Magistrate Swapnil Wankhade told PTI.
A total of 21 candidates were in the fray, including Ghanshyam Singh and Ashutosh Tiwari.
At one point, Singh's lead of 12,607 votes over his nearest rival appeared unassailable, but the BJP nominee managed to close the gap to an extent in the last rounds.
The byelection was necessitated after a Delhi court in April this year sentenced sitting Congress MLA Rajendra Bharti to three years' imprisonment in a cheating case, leading to the termination of his Assembly membership.
"This verdict marks the beginning of the end of the BJP," Ghanshyam Singh told reporters.
In Bhopal, celebrations broke out at the state Congress headquarters with party workers distributing sweets.
A total of 21 candidates contested the by-election, which saw a healthy 71.44 per cent voter turnout, though the main fight was between Congress' Singh and Tiwari of the ruling BJP.
Then-Congress nominee Bharti had defeated BJP candidate and former state Home Minister Narottam Mishra in Datia by over 7,700 votes in the 2023 Assembly elections.
For the by-election, the BJP denied a ticket to Mishra and instead fielded Tiwari.
Ghanshyam Singh expressed confidence that the Congress will form the next government in Madhya Pradesh in 2028, adding that the party was working to see Rahul Gandhi become the next Prime Minister.
He said his priority would be to promote communal harmony in Datia and end political vendetta.
"I will work to end gambling and betting rackets in the constituency," he said.
State Congress President Jitu Patwari described it as a victory for the people of Datia, a clarion call for the 2028 assembly elections, and the result of the collective efforts of Congress leaders.
Patwari told reporters in Bhopal that Datia voters have exposed the corruption, terror, and arrogance of the BJP-led government.
He said the people of Datia have laid the foundation for change and the BJP's departure.

full_text:

Around a dozen Kanwariyas collected holy Ganga water from Har Ki Pauri before beginning their journey with the massive Tricolour-themed Kanwar.
Devotees carrying a 251-foot-long Tricolour Kanwar from Haridwar to Baghpat drew widespread attention, showcasing their patriotic spirit during the Kanwar Yatra.
Around a dozen Kanwariyas collected holy Ganga water from Har Ki Pauri before beginning their journey with the massive Tricolour-themed Kanwar. The unique Kanwar became a major attraction, with the devotees also urging the country's youth to stay away from drugs.

The devotees appealed to people across the country to remain united and not be misled by divisive influences. They also urged young people to stay away from substance abuse and requested Kanwariyas visiting Haridwar to maintain peace and discipline while undertaking the pilgrimage.

headline: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat to interact with 2,000 teenagers in Mumbai on August 6 amid growing youth assertiveness
full_text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat to interact with 2,000 teenagers in Mumbai on August 6 amid growing youth assertiveness
NEW DELHI: Days after saying that the era of unquestioned obedience was over and young people now sought reasons and logic, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat will interact with nearly 2,000 teenagers in Mumbai on August 6, bringing him face to face with the generation he has urged elders to engage through dialogue rather than commands.The students, aged between 15 and 19, will come from schools and colleges across more than 100 cities. The interaction will be held at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre as part of the 15th anniversary programme of Indiaâs International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN), a youth-led organisation.
The event comes against the backdrop of growing youth assertion in the country, with students increasingly using social media and street protests to demand answers from governments and institutions. The recent agitation over irregularities in NEET-UG and other examinations has also brought questions of transparency, accountability and the role of young people in public debate to the centre stage.Bhagwat did not refer to any particular agitation while speaking recently about changing relations between generations. He had said that, unlike in the past, children today expect reasons, examples and explanations and must be engaged through regular conversation.
The Mumbai interaction will, therefore, be watched for the issues raised by students and whether the session allows them to directly question the RSS chief on education, leadership, nation-building and social change.IIMUN founder Rishabh Shah said the gathering was aimed at creating a dialogue between senior leaders and young people.
âLeadership is not only about guiding the next generation, but also listening to it. At this critical juncture in Indiaâs journey, we need this dialogue more than ever before,â Shah said.Bhagwatâs address will mark the opening of the organisationâs annual championship conference, where students will debate national and international issues. This yearâs theme is âThe Role of Youth in Uniting the World, the Indian Wayâ.

Renowned for his incisive coverage of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, accreditation reforms, and skilling initiatives, he has also reported on student politics, urban policy, and social movements. headline: NEW DELHI: Indiaâs one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the countryâs 101st such site and the stateâs first to join the elite club for additional care and conserva...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Indiaâs one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the countryâs 101st such site and the stateâs first to join the elite club for additional care and conservation.Located within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary, Glaw Lake is a pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas and a biodiversity hotspot. The lake is fed by perennial mountain streams and is surrounded by lush vegetation, supporting rich floral diversity.âEvery new Ramsar site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,â said Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav while announcing the development on X on Monday.The Glaw Lake wetland has over 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment, underscoring its ecological significance and surrounding landscape.âFrom 26 Ramsar sites in 2014 to 101 today, this remarkable journey reflects our unwavering commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development,â said Yadav.
Globally, there are nearly 2,600 such designated wetlands under the Ramsar Convention.
India has the highest number of such wetlands in Asia and third highest in the world after the UK (176) and Mexico (144).Wetlands are land areas covered by water, either temporarily/ seasonally or permanently. These are critical ecosystems that play a significant role in supporting biodiversity, and providing various ecosystem services such as flood control, water supply, food, fibre and raw materials.

He has been covering Parliament since 2003 to see how politics shaped up domestic policy and Indiaâs position at global platform. Before switching over to explore sustainable development issues, Vishwa had covered internal security and investigative agencies for more than a decade.

headline: The flood situation in Assam improved on Sunday (August 2, 2026) with around 1.35 lakh people now affected in five districts even though three more persons died, taking the toll in this year's deluge to 85, according to an official bulletin.
full_text:
The flood situation in Assam improved on Sunday (August 2, 2026) with around 1.35 lakh people now affected in five districts even though three more persons died, taking the toll in this year's deluge to 85, according to an official bulletin.
All three deaths were reported from Sivasagar district.
The Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) reported that more than 1,36,200 people have been affected by floods in the Charaideo, Dhemaji, Golaghat, Jorhat, and Sivasagar districts. On Saturday (August 1), almost 1.8 lakh people were affected across five districts.
Sivasagar is the worst-hit district with over 55,000 people affected, followed by 40,000 people in Charaideo and 22,000 in Jorhat. According to ASDMA, 335 villages are inundated, while 15,422 hectares of farmland have been damaged.
The administration has been operating 54 relief camps and relief distribution centres in five districts, taking care of 13,771 people at present.
At present, the Dhansiri river is flowing above the danger level at Numaligarh.
