headline: Phuket-Delhi Air India pilot tests positive for marijuana in 2nd dope test: Sources
full_text:
Phuket-Delhi Air India pilot tests positive for marijuana in 2nd dope test: Sources
Both pilots had undergone mandatory psychoactive substance screening after the August 4 incident. While the co-pilot's screening did not raise a similar concern, the initial test of the Pilot-in-Command returned a result requiring further analysis.
The Pilot-in-Command of Air India flight AI2379 has tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory laboratory test, sources said on Tuesday, days after the Phuket-Delhi flight suddenly lost around 300 feet in altitude and left 24 passengers and crew members injured.
Both pilots underwent mandatory psychoactive substance screening following the August 4 incident. The Pilot-in-Command’s initial test required further confirmation, following which his sample was sent to a designated laboratory. The confirmatory test has now returned positive for marijuana, sources said.
Both pilots have already been taken off the flying roster pending the investigation.
The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), however, has cautioned against drawing conclusions from any isolated piece of information while its investigation is underway, saying all technical, operational, medical and human-factor evidence will be examined in its entirety.
AI2379 LOST 300 FEET DURING CRUISE
The Airbus A320, registered as VT-EXO, was flying from Phuket to Delhi on August 4 when it experienced a sudden altitude variation of around 300 feet during cruise.
The aircraft was carrying 137 passengers, including three infants, and eight crew members — two pilots and six cabin crew.
According to the latest government statement, 20 passengers and four cabin crew members were injured during the incident. The aircraft subsequently stabilised and landed safely in Delhi.
The AAIB has taken up the investigation in accordance with applicable provisions and International Civil Aviation Organization protocols, with the requisite notifications sent to ICAO and the concerned states.
The probe will examine the aircraft and its systems, recorded flight data, operational and maintenance records, medical information and interviews with those concerned.
TECHNICAL GLITCHES UNDER PROBE
Investigators are also examining reports that the aircraft suffered multiple technical anomalies during the flight.
Sources had earlier said the A320 experienced an autopilot disconnect, triple hydraulic failures and other technical and mechanical glitches.
The co-pilot reportedly took manual control after the autopilot disconnected. Soon afterwards, a flight-control stall message appeared and several indicator switches briefly went off.
The AAIB will examine whether the reported technical failures, turbulence and sudden altitude loss were connected and establish the sequence of events.
France’s aviation accident investigation agency BEA, along with technical representatives from Airbus, is assisting the AAIB by providing technical information and design documentation under the ICAO investigation framework.
The AAIB said the sole objective of the investigation was to determine the circumstances and contributing factors behind the incident and identify safety measures to prevent a recurrence.
AIR INDIA CEO QUESTIONED
The positive confirmatory result comes as the government steps up scrutiny of Air India over the incident.
Outgoing Air India CEO Campbell Wilson was summoned to the Ministry of Civil Aviation headquarters on Tuesday, where officials reviewed the AI2379 incident and broader safety and operational concerns involving the airline.
Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu, the Civil Aviation Secretary and senior DGCA officials attended the discussions, according to sources. Air India has said it is cooperating with investigators.

headline: President Murmu gives assent to Vande Mataram Bill, grants it same legal protection as National Anthem
full_text:
President Murmu gives assent to Vande Mataram Bill, grants it same legal protection as National Anthem
The Parliament had passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amending the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.
President Droupadi Murmu on Tuesday gave assent to the Vande Mataram Bill, granting the National Song the same legal protection as the national anthem.
The Parliament passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, last month, amending the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971. The legislation seeks to give Vande Mataram the same statutory protection as the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.
With the president's assent, the bill has become a law. Now, such offences are punishable with imprisonment up to three years, a fine, or both.
Earlier, the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act prohibited intentionally preventing the singing of the national anthem (Jana Gana Mana) or causing disturbance to any assembly engaged in such singing.
These offences were punishable by up to three years' imprisonment, a fine, or both, while a second and every subsequent conviction attracted a minimum of one year's imprisonment. The erstwhile law did not accord the same protection for the national song.
"Presently, there is no specific legal provision to prevent insults to the singing of 'Vande Mataram', which is honoured as the national song. Therefore, in order to prohibit any person from intentionally preventing the singing of the national song or causing disturbance to any assembly engaged in such singing, it is proposed to amend Section 3 of the said Act to include the national song also within its ambit, so as to make such acts punishable," the Bill had said.
The president of the Constituent Assembly, Dr Rajendra Prasad, on January 24, 1950, stated that the song 'Vande Mataram' composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, which played a historic role in the Indian freedom struggle, shall be honoured equally with the national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' and shall have equal status with it, the Bill further said.
Home ministry's Vande Mataram order
The Union home ministry said on Monday that for the first time at the Independence Day function, Vande Mataram will be sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort this year.
Earlier this year, the Union Home Ministry directed that all six stanzas of 'Vande Mataram' shall be sung first when the national song and the national anthem are played together.
In an order dated January 28, the home ministry gave the first set of protocols for singing the national song, directing that six stanzas of it, having a duration of 3 minutes and 10 seconds, shall be sung at official functions such as the arrival of the president, unfurling of the national flag, and speeches of governors.
"When the national song and the national anthem are sung or played, the national song will be sung or played first," the order read.
The assembly where the national song is sung shall stand in attention, it said.
The order, which carried several directives, said that in all schools, the day's work shall begin with community singing of the national song.

headline: NDA MPs target Rahul Gandhi over silence on use of lathis, water canons on protesting students in Jharkhand
full_text:
NDA MPs target Rahul Gandhi over silence on use of lathis, water canons on protesting students in Jharkhand
BJP MPs are questioning Rahul Gandhi's silence over the alleged use of lathis, water cannons against protesting students.
NDA MPs on Tuesday held a protest in Delhi targeting the Opposition, accusing it of avoiding discussions in Parliament while raising issues outside the House.
The protest focused on the recent student agitation in Jharkhand, with BJP MPs questioning Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's silence over the alleged use of lathis and water cannons against protesting students.
BJP MP Aparajita Sarangi questioned Rahul Gandhi's silence on the Jharkhand protests and asked him to respond.
"When there is a lathi-charge against students in Jharkhand, Rahul Gandhi is silent. What is the reason behind his silence? We urge him to reply," Sarangi said.
BJP MP Anurag Thakur also criticised the Congress leader over the issue and said justice should be delivered to the protesting youth in Jharkhand.
"Justice must be done for the youth of Jharkhand. The way they were subjected to lathi-charges and atrocities reveals the mindset of Rahul Gandhi," Thakur said.
He alleged that the incident reflected the alleged mistreatment of youth in a state governed by parties supporting Gandhi.
Thakur also accused Rahul Gandhi and the Congress of demanding answers from the Union Home Minister while not attending the House.
"The Home Minister is ready to provide answers, but Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party are peddling lies and making reckless statements merely to stay in the headlines," he said.
BJP MP Tarun Chugh also targeted Gandhi, alleging that he was "running away from the House" and remaining silent on the alleged lathi-charge against students in Jharkhand.
"He should come to the House and answer on it," Chugh said.
Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Shinde said the Union Home Minister was ready to discuss the students' protest in Parliament, but alleged that the Opposition was preventing the House from functioning.
"The Home Minister is ready to hold a discussion in Parliament on the students' protest, but the Opposition is not letting the House function," Shinde said.
BJP MP Jagadambika Pal also raised the issue of police action in Jharkhand.
"The way the police have carried out the lathi charge, used water cannons in Jharkhand, but today they are silent on it?" Pal said.
He alleged that there was "chaos" in Parliament and said the Opposition was being exposed before the country through its silence on the Jharkhand student protests.
The remarks came amid an ongoing political dispute over the protests by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Ranchi. The students have been demanding action over alleged irregularities in examinations and the recruitment process, including cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a CBI probe and recruitment reforms.
The Opposition and the government have also been at odds over the functioning of Parliament, with the NDA MPs accusing the Opposition of avoiding discussion while the Opposition has continued to raise issues concerning the government.

headline: Border will define ties: India to China over reports of troop activity in Arunachal
full_text:
Border will define ties: India to China over reports of troop activity in Arunachal
India said border issues with China remain a top concern and peace along the LAC is essential. New Delhi signalled that any broader improvement in ties will depend on stability and restraint.
India on Tuesday said it treats issues related to the border with China as "most serious" and stressed that maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control is of "utmost importance". The Ministry of External Affairs also said the situation on the border will shape the broader course of India-China ties.
The remarks came amid reports of aggressive posturing by Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh's Upper Subansiri region. India also rejected China's criticism of its decision to formally identify 27 places and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names, saying the state is an "inalienable and integral" part of India.
At his bi-weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, "In matters relating to the border areas between India and China, we have always emphasised in discussions with the Chinese side that we consider these issues as most serious and that the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in these areas is of the utmost importance." He added, "We have also stated that the state of the border affairs will reflect on the state of our larger bilateral ties."
Jaiswal was responding to questions on reports of a standoff between the two sides in Upper Subansiri late last month and whether the matter had been taken up diplomatically with China. There was no comment from the Indian Army on the reports.
The spokesperson said India had again flagged the need for peace and tranquillity in the border areas during the latest round of diplomatic talks with China. "This was also reiterated at the recently held 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China border affairs (WMCC) on August 6," he said. Jaiswal said the two sides held frank discussions and reviewed the situation along the LAC. "The Indian side again underlined that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations." He added, "It was agreed to continue to use existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander-level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC."
On Arunachal Pradesh, Jaiswal rejected Beijing's criticism of New Delhi's move to standardise names of 27 places and geographical features in the state. "Arunachal is inalienable and integral part of India and this is a fact which is self-evident. At the same time, let me also underline that nothing can change this indisputable reality," he said.
India and China have rolled out a series of measures over the last year to rebuild ties after relations came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020 and the military face-off that continued for over four years. In October 2024, the two sides finalised a disengagement pact for Depsang and Demchok, the last two friction points in eastern Ladakh. Days later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in Kazan and took a number of decisions to improve ties. In August last year, Modi travelled to Tianjin for the annual SCO summit, where he and Xi held extensive talks. Modi said at the meeting that India is committed to taking forward ties with China based on mutual trust, respect and sensitivity.
India's latest position makes clear that while both sides have taken steps to reset ties, New Delhi continues to link the future of the broader relationship to peace and stability along the LAC.

headline: ‘Will update when there is one’: India on Dhaka’s Hasina extradition request
full_text:
‘Will update when there is one’: India on Dhaka’s Hasina extradition request
Jaiswal’s remarks came a day after Dhaka called for expediting Hasina’s extradition at a meeting between PM Tarique Rahman and Indian envoy Dinesh Trivedi.
India said on Tuesday that Bangladesh’s request for the extradition of former premier Sheikh Hasina, who has lived in the country in self-exile since August 2024, is being examined in line with established processes, though a decision is yet to be made.
External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal outlined New Delhi’s position a day after Dhaka called for expediting Hasina’s extradition during a meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Indian envoy Dinesh Trivedi in the Bangladeshi capital. The matter has emerged as the main irritant in relations between the two neighbouring countries.

Sheikh Hasina’s extradition
Trivedi met Rahman and discussed matters of mutual interest, Jaiswal told a regular media briefing. He noted that India has already outlined its position on Hasina’s extradition, which was first raised by the Bangladeshi side in late 2024.
“We have made it very clear that this issue is being examined in line with established processes on the Indian side. We will give you an update when there is one,” Jaiswal said, speaking in Hindi.
Handing over of two Bangladeshi nationals
Jaiswal responded to another question on Bangladesh seeking the handing over of two Bangladeshi nationals arrested in West Bengal earlier this year on suspicion of involvement in the killing of Bangladeshi political leader Sharif Osman Hadi by saying that investigations by Indian authorities are yet to be completed.
“This is a legal matter, in which investigations are ongoing,” he said.
The Bangladeshi side had also raised this matter during Trivedi’s meeting with Rahman in Dhaka on Monday. Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman described the matter as a “sensitive issue” and said Dhaka had submitted all the documents sought by New Delhi.

The two Bangladeshi nationals were arrested in March for alleged involvement in the killing of radical leader Hadi, who was shot by gunmen in Dhaka last December and subsequently died while being treated in Singapore. The attack triggered violent protests across Bangladesh that assumed anti-India overtones because of unsubstantiated reports of an Indian link to Hadi’s killing.
Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman's bilateral visit to India
Jaiswal referred to two separate invitations extended to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for a bilateral visit to India and to join the outreach session of the Brics Summit in September and said: “We will keep you updated on this particular matter.”

headline: President Droupadi Murmu on Tuesday gave assent to a Bill that criminalises intentional disruption or prevention of the singing of the National Song Vande Mataram, giving it the same legal protection currently accorded to the National Anthem, a gover...
full_text:
President Droupadi Murmu on Tuesday gave assent to a Bill that criminalises intentional disruption or prevention of the singing of the National Song Vande Mataram, giving it the same legal protection currently accorded to the National Anthem, a government statement said.
With the President’s assent, the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, has become a law.
The Lok Sabha had passed the Bill on July 30, while the Rajya Sabha had cleared it a day earlier.
The legislation grants Vande Mataram the same status as the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana.
Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor questioned the practicality of implementing the newly amended law, arguing that mandating its full rendition at official functions could prove counterproductive asking whether respect and patience could be legislated.
Mr. Tharoor noted that while Jana Gana Mana takes about 52 seconds to sing, a full rendition of Vande Mataram lasts around three minutes and 10 seconds. Referring to Tamil Nadu’s decision to precede both with the State Song, he asked whether audiences could realistically be expected to stand respectfully for nearly six minutes before and after every function.
He said he feared that the legislation’s intended objective of promoting greater respect for the National Song might not be achieved and could instead produce the opposite effect.

headline: New Delhi: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi to “forgive himself” for his 2017 remark against former prime minister Manmohan Singh, in which he had said Singh knew “the art of bathing with a ...
full_text:
New Delhi: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi to “forgive himself” for his 2017 remark against former prime minister Manmohan Singh, in which he had said Singh knew “the art of bathing with a raincoat on”.
Referring to the recent Supreme Court ruling upholding the Central Bureau of Investigation’s (CBI) clean chit to the former prime minister in the coal block allocation case, Gandhi has written in an article in The Indian Express that there was a “witch hunt” against Dr Manmohan Singh. “The lobby against him was coordinated and well-organised, with actors stretching from the bureaucracy to the media, the judiciary, civil society, and most certainly to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Today, their bogus crusade has come to its inevitable conclusion of nothingness. Dr Singh has been vindicated on every count,” she wrote.
Gandhi referred to PM Modi’s ‘raincoat’ remark against his predecessor as the lowest point of parliamentary history, and sought an apology, citing his recent Instagram video where he forgave students for using “abusive words” against him.
“It is not a coincidence that the Prime Minister was also among the most vocal proponents of the attack on Dr Singh. His snide and atrocious remarks in the Rajya Sabha on 8 February 2017, that only Dr Singh knew ‘the art of bathing with a raincoat on’, will go down as the lowest point of our parliamentary history. Since Mr Modi is these days ‘forgiving’ India’s students for attacking him, perhaps he can take this opportunity to forgive himself for his undignified slander against Dr Singh,” she wrote.
Gandhi’s comments come after the Supreme Court’s 29 July judgement upholding the CBI’s clean chit to Singh in the alleged coal block allocation scam. The court also pulled up the trial court for rejecting the CBI’s closure reports and making adverse observations against Singh without a “compelling reason”.
Gandhi further wrote the campaign questioning his integrity involved sections of the bureaucracy, media, judiciary and civil society, as well as the RSS and BJP. Gandhi also accused the Modi government of misusing the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and CBI to pressure political opponents.
“Leaders are either silenced through coercion or cynically folded into the BJP or, in some remarkable instances, rewarded with ministerial positions as well. When credible accusations of corruption emerge, the Modi government simply brushes them aside. Corrupt when you’re in the Opposition, suddenly clean when you jump ship!”
She also pointed to the economic growth during Singh’s 10 years as prime minister, along with rising consumption and private investment. Gandhi said the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government recorded higher economic growth than the following 12 years and argued that millions of people were pulled out of poverty during the period.
“Dr Manmohan Singh’s government heralded profound economic change with unprecedented rates of growth and a consumption and private investment boom that propelled us into the ranks of middle-income countries. In 2008, when the global economy faced turbulence and collapse, India demonstrated its resilience. During his tenure, the shift in employment patterns became very discernible with lakhs moving into higher-productivity occupations. Over the last decade, however, this diversification has been reversed. Based significantly on the programmes put in place in the previous government and the acceleration in growth rates, India decisively began winning the battle against poverty and deprivation. Let us not forget that in spite of the re-working of how the growth of India’s GDP is calculated, the 10 years of the UPA government saw higher economic growth than the past 12 years, resulting in millions being pulled out of poverty.”
Gandhi said Singh’s “statesmanship, erudition, and fundamental decency” were “sorely missed in today’s conflicted times”. His record, she said, was increasingly being recognised as a period of “decisive economic, political, and social advancement”.
She also listed the Right to Education Act, Other Backward Caste (OBC) reservations in centrally funded higher education institutions such as the Indian Institutes of Tehchnology and Indian Institutes of Management, the Forest Rights Act, Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) and the National Food Security Act, 2013, among the major measures of the Singh government.
On MGNREGA, Gandhi wrote that it was the “most powerful social security intervention”, pointing to its role during the Covid pandemic in reaching poor and vulnerable sections. She said the National Food Security Act was another major avenue through which the government was able to provide basic food rations to crores of families.
Gandhi also drew a contrast between the democratic environment under Singh and the present government. “Politically, the Dr Manmohan Singh decade as prime minister was characterised by the growth and strengthening of democratic institutions of the state and civil society. Dr Singh heralded a new era of transparency in government through the landmark Right to Information Act (RTI), which enabled citizens to access the government’s inner workings. The RTI now stands totally emasculated. There was an explosion of independent media, which was characterised by a fearlessness that appears more remarkable when juxtaposed with its current enfeeblement.”
“Civil society emerged as a force to be reckoned with, and our students had the freedom to protest against the government and even the prime minister, without being fired upon by metallic pellet guns or AK-47s,” she added.
She also pointed to Singh’s record of engaging with Parliament and the media, noting that he held more than 100 unscripted press conferences as prime minister. The Indo-US nuclear deal was another major achievement, she said, ending decades of nuclear discrimination against India and marking the country’s arrival on the global stage. “We all certainly regret that he is not here to see this day,” Gandhi said, adding that it was nevertheless a solace that Singh’s prediction from January 2014 was becoming increasingly evident.
History, she said, would remember Singh as “a quiet, gentle but a most consequential prime minister”.
(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)

headline: Faced with demands to scrap the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, from different corners of the country on Tuesday — including a unanimous resolution passed in the Tamil Nadu Assembly and mass protests in the streets of Mizoram’...
full_text:
Faced with demands to scrap the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, from different corners of the country on Tuesday — including a unanimous resolution passed in the Tamil Nadu Assembly and mass protests in the streets of Mizoram’s capital — the Union government informed its allies and other parties that it would move a resolution in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday to refer the Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, sources said.
Moving the resolution urging the Centre to withdraw the Bill in its present form, Tamil Nadu Minister Rajamohan said the Assembly was deeply concerned by provisions in the legislation relating to the transfer, management, and sale of assets of charitable organisations to the government on grounds such as expiry of FCRA registration, non-renewal or refusal of renewal, cancellation of registration, or surrender of registration. “These provisions may adversely affect the autonomy of charitable organisations and, in particular, the functioning of educational and social welfare institutions run by the minority communities,” the resolution said, urging the Centre to undertake comprehensive consultations with all stakeholders, including State governments.
Fears that Christian institutions will be disproportionately affected by the Bill overflowed onto the streets in Mizoram, one of the three Christian-majority States in the country. Hundreds of Christians from different denominations participated in a rally in Aizawl under the newly formed Council of Churches in Mizoram. The Bill would give a designated authority sweeping powers over the land, buildings, funds, and other assets of churches and NGOs whose FCRA registrations are cancelled or not renewed, without judicial oversight, said R. Lalbiakliana, the council’s president.
The Bill came up for discussion at a meeting of the Business Advisory Committee of the Rajya Sabha, but the government made no commitments at the meeting, despite strong Opposition objections.
According to sources, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju raised the issue at the meeting. Congress general secretary and Rajya Sabha Chief Whip Jairam Ramesh pointed out that the Bill was not on the agenda and said the Opposition was of the view that it should be withdrawn. Trinamool Congress deputy leader in the Rajya Sabha Sagarika Ghose echoed the demand. DMK leader Tiruchi Siva also strongly opposed the Bill. “The FCRA Bill in its current form is unacceptable to us. Sending it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee will not serve any purpose,” he told The Hindu.
Sources said Mr. Rijiju did not make any commitment about the fate of the Bill, despite the Opposition insisting that a decision be taken at the meeting. However, the government later informed allies and other parties that it would move a resolution in the Lower House to refer the Bill to a JPC, according to sources.
BJP MP Sasmit Patra, who attended the meeting as a special invitee in his capacity as a member of the panel of chairpersons, is learnt to have argued that the Bill should be referred to a JPC for another round of scrutiny.
The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution said that “any amendment must preserve the principles of natural justice, proportionality, protection of property rights, legitimate expectation, and federalism. While ensuring transparency and accountability in foreign contributions, it must protect the rights of legitimate charitable, educational, religious, cultural and social welfare organisations.”
Asset seizure threat
The Bill, introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25, proposes tighter government oversight of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and foreign funding in the country.
Among its key provisions is the creation of a designated authority to manage and dispose of assets if an organisation loses its FCRA licence. Under the proposed law, if an FCRA certificate is cancelled, surrendered, or lapses, foreign contributions and all assets created using those contributions would vest in a government-appointed designated authority without any prior hearing or judicial determination.
The Bill also provides that if a fresh certificate is not obtained within a prescribed period, these assets could be sold or transferred to a government department, with the proceeds credited to the Consolidated Fund of India. The existing right to reclaim assets upon re-registration would be removed, and the founding institution would be permanently barred from reacquiring them.
Opposition parties have argued that the Bill disproportionately affects minority institutions, alleging that some of its provisions would restrict legitimate foreign funding for Christian NGOs and minority-run welfare and educational institutions. The government, however, has maintained that the proposed legislation is not religion-specific and is intended to strengthen the regulation of all foreign contributions.

headline: Cash-at-residence row: Inquiry report on Justice Yashwant Varma to be tabled in Lok Sabha
full_text:
Cash-at-residence row: Inquiry report on Justice Yashwant Varma to be tabled in Lok Sabha
The probe panel had submitted its findings to the Lok Sabha Speaker in May.
Report of an inquiry committee which invested allegations against Justice Yashwant Varma -- against whom removal proceedings were initiated over the alleged discovery of unaccounted for cash from his official residence -- will be placed before the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.
According to the list of business of the Lok Sabha for Wednesday, the secretary general will "lay" the two volumes of the report along with oral evidence in the House.
Probe panel submitted findings in May
The probe panel had submitted its findings to the Lok Sabha Speaker in May.
The Speaker had constituted a three-member inquiry committee on August 12, 2025, to probe the alleged discovery of wads of cash from the judge's Delhi bungalow.
Cash allegedly discovered after fire
A fire broke out in the official residence of Justice Varma on the night of March 14, 2025. Firefighters called to put out the blaze allegedly discovered massive amounts of burnt currency in a storeroom.
Varma has resigned
Justice Varma has since resigned, and removal proceedings against him have virtually become infructuous. His resignation, however, has not yet been notified by the law ministry.
Justice Varma was a judge of the Delhi High Court and was repatriated to his parent court, the Allahabad High Court, following the controversy.

headline: Assessing ramifications of new defence pact between Pak, Türkiye and Saudi: MEA
full_text:
Assessing ramifications of new defence pact between Pak, Türkiye and Saudi: MEA
The three Sunni Muslim countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7 that builds on a bilateral defence pact between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia
India said on Tuesday that it is assessing the ramifications of a joint defence agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye for the country’s national security and regional stability, and will take “all necessary measures” to safeguard its national interests.
The three Sunni Muslim countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Makkah on August 7, following a meeting between Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Türkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. The pact builds on a bilateral mutual defence agreement concluded by Pakistan and Saudi Arabia last year.
When external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked about the trilateral pact at a regular media briefing, he said India is closely following all “developments in the West Asia conflict” and will act to protect the country’s national interests.
“As far as this particular agreement is concerned, we are examining its implications, both from the perspective of our national security, as well as considerations of regional peace and stability,” Jaiswal said.
“India remains fully committed to safeguarding its national interests and will take all necessary measures in this regard,” he said, without going into details.
When Pakistan and Saudi Arabia concluded their mutual defence pact in September 2025, the Indian government said it would take all steps to protect the country’s national interests and ensure comprehensive national security in all domains, reflecting New Delhi’s concerns over the development. Saudi Arabia’s growing military proximity to Pakistan against the backdrop of the West Asia conflict has not gone down well in New Delhi, people familiar with the matter said.
A joint statement issued by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye on Friday said the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement builds on shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation. The pact also reflects the shared commitment of the three countries to strengthen their collective security and promote peace, security and stability in the region.
“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all. It further provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation among the three states,” the joint statement said.
Jaiswal responded to separate questions on events organised in different part of the world to mark the “independence” of Pakistan’s Balochistan province and the violent protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) by urging the world community to hold Pakistan accountable for human rights violations and atrocities.
“We continue to follow developments across the world. At the same time, I would like to highlight that we have seen the kind of human rights violations that were committed in PoK and other parts of that country. We call on the international community to hold Pakistan accountable for its misdeeds, abuses and flagrant violation of human rights, including of all its people,” he said.
Over the past few months, large-scale protests in PoK related to elections to the local assembly had led to a situation where “public discontent was answered with bullets, blackouts, repression and oppression”, Jaiswal said. More than 90 people were killed and many more injured in the violence, and the international community needs to hold Pakistan to account for the mass violation of human rights, he said.
Jaiswal said that there has been no change in India’s policy towards Pakistan. “We are where we were earlier. I need not emphasise which country is responsible for cross-border terrorism and which is the epicentre of terrorism, and where the action lies for stopping cross-border terrorism,” he said.

headline: In new video, PM Narendra Modi asks people to make Har Ghar Tiranga a celebration in every home

In new video, PM Narendra Modi asks people to make Har Ghar Tiranga a celebration in every home
Ahead of Independence Day, PM Narendra Modi has a request for citizens.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday asked citizens to participate in the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign and make it a celebration in every home ahead of Independence Day.
“Come, let us make #HarGharTiranga a celebration in every home,” Modi said in a post on Instagram, sharing a video related to the campaign. This came ahead of the 80th Independence Day celebrations on 15th of August.
“Come, let us celebrate August 15 with pride and honour, pay tribute to the freedom fighters, and pledge to build a developed India (Viksit Bharat). Har Ghar Tiranga, Ghar Ghar Tiranga, Har Mann Tiranga. Come, let us hoist the Tricolour at every home,” the PM said.
The 2026 edition of the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign is being observed in August, with citizens encouraged to hoist the national flag at their homes and participate in the nationwide celebration.
The campaign seeks to encourage people to bring the Tricolour into their homes and celebrate the spirit of independence.
‘Vande Mataram’ at Red Fort
Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Tuesday said the national song ‘Vande Mataram’ will be collectively sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort before the National Anthem on Independence Day.
On X, Gupta described the occasion as a “glorious and historic moment” and said it would be the first time that a collective rendition of ‘Vande Mataram’ would take place at the Red Fort before the National Anthem.
Gupta said ‘Vande Mataram’ has been an “immortal national mantra” of India’s independence movement, inspiring revolutionaries and giving voice to the sacrifices of freedom fighters.
She also linked the event to the 150th anniversary of ‘Vande Mataram’, the resolution passed in Parliament and the leadership of PM Modi, saying the developments would mark a “grand proclamation” of India’s national memory, cultural pride and devotion to the country.
“Vande Mataram. Jai Hind, Mother India!” Gupta said in her post.
Goa hosts Tiranga rally ahead of Independence Day
Panaji witnessed a Tiranga Rally as part of the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign, with participants taking part in a march from Miramar Circle to Azad Maidan via Kala Academy.
Chief minister Dr Pramod Sawant addressed participants at Kala Academy, PTI reported.

This came a day after the government offered to debate students’ issues and police action in Parliament with a reply by Shah to resolve the Parliament logjam.
The Congress on Tuesday took a jibe at Amit Shah, with party general secretary Jairam Ramesh saying the Union home minister was a “no-show” in Lok Sabha despite business reportedly listed against his name.
While Ramesh alleged that “those who intimidate are themselves cowards”, Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju responded saying Shah was “ready” with a reply. Rijiju claimed the Opposition was “not letting a discussion take place”, adding that Congress was “running away from it.”
This came a day after the government offered to debate students’ issues and police action in Parliament with a reply by Shah, in an effort to resolve the two-week-long Parliament logjam. ‘Shah proved that those who intimidate are themselves cowards’: Ramesh

That Home Minister should issue a statement. We are saying that we will have a full-fledged discussion and reply on each and every point...When that happens, everything will be clear,” he said.
“Rahul Gandhi has run away. Monsoon session is at its end, Govt has made an offer of detailed discussion on students' protest. Congress party should not run away,” he added.

headline: Deepti Gaur Mukerjee named Higher Education Secretary after NEET row
full_text:
Deepti Gaur Mukerjee named Higher Education Secretary after NEET row
The Centre has appointed Deepti Gaur Mukerjee as Higher Education Secretary in a late-night reshuffle. The move comes amid the NEET paper leak controversy and wider changes across key ministries.
Senior bureaucrat Deepti Gaur Mukerjee has been appointed as the new Higher Education Secretary as part of a top-level bureaucratic reshuffle carried out by the Centre on Monday. She succeeds Vineet Joshi, who was appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Panchayati Raj last month.
The Personnel Ministry said late on Monday night that the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet had approved Mukerjee's appointment in a partial modification of its July 23 order. The appointment comes in the wake of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) paper leak controversy.
Mukerjee, a 1993 batch Indian Administrative Service officer of the Madhya Pradesh cadre, is currently serving as the Corporate Affairs Secretary. In the earlier order, Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary in the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, had also been named Higher Education Secretary in place of Joshi.
Following the latest changes, Youth Affairs Secretary Pallavi Jain Govil will be the new Corporate Affairs Secretary in place of Mukerjee. Sunil Paliwal, Chairman of the Inland Waterways Authority of India, has been appointed Youth Affairs Secretary in place of Govil, while Sushil Kumar Lohani, Officer on Special Duty in the Cabinet Secretariat, will succeed Paliwal as Chairman of the Inland Waterways Authority of India.
In another change, V L Kantha Rao, Secretary in the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, has been appointed Officer on Special Duty in the Department of Official Language in the Ministry of Home Affairs. He will take over as Secretary in the Department of Official Language after the retirement of incumbent Ansuli Arya at the end of next month. Senior bureaucrat Archana Varma, a 1995 batch Indian Administrative Service officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre and currently Mission Director of the National Water Mission, will replace Rao as Secretary in the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation.
The reshuffle includes Mukerjee's move to the Higher Education Department, changes in the Corporate Affairs and Youth Affairs ministries, a new chairman for the Inland Waterways Authority of India, and fresh appointments in the departments of Official Language and Water Resources.

headline: The Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA), which met in Delhi on Tuesday (August 11, 2026), affirmed and endorsed the decision by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) to direct Karnataka to ensure the release of Cauvery water at the rate...
full_text:
The Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA), which met in Delhi on Tuesday (August 11, 2026), affirmed and endorsed the decision by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) to direct Karnataka to ensure the release of Cauvery water at the rate of 12,000 cusecs a day from Wednesday for the next 15 days to neighbouring Tamil Nadu.
This means that Karnataka would have to provide about 15.55 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft), considering that the flow of 11,574 cusecs in 24 hours equals one tmc ft.
Distress and dispute: On Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and the Cauvery
Responding to this, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said a decision on the next course of action would be taken after carefully assessing the water availability in the State. He stressed the need to protect the interests of State’s farmers while also complying with the orders of the Authority and the CWRC. He is set to hold a meeting with legal experts and bureaucrats on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) on the possible legal options.
CWMA chairperson Saumitra Kumar Haldar told The Hindu later that Karnataka “is in a comfortable position” to comply with its order. The CWMA arrived at the decision after considering the storage, inflows, and the meteorological outlook for the next seven days, he said.
Karnataka’s argument
Earlier, Karnataka appealed to the CWMA to defer any decision on further releases and take a considered decision based on actual hydrological realities at the end of the South-west monsoon season. If not, it pleaded, the CWMA should at least reduce the quantum of water release from 12,000 cusecs a day to 10,000 cusecs.
Karnataka told the CWMA that the Cauvery basin was “reeling under severe hydrological distress”. It pointed out that all four reservoirs in the Cauvery basin had received only 77.746 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft) of cumulative inflows in this water year, which was “about 47% less” than the 30-year average. Also, the inflows to the reservoirs were rapidly declining, it said.
Karnataka argued that it had already ensured flows of 86,942 cusecs at Biligundlu [the measuring point of Cauvery flow on the inter-State boundary] as against the prescribed quantum of 52,500 cusecs by the CWMA. It argued that the realisation by Tamil Nadu was bound to be much more as additional flows too were in transit
It argued that there was no scope for further water release to the neighbouring State given its own “deficit monsoon, dwindling inflows and limited storage”. Also, there was a dire need to conserve water for drinking and essential uses besides taking care of farmers’ kharif crop.
Karnataka contended that Tamil Nadu, in contrast, was “in an advantageous position” as it already had “sufficient storage” in its reservoirs, besides having the benefit of forthcoming north-east monsoon as well as any downstream flows.
Also read: Why did Cauvery panel order Karnataka to release water? | Explained
The State said that distress sharing must be equitable, while contending that a rigid, predetermined pro-rata formula based solely on inflows into Karnataka’s reservoirs could “disproportionately burden the State”. Karnataka further demanded that a broader system be put in place to assess distress based on the situation across the entire basin, rather than merely on inflows to its four reservoirs.
TN’s demands and arguments
On its part, Tamil Nadu appealed to the CWMA to direct Karnataka to ensure releases of 37 tmc ft at Biligundlu by August end, taking cognisance of the backlog and the quantum that is due on pro-rata basis from August 13 to 31.
It argued that maintaining the entire one year’s drinking water requirement for Bengaluru as a contingency plan against any worst-case scenario was not justified and should not be used to deny its legitimate share.
Tamil Nadu argued that its basin area experienced a much higher rainfall deficit of 36% so far in this water year, compared with the 9% deficit in upstream of KRS and 19% in that of Kabini.
Tamil Nadu maintained that the present substantial downstream flow to it was largely due to surplus flow from Kabini and contended that despite improved inflows into the KRS catchment, releases from this reservoir had remained low, indicating issues related to equitable sharing of available flows. It appealed to the CWMA to direct Karnataka to regulate releases from both KRS and Kabini.
It argued that Karnataka’s projection of substantial benefit to Tamil Nadu from the north-east monsoon “lacked adequate scientific basis.”
CWMA stance
Speaking to The Hindu, the CWMA chairperson said that as “against the long term average of 83 tmc ft in the four reservoirs of Karnataka in the Cauvery basin, the current storage is 77 tmc ft”. Besides, the upper riparian State’s reservoirs would be receiving 2 to 2.5 tmc ft a day at least for the next one week. “It is for this reason that we have decided that Karnataka can spare one tmc ft a day to Tamil Nadu,” Mr. Haldar observed.
While the upper riparian State wanted the Authority to settle for 9,000-10,000 cusecs (0.78 tmc ft to 0.86 tmc ft a day), Tamil Nadu, the lower riparian State, had sought the release of 1.5 tmc ft a day.
Referring to the circumstances under which the CWMA decided on July 30 to go by the CWRC’s position, Mr. Haldar said, “We were not sure how the southwest monsoon would behave. Even the meteorological forecast, both from the Indian Meteorological Department and Skymet, was not positive. As there was a 50% deficit in realisation at Biligundulu, we had asked Karnataka to release about 4.5 tmc ft. But, the rain started from then on.”
As for the need for a “permanent, scientific” distress-sharing formula, Mr. Haldar replied that “given the conditions that characterise the basin, there is no single formula that will work in the case of the Cauvery, as dynamics keep on changing”. However, he had sought views of the riparian States to come up with a formula, the chairperson added.

headline: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) will hold its annual Akhil Bharatiya Samanvay Baithak (All India Coordination Meeting) at Gudilova in Andhra Pradesh’s Visakhapatnam district from August 19 to 21, the organisation said on Monday.

headline: NEW DELHI: As India gears up to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on Aug 15, three Russian cosmonauts on board the International Space Station have extended their I-Day greetings to the Indian people by holding the tricolour and sending a special v...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: As India gears up to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on Aug 15, three Russian cosmonauts on board the International Space Station have extended their I-Day greetings to the Indian people by holding the tricolour and sending a special video message recalling decades-old friendship between Moscow and New Delhi. The message transmitted from the space station from an altitude of 408 km serves as a masterclass in orbital diplomacy.In the video message reposted by the Embassy of Russia in India on Monday, Russian space crew â Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Andrey Fedyaev â congratulated India and described space exploration as a key pillar of bilateral ties. âEight decades ago, India broke free from colonial rule and embarked on a journey towards self-reliance and prosperity... Dear friends, today the Republic of India is celebrating its 80th Independence Day,â cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov said, extending his wishes to India.
Holding the tricolour alongside three posters showcasing India-Russia space cooperation, the space crew highlighted key milestones in the Indo-Russian partnership, including the 1975 launch of Indiaâs Aryabhata satellite and 1984 flight of India-born cosmonaut Rakesh Sharma.
The cosmonauts also talked about Indiaâs most-ambitious ongoing Gaganyaan programme, noting four Indian astronauts (Gaganauts) were trained in Russia â Prashanth Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap, and Shubhanshu Shukla completed their space training module at Russia's Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre in Star City between Feb 2020 and March 2021.Anna Kikina recalled Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarinâs historic visit to India in Nov 1961. She quoted Gagarinâs famous words about the country: âIndia is very beautiful from above, but it is even more beautiful and special because it is home to true friends.ââThe friendship between our countries has been time-tested, and space exploration is one of the main areas of our cooperation,â she said.

headline: Video: Uttarakhand flashflood rips apart bridge, sweeps away vehicle and driver
full_text:
Video: Uttarakhand flashflood rips apart bridge, sweeps away vehicle and driver
A bridge collapse cut off the border area and around a dozen villages, with rescue teams deployed to search for the missing BRO driver.
A sudden surge of floodwaters triggered by cloudbursts and intense monsoon rains turned the Tamak drain in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli into a raging torrent, sweeping away a Bailey bridge, a vehicle and a Border Roads Organisation (BRO) driver.
The bridge on the Malari-Niti National Highway connects Jyotirmath to the border area and the collapse snapped road connectivity to around a dozen villages, including Jumma and Niti and cut off the frontier.
A BRO driver, Pankaj, a resident of Pithoragarh district, was swept away by the powerful current as he was watching the floodwaters when the bridge suddenly collapsed. He remained missing.
A vehicle was also swept away as the floodwaters surged through the drain.
Rescue teams were quickly mobilised, with personnel from the district administration, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) dispatched to the site.
Following the bridge collapse, authorities suspended traffic on nearby roads as well. Officials said administrative teams were assessing the damage, while the BRO began work on alternative arrangements. Traffic is expected to be restored within a day or two, Chamoli District Disaster Management Officer NK Joshi added.
Over the past several years, floods and landslides in the Tamak drain have disrupted the Joshimath-Niti road, while flood debris has repeatedly choked the nearby Dhauli Ganga.
Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami directed officials to intensify relief and rescue operations and take precautionary measures in the lower areas following the flooding.
Dhami also directed officials to ensure that supplies of ration, food, medicines and other essential commodities to villages in the surrounding areas are not affected by the bridge collapse.

headline: 18 shortlisted for Ram Temple CEO post amid donation case, interviews from today
full_text:
18 shortlisted for Ram Temple CEO post amid donation case, interviews from today
The 18 shortlisted candidates reached Ayodhya late on Monday and were instructed to not talk to media during their stay in the city.
Eighteen candidates have been shortlisted from a pool of 5,200 applicants for the first full-time chief executive officer (CEO) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, people familiar with the matter said on Monday.
The decision to appoint a full-time CEO was taken after the allegations of embezzlement of donation funds came to light.
Shortlisted candidates reach Ayodhya
According to a senior trust official, all 18 candidates reached Ayodhya late on Monday and stayed at various locations in the temple town suggested by the trust, a trust official said.
The shortlisted candidates, who include former bureaucrats and former senior position holders of temples in South India, will be interviewed at the temple premises on Tuesday and Wednesday by a panel comprising former justice Pramod Kohli, lieutenant general (retired) Vishnukant Chaturvedi and scientist Suresh Haware, former chairman of the Shirdi Sai Baba Trust, a senior staff member of the trust said, adding that the interview process will start at 10am.

“The interview will be conducted in the Ram temple and the candidates have been instructed not to interact with the media,” the trust official aware of the details said.
From the 18 applicants, it will zero in on three names for the trust to make the final call.
CEO's rule and current general secretary
The CEO’s primary responsibility will be to oversee the administration and management of the Ram temple’s affairs and businesses. According to the official, the selected candidate will have to be a practising Hindu and strictly follow Hindu traditions and guidelines.
The candidate will also have to be a pure vegetarian and a strict teetotaller.
The age criterion for the post has been fixed between 50 and 70 years, the official added.

Rai is currently senior vice president of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad.

headline: Nagpur: Maharashtra chief ministerDevendra Fadnavis on Monday defended proposed amendments to Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), alleging that a section of organizations receiving foreign funds had used the money for "anti-national activit...
full_text:
Nagpur: Maharashtra chief ministerDevendra Fadnavis on Monday defended proposed amendments to Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), alleging that a section of organizations receiving foreign funds had used the money for "anti-national activities" and that the changes were intended to curb such misuse rather than target any particular community.Responding to criticism from Congress, which has described the proposed amendments as "anti-Christian", he said FCRA framework applies uniformly to every organisation receiving foreign contributions, irrespective of religion or community."The reason for bringing the FCRA amendments is that some organisations have been bringing foreign money into the country and using it for anti-national activities. That has to stop," Fadnavis said."Those who are doing good work have nothing to worry about. There will be an FCRA mechanism and their licences will be protected," he said.Rejecting the allegation that the amendments specifically target Christian organizations, Fadnavis said the law governs all entities receiving foreign donations."This is not a question of one community. It is applicable to every organization that receives foreign donations, irrespective of its community," he said.
Fadnavis said anyone with reservations about the proposed legislation should raise them during the parliamentary process, adding that Union govt was open to hearing different views."I believe that if anyone has objections, they should raise them in Parliament. The govt of India is receptive," he said.
Referring to statements made in the United States on the proposed amendments, Fadnavis questioned why individuals outside India were reacting to the legislation."Some people in the US have commented on the FCRA Amendment Bill. What does that mean? The very purpose of these amendments becomes clear from such reactions," he said, without elaborating further.The CM reiterated that the objective of the proposed amendments was to ensure accountability in the use of foreign contributions and prevent their misuse, while protecting organizations carrying out lawful activities.

headline: Mamata Banerjee faces 'chor' slogans at protest against BJP leader's Netaji remarks
full_text:
Mamata Banerjee faces 'chor' slogans at protest against BJP leader's Netaji remarks
Mamata Banerjee faced 'chor, chor' slogans during a TMC protest in Kolkata over remarks on Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose made by a BJP leader.
TMC chief Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday faced "chor, chor" slogans in Kolkata during a party programme held to protest controversial remarks about Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose by a BJP MP. The disruption came just two days after Banerjee was met by similar protests in Halisahar, adding to the political tension around her public appearances.
The TMC programme had been organised around alleged derogatory comments on Netaji, but it turned into another confrontation as a group gathered near the venue and raised slogans against Banerjee. BJP leader Nagendra Roy's remarks have given the TMC an opening to present the issue as an attack on Bengal's nationalist legacy, while the protests against Banerjee have shifted attention to allegations of corruption and public anger.
Banerjee reached Shyambazar five-point crossing in north Kolkata carrying a portrait of freedom fighter Khudiram Bose and paid tribute at the feet of Netaji's statue. The programme was organised by the TMC over remarks made by Roy, popularly known as Ananta Maharaj.
The controversy began after Roy described Netaji as a "war criminal", questioned his leadership and raised doubts over the role of the Azad Hind Fauj in India's freedom struggle. West Bengal BJP leaders later distanced themselves from the statement, saying Roy's comments were personal and were neither endorsed nor believed by the party.
As Tuesday's event was underway, a group raised "chor, chor" slogans targeting Banerjee, briefly disrupting the proceedings. The TMC alleged that the protest at Shyambazar was deliberately orchestrated by people backed by the BJP to disturb the programme and insult Banerjee.
The BJP has denied involvement in the Halisahar incident as well, with its leaders saying the protests reflected public anger against Banerjee. On Sunday, protesters surrounded her vehicle and shouted "chor" slogans, and also allegedly threw mud and slippers, when she had gone to meet the family of a TMC worker who died in police custody. Police personnel formed a cordon around her vehicle as protesters reportedly blocked its passage.
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had denied any role of his party in that episode, saying it showed "strong public anger" against Banerjee. He had also said that since Banerjee had "committed so much theft", she would have to hear people call her a "thief".
Banerjee, meanwhile, tried to keep the focus on the freedom movement by invoking Netaji, Mahatma Gandhi and Matangini Hazra. She said her party did not organise programmes merely for "show" but honoured freedom fighters from the heart.
With similar slogans being raised at two events within days, the political clash has sharpened around both Netaji's legacy and Banerjee's public standing.

headline: 'Tamil Nadu waiting to see CM Vijay pick Trisha as deputy CM': AIADMK leader
full_text:
'Tamil Nadu waiting to see CM Vijay pick Trisha as deputy CM': AIADMK leader
In a video, Udhayakumar can be heard saying that the TVK government was appointing individuals closely associated with the chief minister.
In remarks that could stoke fresh controversy, All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) leader R B Udhayakumar on Tuesday took a swipe at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay, asking him when he would appoint actor Trisha Krishnan as deputy chief minister.
His remarks came days after former Tamil Nadu deputy chief minister Udhayanidhi Stalin sparked an uproar with an offensive remark apparently aimed at the actor. Stalin was arrested for over 10 hours before being released last week.
Actor-politician Vijay has worked in several films with actor Trisha.
What did Udhayakumar say on Trisha?
In a video that has gone viral, Udhayakumar is heard saying that the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government was appointing individuals closely associated with the chief minister, specifically producers and technical crew members who worked in his films, to various official government positions.
The former state minister went on to name the persons appointed as temple trustee, Tamil Nadu government's special representative in New Delhi, personal secretary to the chief minister, head of state film training institute, as government advisors, and sarcastically remarked when Trisha would be appointed as deputy Chief Minister.
“The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, which sits on the throne of Tamil Nadu's governance, has been proclaiming the slogan "equality by birth" (Pirappokkum Ella Uyirkkum). We all believed it, but now the government appointments are turning into a major controversy. Producers and technical artists who worked in Chief Minister Vijay’s films are currently being quietly appointed to government positions. Currently, as a member of the Temple Board of Trustees, Chief Minister Vijay's GOAT movie producer Archana Kalpathi, whose roots are in Kerala, has been appointed,” he said.
“Earlier, Karnataka-rooted Venkat Narayana, the producer of the film Jananayagan starring our Chief Minister Vijay, was appointed as Tamil Nadu government's Special Representative in Delhi. Similarly, Jagadish Palanisamy, co-producer of Vijay’s film Leo, has been appointed as the Chief Minister's Personal Secretary. Manoj Paramahamsa, the cinematographer of the Vijay-starrer Beast, has been appointed as the Chairman of the Film and Television Institute of Tamil Nadu,” he added.
Udhayakumar continued: “Furthermore, the Chief Minister's close aides John Arokiaswamy and Ramkumar have been appointed as government advisors. Tamil Nadu is now waiting in shock and anticipation to see when an announcement will be made appointing Ms Trisha as the Deputy Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu.”
Drama at the age is embarrassing: Actor Trisha Krishnan’s cryptic post
Meanwhile, actor Trisha on Tuesday shared a cryptic Instagram story that said: “Drama at this age is embarrassing… Go make some money and find peace”.
She did not mention any name but the post coincided with the surfacing of the video featuring Udhayakumar making the remarks and a week after Udhayanidhi targeted the actor.
Posters pasted by a Trisha fan club also surfaced in Madurai, criticising Udhayakumar’s comments.
Udhayanidhi Stalin arrested, released amid high drama
Last week, Udhayanidhi was arrested on charges of insulting the modesty of a woman, obscenity and criminal intimidation, among others, over an obscene remark apparently aimed at the female actor.
The controversy began on August 3 when Udhayanidhi was speaking at a rally in Thanjavur meant to press the state government on the Cauvery water sharing – a century-old irritant in relations between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. As the crowd chanted the name of Trisha – a friend of the chief minister – Udhayanidhi made an obscene remark.
On August 4, Udhayanidhi was arrested from his residence in Chennai at 10am and taken to Thanjavur. The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) hit the streets and approached the Madras high court, where the state government clarified that Udhayanidhi would be released “today itself”.
Later that evening, Udhayanidhi was taken to the Sengipatti police station after huge crowds gathered in Thanjavur – roughly 350km from state capital Chennai, he was quizzed for more than an hour. At around 8pm, he was released on station bail, and returned to Chennai around midnight.
“They arrested me for nothing. I have not said anything wrong. I have not said anything wrong against anybody,” the son of former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin said. The 49-year-old leader stood atop a vehicle and greeted supporters late into the evening at Sengipatti in a show of strength by the DMK. “With 3,000 police personnel, they took us by road from Chennai to Thanjavur like a terrorist,” he said, dismissing the allegation that he made offensive comments.
Row erupts, MK Stalin defends son
DMK chief MK Stalin defended his son. “Udhayanidhi is not someone who speaks inappropriately. Even if he were to make a mistake in his speech, he is of the nature to apologise immediately,” he said.
AIADMK chief Edapaddi Palaniswami criticised Udhayanidhi. “Unaware of the dignity of the position he holds, his continuous loose talk and derogatory remarks about women are strongly condemnable,” the former chief minister said.
DMDK chief Premalatha Vijayakanth said, “This act of stifling the opposition is condemnable.”
BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan attacked the DMK, saying “We strongly condemn the derogatory words of Udhayanidhi Stalin against womenhood, humiliating women celebrities.”
(With inputs from Vijay Karthik)

headline: FSSAI bans plastic, foil packaging for pan masala under new rules
full_text:
FSSAI bans plastic, foil packaging for pan masala under new rules
Moving forward, pan masala can only be sold in eco-friendly packaging or traditional rigid containers.
India’s food safety regulator, FSSAI, has updated its packaging rules to ban plastic and foil packaging for pan masala. Under the new Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026, manufacturers can no longer use plastic-based materials, plastic laminates, aluminum foil, or metallised layers to pack pan masala.
Moving forward, pan masala can only be sold in eco-friendly packaging or traditional rigid containers.
The new rules have been notified as the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026 and will come into force from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette, according to a press release.
ALSO READ | Rotten meat, fungus on veggies: Bengaluru's 3-star, 5-star hotels in soup over food safety violations
What packaging will be allowed?
Under the amended regulations, pan masala can be packed using paper, paper board, cellulose or other naturally derived materials.
That said, these materials must be completely free of plastic, including polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and other synthetic polymers, copolymers or laminates. Tin and glass containers have also been listed as permitted packaging materials for pan masala.
ALSO READ | Manimahesh Yatra: Sale of small plastic bottles, snack packets banned along yatra route
Plastic waste rules will also apply
The amendment further states that relevant provisions under clauses (f) and (i) of Rule 4(1) of the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, will also apply to pan masala packaging.
The FSSAI issued the amendment under the powers granted by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, with the prior approval of the Central Government.
What other plastic packaging is banned?
India already prohibits plastic sachets used to store, pack or sell gutkha, tobacco and pan masala under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016. The latest FSSAI amendment specifically lays down permitted materials for pan masala packaging and excludes plastic-based and plastic-laminated materials.
ALSO READ | Delhi high court stays FSSAI ban on Dabur selling food products with '100 per cent' claims
Earlier, the government completely banned plastic sachets used for storing, packing or selling gutkha, tobacco and pan masala under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016. The Plastic Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011 prohibited the use of plastic sachets for storing, packing or selling gutkha, tobacco and pan masala. They also said plastic material in any form could not be used for packing these products.
India also prohibits plastic carry bags and plastic sheets below 50 microns under the Plastic Waste Management Rules. The rules were introduced in 2016 and increased the minimum thickness for plastic carry bags from 40 microns to 50 microns.
Plastic wrapping or packing films around sweet boxes, invitation cards and cigarette packets are also prohibited under the Plastic Waste Management Rules.

headline: Pan masala's plastic packaging banned; FSSAI mandates paper, tin or glass
full_text:
Pan masala's plastic packaging banned; FSSAI mandates paper, tin or glass
The FSSAI has targeted the plastic used in pan masala's packaging. Under the new rules, pan masala manufacturers can use only plastic-free paper, paperboard, cellulose or other naturally derived materials, along with tin or glass containers.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has introduced new packaging requirements for pan masala, specifying plastic-free materials that can be used to package the product and ruling out plastic, aluminium foil and metallised layers from the permitted packaging options.
The changes were notified through the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026, published in the Gazette of India on Monday (August 10).
The amendment modifies the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018 by adding pan masala as a new entry under Schedule 4, which deals with the list of suggestive packaging materials.
Under the new provisions of the FSSAI, which comes under the Union Ministry of Health and Welfare, pan masala can be packaged in paper, paperboard, cellulose or other naturally derived materials, but these materials must be completely free from plastic.
The notification specifically states that the packaging cannot contain polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), or any other synthetic polymers, copolymers or laminates.
The restriction goes beyond conventional plastic packaging. The specified paper and naturally derived materials must also be free from aluminium foil and metallised layers. This means packaging that uses a paper-based outer material but contains plastic or metallised layers within the packaging would not meet the material specifications set out in the amendment.
FSSAI has also permitted manufacturers to use tin or glass containers for pan masala. These are listed separately as permitted packaging options under the new entry.
The amendment further states that certain provisions of the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, framed under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, will also apply to pan masala packaging.
The regulations come into force from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. FSSAI notified the final amendment after completing a consultation process on the proposed changes.
The authority had first published the draft Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026, on April 28, inviting objections and suggestions from people likely to be affected by the proposed regulations.
The draft was open for public feedback for a period of 60 days.
FSSAI said the objections and suggestions received from the public in response to the draft were considered before the final amendment was issued.
The final notification was issued under the powers granted to FSSAI under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, with the previous approval of the Central Government.
The notification is specifically a packaging regulation.
It does not announce a ban on pan masala as a product. Instead, it adds pan masala to the packaging schedule and specifies the materials that can be used for its packaging.
The new rules therefore place the focus on moving pan masala packaging away from plastic-based materials.
Manufacturers using paper, paperboard, cellulose or other naturally derived materials will have to ensure that these materials contain no plastic, synthetic polymer, copolymer or laminate and do not use aluminium foil or metallised layers.
The other packaging alternatives explicitly listed by FSSAI are tin and glass containers. With the amendment coming into force upon publication, these provisions now form part of the amended Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018.

headline: Crocodile tears: Dharmendra Pradhan slams Rahul Gandhi over Jharkhand protests
full_text:
Crocodile tears: Dharmendra Pradhan slams Rahul Gandhi over Jharkhand protests
Dharmendra Pradhan accused Rahul Gandhi and the Congress of dodging a Parliament debate on student issues. The clash deepened the deadlock in the House and sharpened the BJP's charge of double standards on youth concerns.
Former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Tuesday attacked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the Opposition's stand on a discussion on student issues in Parliament. He accused Gandhi of spreading lies and shedding "crocodile tears" instead of agreeing to take part in the debate.
Pradhan also alleged that the Congress was showing "double standards" on issues linked to youth and students. He referred to the police action against job aspirants protesting over alleged irregularities in recruitment exams in Jharkhand, where the Congress is part of the JMM-led coalition government.
In a post on X in Hindi, Pradhan said, "The Congress party's approach to democracy is also selective. There is violence against youth wherever it holds power. And where it has to shine its politics, there is falsehood and uproar."
He said the country had witnessed what he described as brutality against students in Jharkhand and questioned why Rahul Gandhi, who often addresses issues through press conferences, had remained silent on the matter.
On Monday, the government offered to hold a discussion in the Lok Sabha on student protests, with Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju saying in the House that Home Minister Amit Shah would respond to the debate.
However, the Congress and its allies said they would agree to the offer only if a discussion on the alleged embezzlement of Ram temple donations was also taken up.
The BJP then accused Gandhi of shifting the goalposts to deliberately disrupt Parliament.
As the deadlock between the government and the Opposition continued on Tuesday, Pradhan said, "The Congress is constantly spreading lies regarding the students' interests. Rahul Gandhi lacks facts."
He also criticised Gandhi for making what he called "baseless" allegations against the Union home minister, and described the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha as "a habitual liar".
Pradhan said, "Gandhi has no intention of attending Parliament or listening to the reply. All he wants to do is spread falsehoods and shed crocodile tears."
Pradhan further alleged that while the government was ready to discuss "every issue" in Parliament, the Congress was disrupting proceedings and working against the interests of the country and its youth.
"This is because their intent is to prioritise their own interests over the national interest. They create a ruckus outside (Parliament Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) when discussions are taking place inside the House, simply because they lack the capacity to listen to the answers provided there," he said.
He added that the country’s youth had understood what he described as the Congress’ “double standards” and accused Rahul Gandhi and the party of carrying a mindset rooted in the Emergency era, warning that there was no place for dictatorship in a democracy.
The exchange came as the government and the Opposition remained at odds over a discussion on student issues in Parliament, with Pradhan stepping up the BJP's attack on Gandhi over the Congress' stand and its handling of youth-related issues in states where it shares power.

full_text:
FSSAI tightens pan masala packaging norms; bans plastic, foil and synthetic laminates

Pan masala may now only be packaged in paper, paperboard, cellulose, or other naturally derived materials (Photo: Agencies).
NEW DELHI: India's food safety regulator has barred the use of plastic and plastic-laminated packaging for pan masala, under an amendment aimed at tightening existing packaging norms, according to a press release.The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has specified that pan masala may now only be packaged in paper, paperboard, cellulose, or other naturally derived materials. Such materials must be entirely free of plastic, including polyethene, polypropylene, polyester, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and other synthetic polymers, copolymers or laminates, as well as aluminium foil or metallised layers, the release said. Tin and glass containers continue to be permitted, it added.The press release further stated that packaging will also need to conform to clauses (f) and (i) of sub-rule 1 of rule 4 of the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, framed under the Environment Protection Act, 1986.The amendment has been incorporated as a new entry in Schedule IV of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018, which lists suggested packaging materials. It has been placed right after the existing entries at Serial Number 10, the release said.
Notified as the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026, the amendment will come into force from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette, according to the release.The regulations were issued by FSSAI in exercise of powers conferred under clause (k) of sub-section (2) of Section 92 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and with prior approval of the Central Government, the release said.
