headline: Manmohan Singh ‘most consequential PM’: Sonia Gandhi says his prophecy on Narendra Modi is coming true
full_text:
Manmohan Singh ‘most consequential PM’: Sonia Gandhi says his prophecy on Narendra Modi is coming true
Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson's remarks come days after Supreme Court gave the late ex-PM Manmohan Singh a clean chit in coal block allocation case.
Echoing the late ex-PM Manmohan Singh's words about himself, that history will remember him kindly, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi said on Tuesday that he was a quiet but “most consequential” prime minister that India has had.
The Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson's remarks in an article published in The Indian Express came days after the Supreme Court gave Manmohan Singh the clean chit in the coal block allocation case, one of the many corruption cases of the Congress-led UPA era before Narendra Modi and the BJP ascended to power in 2014.
"The date July 29, 2026, was an important but unacknowledged day in our recent political history as in a remarkable judgment, the Supreme Court upheld the CBI's clean chit to Dr Manmohan Singh in the alleged coal block allocation scam," Gandhi noted.
She said the judgment brings to a conclusion one of the most tragic arcs of our public discourse — “the witch-hunt against Dr Singh, a man of the most remarkable probity and integrity”.
Swipes at Modi
On Modi, Sonia Gandhi said that Manmohan Singh's prophetic prediction of January 2014 was now becoming increasingly self-evident, in an apparent reference to his then statement that it would be “disastrous for the country” to have Modi as PM.
In a more immediate swipe at Modi, Sonia Gandhi further referred to his video in which he said he was “forgiving” students who'd used abusive words against him during the recent protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party that forced a change of education minister. Sonia Gandhi said that since Modi was these days forgiving India's students for attacking him, perhaps he would take this opportunity to forgive himself for his slander against Manmohan Singh.
It was not a coincidence that Modi was also among the most vocal proponents of the attack on Manmohan Singh, she said. “His snide and atrocious remarks in the Rajya Sabha on February 8, 2017, that only Dr Singh knew 'the art of bathing with a raincoat on', will go down as the lowest point of our parliamentary history,” she said.
"The lobby against [Manmohan Singh] was coordinated and well-organised, with actors stretching from the bureaucracy to the media, the judiciary, civil society, and most certainly to the RSS and BJP… Today, their bogus crusade has come to its inevitable conclusion of nothingness. Dr Singh has been vindicated on every count," Gandhi said in her article.
On the SC clean shit, she that, more importantly, the top court pulled up the trial court for rejecting the CBI's closure reports and making adverse observations against the former prime minister for “no compelling reason”.
‘Stark contrast’
Manmohan Singh's record of integrity and accountability stands in stark contrast to how the Modi government has operated, so clearly and grossly misusing agencies designed to investigate crime and corruption like the ED and the CBI, she said.
“Leaders are either silenced through coercion or cynically folded into the BJP or, in some remarkable instances, rewarded with ministerial positions as well… When credible accusations of corruption emerge, the Modi government simply brushes them aside. Corrupt when you're in the Opposition, suddenly clean when you jump ship!” Sonia Gandhi wrote.
“Introspection, like charity, must begin from home. Ultimately, the attack on Dr Singh was motivated by a desperate desire to shift the public conversation and narrative away from his outstanding governance record,” she further said.
Manmohan Singh's government heralded profound economic change with unprecedented rates of growth and a consumption and private investment boom that propelled India into the ranks of middle-income countries, Gandhi stressed.
In 2008, when the global economy faced turbulence and collapse, India demonstrated its resilience, she said. “Let us not forget that in spite of the reworking of how the growth of India's GDP is calculated, the 10 years of the UPA government saw higher economic growth than the past 12 years, resulting in millions being pulled out of poverty,” Gandhi said.
UPA's work 'being sought to be amended'
The Manmohan Singh government delivered on the constitutional promise of a Right to Education and expanded social justice through the introduction of OBC reservation in centrally-funded higher education institutes like the IITs and IIMs, she said. “The Forest Rights Act recognised the ancestral rights of our Adivasi and forest-dwelling communities, after a decades-long struggle. The MGNREGA, recently demolished by the Modi government, was the most powerful social security intervention set up anywhere,” she said.
Another signature achievement of Singh's government was the National Food Security Act, 2013, which identified and guaranteed access to basic food rations for crores of families, she said. “This is being sought to be amended. Soon after he demitted office, he had warned that the rights-based legislation would come under assault and his fears have, most sadly, come true,” she said.
Singh heralded a new era of transparency in government through the landmark Right to Information Act, which enabled citizens to access the government's inner workings, she said.
"The RTI now stands totally emasculated. There was an explosion of independent media, which was characterised by a fearlessness that appears more remarkable when juxtaposed with its current enfeeblement," she said.
Civil society emerged as a force to be reckoned with, and our students had the freedom to protest against the government and even the prime minister, without being fired upon by metallic pellet guns or AK-47s, Gandhi said, taking a swipe at the Modi government.
The prime minister regularly made himself accountable to Parliament and to the media through 100-plus unscripted press conferences, she said.
"And of course, we cannot forget that the landmark and path-breaking Indo-US nuclear deal, which overturned decades of nuclear discrimination against and denial towards India and marked our arrival on the global stage, was possible because of his political courage and sustained initiative," she said.
The “mischievous and indefensible” allegations against his integrity have been exposed as hollow, and his record as prime minister is increasingly being recognised for what it was — a period of decisive economic, political, and social advancement in Indian history, she said.
"We all certainly regret that he is not here to see this day and to guide the nation with his wisdom. But it is a solace to us all that his prophetic prediction of January 2014 is becoming increasingly self-evident with every passing day… History will indeed remember him kindly as a quiet, gentle but a most consequential prime minister," Gandhi said.
Her remarks come after the apex court closed the criminal case against Singh by setting aside a summoning order passed against him. The veteran Congress leader, who passed away on December 27, 2024, now stands formally acquitted in the high-profile criminal case.

headline: John Brittas vs Sushmita Dev ‘lungiwala’ row escalates as BJP MP moves privilege notice against CPI(M) leader
full_text:
John Brittas vs Sushmita Dev ‘lungiwala’ row escalates as BJP MP moves privilege notice against CPI(M) leader
The CPI(M) leader had also earlier moved a privilege notice against Sushmita Dev and criticised the use of stereotypes in parliamentary discourse.
The row betweem Sushmita Dev and John Brittas escalated as the BJP MP moved a breach of privilege notice against the CPI(M) leader on Wednesday. This came hours after CPI(M) lawmaker John Brittas alleged that a member from the ruling side made disparaging remarks about his attire during his Monday address, calling him "lungi-wala."
Brittas further went on to move a breach of privilege notice against Dev.“I’m a proud Indian, South Indian and a proud Malayali…I cherish every moment being a Malayali — our language, culture, cuisine, and of course, our attire,” Brittas said.
Alleging that a member of the House, without naming the Bharatiya Dev, disturbed him and also passed remarks on his attire, he said, “The other day, an honourable member whom I hold in high esteem— that member came here and was disturbing me when I was fulfilling my obligation as a mover of a statutory resolution. The verbal duel is okay. We fight each other. But she repeatedly called me ‘lungi-wala, lungi-wala.’”
Dev said that neither she nor any other member has cast aspersions against any state’s attire. She added that she is willing to approach Brittas personally.
JP Nadda said both members can come to his chamber to clarify the misunderstanding.
The chairman CP Radhakrishnan said, “Members, certain instances have come to my notice regarding discourteous and undignified comments being made by members interrupting the speech of other members in the House. I would advise that Hon'ble members should be careful not to hurt the sentiments and feelings of fellow members. Our culture is unique and inclusive of diverse regional cultures. There should be no disrespect to the cultural traditions and regional identities of our colleagues.”
He further invited the concerned members to his chamber. “If anybody wants to express their feelings, I’m inviting every member to come to my chamber,” Radhakrishnan said.
Union Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju requested the chair to allow Dev to give her response on record. “He is making an allegation against one of the members. The conduct of the House demands that both members should be heard because Hon'ble member John Brittas’s statement has gone on record,” Rijiju said.
The chairman said he would speak to both MPs, while the ruling side insisted that Dev also be given a chance to state her side of the story on record.
Leader of the House JP Nadda said that the government does not subscribe to such statements and respects every state’s attire, further insisting that Dev should be allowed to present her statements.
“Certainly we respect every attire of every state. We don’t call it lungi, it is dhoti and we respect it. We do not subscribe to such statements. But at the same time, what Sushmita Dev has to say should also be on record. Sir, so please allow Sushmita Dev to speak,” he said.
The chairman, however, adjourned the House until 2 pm.

headline: ‘Jantar Mantar Season 2 going to start very soon’: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke's big remark
full_text:
‘Jantar Mantar Season 2 going to start very soon’: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke's big remark
‘Season 1’ points back to the massive student protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar last month which forced Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is getting ready for another round of street action. “Season 2 of Jantar-Mantar” would start very soon, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said on Wednesday.
The reference to ‘Season 1’ points back to the massive student-led agitation at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar last month. The demonstrations over exam paper leaks, student suicides and calls for educational reform turned up enough heat to force Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister. The CJP then announced it would continue as a pressure group to hold democratic institutions accountable.
ALSO READ | CJP Delhi meet cancelled, Abhijeet Dipke says hall owners 'threatened by BJP'
“Many people were commenting on Instagram when Season 2 of 'Jantar-Mantar' will begin. I want to tell them that Season 2 of 'Jantar-Mantar' is going to start very soon,” Dipke said.
CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said Dipke’s “Jantar Mantar Season 2” remark was not limited to another protest at the Delhi venue. “This itself is Season 2," Saurav Das told ANI.
"Protests are taking place across the country against such incompetent governments and officers. On behalf of CJP, we are now embarking on a nationwide 'listening tour' to hear what the public has to say. We will run a campaign, and we are prioritising the issue of education starting from Independence Day,” he added.
Spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka wrote on X, “Jantar Mantar Season 2 starting soon!”
Dipke's ‘pressure from above’ claim
Dipke on Wednesday alleged that the party struggled to find a venue for its volunteers’ meet in Delhi. He claimed several hall owners refused to rent space because of “pressure from above” and blamed the BJP.
“We were scheduled to hold our volunteers' meet in Delhi today. We were looking for a hall, but no one would rent us one. Everyone kept saying there was pressure from above," Dipke told reporters.
He said the party eventually managed to secure a hall after considerable difficulty and had a receipt to prove the booking. The venue owners were threatened, though, on the morning of the meeting, he said.
ALSO READ | ‘CJP will work as pressure group to hold democratic institutions accountable’: Abhijeet Dipke
“We had managed to secure this hall with great difficulty. We even have the receipt for it. However, the owners received threats this morning. They were told that if they allowed the CJP meeting to take place here, they would be hung upside down.”
Dipke blamed the BJP for the alleged pressure and said the incident showed that the party was uneasy about the growing youth movement.
“All of this is being done by the BJP. Their actions and words clearly reveal that they are afraid of the country's youth. If they think such petty actions will frighten us, they are sorely mistaken.”
The allegations could not be independently verified by HT.
CJP zeroes in on government schools
Dipke made these remarks as his party, that launched as a satirical digital front, looks beyond the protests that first put them on the map.
On Wednesday, he announced that the party would launch its “School Thik Karo” campaign on Independence Day, August 15, to push for better basic facilities in government schools in villages.
ALSO READ | ‘School Thik Karo’: Dipke announces CJP campaign for Independence Day, says rural kids failed ‘in worst way’
“Kids in villages shouldn’t be pleading for basic facilities at school after 80 years of Independence.”
“As a country, we have failed rural kids in the worst possible way. This Independence Day, CJP will launch the ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign to improve Govt schools in villages,” he said on X.
Saurav Das, on X, said, "The manner in which the governments have ignored our schools is unacceptable. It’s time we FIX them. ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign."
The campaign is expected to begin from Dipke’s village in Hingoli, Maharashtra, with the CJP founder calling on sarpanches, parents and local residents to take up responsibility for improving school infrastructure.
CJP lands support to Gen Alpha protest in UP
Earlier this week, the CJP backed a ‘Gen Alpha’ protest in Uttar Pradesh's Hamirpur. School children marched to the Collectorate and blocked its main gate over a badly damaged road connecting their villages to schools.
CJP's Das praised the children, while Dipke also backed their demand.
ALSO READ | 'Well done': After Gen Z, Alpha get into protest arena in UP; CJP's Dipke, Das give a shoutout
“Salute to these kids who are fighting for their future! All they are asking for is a road to their school. Is that too much to ask after nearly 80 years of Independence? This should have been done decades ago. This 15th August, let’s pledge to work for the children and schools of rural India,” Dipke wrote on X.
CJP has also launched the ‘Kya Bolti Public’ listening campaign to gather public concerns across the country, with education identified as its first priority.

headline: The Rajya Sabha functioned for only about 21 minutes in the pre-lunch session on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) before being adjourned amid an uproar over CPI(M) member John Brittas’ allegation that BJP MP Sushmita Dev had addressed him as ‘lungiwala’ d...
full_text:
The Rajya Sabha functioned for only about 21 minutes in the pre-lunch session on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) before being adjourned amid an uproar over CPI(M) member John Brittas’ allegation that BJP MP Sushmita Dev had addressed him as ‘lungiwala’ during proceedings earlier this week.
After the House was adjourned, Opposition MPs staged a protest at Makar Dwar, the main entrance to Parliament House. Several male MPs wore mundu as a mark of protest and raised slogans celebrating “unity in diversity”.
Also read: Parliament Monsoon session LIVE updates
Soon after listed papers were laid on the table of the House, Mr. Brittas raised the issue, describing it as a matter concerning the dignity of the House and respect for India’s diversity.
‘Heavy heart’
“It is with a heavy heart that I raise this matter. It is a question of the prestige and honour of the House. I am a proud Indian, a proud South Indian and a proud Malayali. Our Constitution celebrates our diversity,” Mr. Brittas said.
He alleged that while he was moving a statutory resolution against the Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, on Monday, Ms. Dev left her allotted seat and repeatedly heckled him, referring to him as “lungiwala”.
The allegation drew support from Opposition members, several of whom attended the proceedings wearing mundu. Treasury Bench members, however, insisted that Ms. Dev should also be given an opportunity to present her version.
‘Don’t hurt sentiments’
Earlier in his ruling, Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan said members should avoid remarks that could hurt the sentiments of fellow parliamentarians.
“Certain instances have come to my notice regarding discourteous and undignified comments being made by members interrupting the speech of other members in the House. I would advise that honourable members should be careful not to hurt the sentiments and feelings of fellow members,” he said.
“Our culture is unique and inclusive of diverse regional cultures. There should be no disrespect to the cultural traditions and regional identities of our colleagues,” the chairman added.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said that since Mr. Brittas had made allegations against another member, Ms. Dev should also be heard. “That member should also be allowed to make a point,” he said, adding that if anything objectionable had been said, the chairman could call both members and ascertain the facts.
BJP women MPs stood up at their seats to protest against the Opposition’s demand that action be taken against Ms. Dev.
In the afternoon, when the House reconvened at 2 p.m., Deputy Chairman Harivansh invited Ms. Dev to speak. She said she is a Bengali from Assam and has seen different states where people wear different attires and clothes. “Neither I nor any members have cast aspersions on any state’s attire. I wanted to put that on record,” she said adding that if Mr. Brittas feels she needs to approach him and say something, she would be more than happy. “No message from this House should go that any member wants division in India whether culturally or on the basis of religion,” Ms. Dev said.
Leader of the House J.P. Nadda also urged the Chair to allow Ms. Dev to speak. He said the House respected the attire and traditions of every State and that Ms. Dev’s version should be placed on record.
Mr. Nadda added that if both MPs could come to his chamber, the misunderstanding can be resolved.

headline: New Delhi: A ruckus erupted in the Rajya Sabha Wednesday morning after CPI(M) MP John Brittas accused BJP MP Sushmita Dev of making derogatory remarks against him by calling him a ‘lungiwala’.
full_text:
New Delhi: A ruckus erupted in the Rajya Sabha Wednesday morning after CPI(M) MP John Brittas accused BJP MP Sushmita Dev of making derogatory remarks against him by calling him a ‘lungiwala’.
The BJP MP’s alleged remarks led the CPM to hit back, terming it an insult to South Indians. Brittas did not mention Dev’s name inside the House but referred to her while interacting with the media.
Brittas, who represents Kerala in the Rajya Sabha, said he has moved a privilege motion against Sushmita Dev.
The alleged incident took place on 10 August during a discussion in Rajya Sabha on the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
The issue was raised in the Rajya Sabha and the chairman maintained that there should be no disrespect. The Rajya Sabha was adjourned until 2 pm amid uproar over Sushmita Dev’s alleged disparaging remarks against Brittas.
“Sir, it is with a heavy heart that I raise this matter because it’s a question of the garima (dignity) of this house, its prestige and honour. And it’s a bipartisan issue. Let me just tell at the outset I’m a proud Indian, South Indian and of course a proud Malayali, sir. I cherish every moment being a Malayali, our language, culture, cuisine and of course our Constitution celebrates our diversity,” Brittas said in the Rajya Sabha.
“Sir, if you ask me when I’m leaving this house, which can happen very soon, what is the takeaway from this house? I would certainly say that the biggest takeaway would be this sterling diversity which holds the unity of this nation in a unique way. That would be my takeaway. Sir, the other day, an honourable member who I hold in high esteem, let me just say, that member came here and was disturbing me when I was fulfilling my obligation as a mover of a statute of resolution… Verbal debate is fine, we debate with each other… She repeatedly called me lungiwala, lungiwala,” he added.
Brittas told the media he has served a privilege notice against Sushmita Dev. “The other day, while I was speaking in the House, she made a derogatory remark—lungiwala—against me. I was wearing a dhoti, and I am proud to be a Malayali, proud to be a South Indian. And these are all part of our culture. But such stereotypes are made in a derogatory manner, which is not acceptable,” he told the media.
“And I feel that the House should take a view on this that we have moved a privileged notice against her. I have nothing against her, of course,” he added.
However, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju while speaking in the Rajya Sabha said he had not heard what Brittas was alluding to.
“Sir, in this August House, every honourable member is equal, we are all equal Indians. Yes sir, if there is anything which is objectionable or which is unbecoming of the character of the nation or the dignity of the house, I would like to request the honourable chairman to call the member to your chamber and listen to what happened. Because, I am not witness to whatever honourable member is saying,” said Rijiju.
Referring to Sushmita Dev’s comment, Brittas told the media: “It is shorthand for othering… The remarks she made are unbecoming of a Member of Parliament, and I believe the Hon’ble Chairman and the Committee of Privileges will take note of this.”
The chairman in his ruling maintained that all members should be careful not to hurt the sentiments and feelings of fellow members.
“Honourable members, certain incidents have come to my notice regarding discourteous and undignified comments being made by members interrupting the speech of other members in the house. Our culture is unique. I would advise the honourable members to be careful not to hurt the sentiments and the feelings of fellow members,” the chairman said.
Reacting to the controversy, Congress MP Christopher Tilak backed Brittas, saying: “It was an insult by the BJP to South Indian culture. It is not just about the attire. Yesterday, one of the senior Members of Parliament from the Rajya Sabha, John Brittas, was presenting his question when a member from West Bengal insultingly called him ‘lungiwala, lungiwala.’ This is very unfortunate in a nation with so much diversity. This clearly shows the BJP’s attitude towards the non-Hindi-speaking belt.”

A political storm erupted in Tamil Nadu on Tuesday after senior AIADMK leader and former minister RB Udhayakumar took an alleged jibe at the state government with a reference to popular actress Trisha Krishnan.
Members of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s local unit in Thoothukudi on Tuesday filed a complaint against Udhayakumar over the remarks , officials said.

What the remarks are
The alleged comments surfaced in a video, in which Udhayakumar is purportedly heard questioning an alleged trend of film industry members who previously worked with or were associated with CM C Vijay Joseph bagging senior administrative roles.
The clip, which HT has seen, was uploaded on Monday. “...Now government appointments are turning into a major controversy as producers and technical artists who worked with our CM (C Joseph) Vijay films are currently quietly appointed in government positions,” he is heard saying.
“Annai (Mother) Tamil Nadu is now waiting in shock and anticipation to see when an announcement will be made appointing our chief minister’s beloved Trisha as the deputy chief minister of Tamil Nadu” he purportedly added.
Krishnan’s fan clubs in Madurai pasted posters criticising the comments. “Women are the eyes of our Nation. We strongly condemn the comments of the former minister,” it said.

headline: CJP's Saurav Das alleges police intimidated family after visit to Puducherry home
full_text:
CJP's Saurav Das alleges police intimidated family after visit to Puducherry home
Saurav Das alleged on X that Puducherry police questioned his family to intimidate them, while police denied harassment and said residents near important routes are routinely questioned for security.
CJP spokesperson Saurav Das on Wednesday alleged that police in Puducherry intimidated his family during a visit to their home, a charge the force denied. A senior police official said officers had gone to the house of Das's relatives as part of a 'routine exercise' ahead of Independence Day.
Das said in posts on X that his family was subjected to questioning and accused the BJP government in Puducherry of trying to intimidate them. Police rejected the allegation of harassment and said residents living near important routes are routinely visited and asked a few questions for security reasons.
While confirming that police had visited the home of Das's relatives, the senior official said such visits are carried out ahead of important days like Independence Day. People living in the vicinity of important routes are visited and asked a few questions for security purposes, the official said, rejecting allegations of harassment and intimidation.
Das said, "Two hours ago, the Pondicherry police showed up at my family's home and subjected them to all kinds of questioning".
He also wrote, "Why this harassment, Puducherry Police? Who ordered this and for what purpose? Is this the legal procedure? Why is the BJP government in Pondicherry intimidating my family? This is not the character of the Pondy government. This is being done at the behest of the Union government," Das alleged.
He further said, "If the intention is to intimidate me into silence, it will not work. This will not cower me down. It only strengthens our resolve to build a better system, one where the police uphold the law instead of acting like goondas".
In another post, Das said Union Minister Amit Shah was in Puducherry two days ago, where he met the Home Minister of the Union Territory and the Lieutenant Governor. "Was this intimidation tactic planned at their meeting?" he asked.
The exchange followed Das's allegation that his family was intimidated during a police visit to their Puducherry home, while police maintained that the visit to his relatives' house was a standard security measure ahead of Independence Day and not an act of harassment.

headline: Jantar Mantar Season 2 to begin soon: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke hints at fresh protest
full_text:
Jantar Mantar Season 2 to begin soon: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke hints at fresh protest
The CJP, which recently ended its 36-day Jantar Mantar protest over the NEET paper leak issue, said it will now launch a nationwide "listening tour" focused on education and public grievances.
The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on Wednesday announced that it would soon launch a fresh protest, with founder Abhijeet Dipke calling it "Season 2 of Jantar Mantar". The announcement came after a CJP volunteers' meeting in Delhi's Naraina was cancelled at the last minute, with Dipke alleging that the banquet hall owner revoked the booking due to "pressure" from the ruling BJP.
Addressing a public meeting, Dipke said the party had been receiving messages on social media asking when the second phase of its Jantar Mantar protest would begin.
"Many people were commenting on Instagram about when Season 2 of 'Jantar-Mantar' will begin. I want to tell them that Season 2 of 'Jantar-Mantar' is going to start very soon," he said.
CJP ALLEGES PRESSURE ON VENUE OWNERS
Dipke said the party had booked a hall for its volunteers' meeting but was denied access when organisers reached the venue. He claimed the organisers were told that there was "pressure" on the owners to not allow the meeting. "We were scheduled to hold our volunteers' meeting in Delhi today. We were looking for a hall, but no one would rent us one. Everyone kept saying there was pressure from above," Dipke said.
He alleged that the CJP faced similar refusals from other venues in the area and claimed people were being intimidated against providing space for party meetings.
Dipke further alleged that the venue eventually secured for the meeting came under pressure on the morning of the event, with its owners allegedly threatened with consequences if they allowed the CJP gathering. "They were told that if they allowed the CJP meeting to take place here, they would be hung upside down," he alleged.
'THEY ARE AFRAID OF COUNTRY'S YOUTH'
The CJP founder blamed the BJP for the alleged pressure and said such actions would not deter the party from continuing its activities.
"All of this is being done by the BJP. Their actions and words clearly reveal that they are afraid of the country's youth. If they think such petty actions will frighten us, they are sorely mistaken," Dipke said. "As much as you threaten, we are not going to be scared," he added.
The BJP has not immediately responded to the allegations.
CJP PLANS NATIONWIDE 'LISTENING TOUR'
CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the party's next phase of mobilisation had already begun and would include a nationwide campaign to gather public feedback.
"On behalf of CJP, we are now embarking on a nationwide 'listening tour' to hear what the public has to say. We will run a campaign, and we are prioritising the issue of education starting from Independence Day," Das said.
He added, "This itself is Season Two. Protests are taking place across the country against such incompetent governments and officers."
CJP'S 36-DAY JANTAR MANTAR PROTEST
The CJP had led a 36-day protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak issue. The agitation drew students, young volunteers and opposition leaders from across the country. Activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the protest on June 28 and began an indefinite hunger strike before being shifted to Safdarjung Hospital after his health deteriorated.
The protest also witnessed police action on July 20 when demonstrators attempted to march towards Parliament. The agitation was called off on July 25 following talks with the government and assurances on the protesters' key demands. The CJP subsequently announced its national team, with Dipke named its national convener, as it moved towards building a broader organisational structure.

headline: Chennai: The Union govt on Wednesday informed Lok Sabha that security assessments are conducted periodically at all nuclear power plant sites by the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) and âexternal govt agencies.âIn a written reply to Congress MP ...
full_text:
Chennai: The Union govt on Wednesday informed Lok Sabha that security assessments are conducted periodically at all nuclear power plant sites by the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) and âexternal govt agencies.âIn a written reply to Congress MP Manickam Tagore, minister of state in the Prime Ministerâs Office Jitendra Singh said the plants also conduct internal security assessments. âThe observations made are reviewed, monitored and necessary upgrades are carried out for compliance,â he said.Tagore had sought details of third-party security audits at nuclear plants, including Kudankulam, and measures to counter threats from drones, cyberattacks and sabotage. He asked whether any foreign or suspected state-sponsored cyberattack attempts had been detected during the past three years.The National Alliance of Anti-nuclear Movements urged the Union govt recently to constitute a commission of inquiry to investigate the alleged leak of files related to the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant. The statement comes in the wake of a ransomware group reportedly publishing hundreds of files linked to the Kudankulam plant which are said to be highly sensitive.
The govt did not directly disclose whether any such foreign or state-sponsored attempts had been detected. It said cybersecurity at nuclear installations was accorded the âhighest priorityâ, with continuous monitoring and surveillance mechanisms in place. Preventive measures include access controls, regular security audits, vulnerability assessments, incident-response mechanisms and capacity-building programmes. It cited CERT-inâs (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) role in issuing alerts and advisories, coordinating responses to cyber incidents and operating the National Cyber Coordination Centre.On physical security, Singh said nuclear power plants were equipped with perimeter intrusion-detection systems, access controls, CCTV surveillance and X-ray baggage inspection facilities. The AERB conducts regulatory inspections covering nuclear security.Singh said regulatory-approved emergency preparedness plans were in place at every nuclear power plant, including Kudankulam. Exercises involving local administration, security agencies and plant authorities are conducted periodically, and feedback is used to revise and strengthen preparedness plans.
Tabletop, Integrated Command, Control and Response (ICCR) exercises are held once every two years. Mock exercises are organised according to the National Disaster Management Authorityâs schedule. An ICCR exercise was conducted at the Kudankulam nuclear power plant on April 15, 2025.The govt said all other nuclear power plant sites had conducted their latest ICCR exercises since Sept 2024. At Kalpakkam, an off-site emergency exercise involving the district administration, was conducted on July 17, 2026, with an initiating event from the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor.

headline: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday met with the Governor to recommend a 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on humanitarian grounds, citing the deteriorating health of the prisoner's mother.
full_text:
Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday met with the Governor to recommend a 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on humanitarian grounds, citing the deteriorating health of the prisoner's mother.
Jagtar Singh Hawara is currently serving a life sentence for his involvement in the 1995 assassination of the then Punjab chief minister Beant Singh.
Speaking to the media after the meeting, the chief minister stated that the recommendation was made to allow Hawara to meet his mother, who has not seen him in over three decades.
"A recommendation was made recently regarding the matter of granting parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara so that, on humanitarian grounds, he could be given parole as his mother's health is not well. His mother has a desire to meet him after 31 years," CM Mann said.
The chief minister explained that since the case is being heard in the Union Territory, the Governor's role is pivotal in forwarding the request to the Central Government.
"I met the Governor today because as the case is being heard in the UT, the Governor will have an important role and the matter will be sent to the Centre. The final decision rests with the Centre, but we have requested a 10-day parole," he added.
Addressing potential concerns regarding security and public order, CM Mann informed that he has provided a formal assurance to the administration.
"In this regard, we have assured the Governor that we will not allow the atmosphere to be spoiled in any way and the situation will remain under control," the CM asserted.
According to the chief minister, the Governor has responded positively to the request and promised to expedite the administrative formalities.
"The Governor has assured that he will speak with the Home Secretary of the Government of India today itself to complete the formalities, and Hawara will receive relief soon. The Punjab government will send whatever necessary documents are required from their side," Mann stated.
Earlier on August 9, CM Mann wrote to Governor Gulab Chand Kataria regarding the same.
"It has been brought to my notice that Mr Jagtar Singh Hawara's mother is not in good health due to age-related health problems. Mr Jagtar Singh Hawara has also filed CRWP No. 3868/2026 in the Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court, Chandigarh, seeking direction to release him on parole. The Hon'ble Court has also directed to consider his parole application. Therefore, on the basis of human compassion, I would like to request you to grant 10-day parole as soon as possible," the letter read.

headline: Karnataka cabinet portfolion allocation: CM Shivakumar keeps finance, law; Zameer gets housing | Check full list
full_text:
Karnataka cabinet portfolion allocation: CM Shivakumar keeps finance, law; Zameer gets housing | Check full list
Ramalinga Reddy was allotted the Forest, Ecology and Environment portfolio, while Lakshman Savadi was assigned Co-operation, excluding Agriculture Marketing.
Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Wednesday allocated portfolios to his council of ministers, finalising his team after days of suspense after the recent cabinet expansion.
Shivakumar, who was sworn in as the chief minister along with 13 ministers on June 3, inducted 19 more ministers on August 3.
Wednesday’s announcement came a day after the Congress central leadership held a meeting in Delhi chaired by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge to finalise the portfolio allocations for the newly inducted ministers in the state government.
The sanctioned strength of Karnataka’s council of ministers is 34, including the CM. After the expansion, the cabinet now has one vacant berth.
According to the order issued by governor Thaawarchand Gehlot’s office, Shivakumar will retain finance, cabinet affairs, personnel and administrative reforms, intelligence, information, law, justice and human rights, parliamentary affairs and legislation, and agriculture marketing. He will also hold control over the commissionerate of Town and Country Planning and all urban local bodies falling under the Bengaluru Development Authority and Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority areas.
B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan has been given housing, while Ramalinga Reddy will handle forest, ecology and environment. Lakshman Savadi has been assigned co-operation, excluding agricultural marketing.
Rudrappa Manappa Lamani will take charge of sugar and textiles.
K.H. Muniyappa, who was earlier named the food and civil supplies minister and was looking for a change, will handle the social welfare department. Muniyappa, who belongs to the Dalit Left community, had been insisting on the social welfare department, a portfolio that has traditionally seen competing claims from the Dalit Left and Dalit Right groups.
Rizwan Arshad has been assigned food and civil supplies and consumer affairs.
Shivaraj Tangadagi has been given backward classes welfare, Kannada and culture.
U.T. Khader will oversee minority welfare, haj and wakf, health and family welfare. T. Raghumurthy has been assigned scheduled tribe welfare, while Ajay Singh will handle minor irrigation and science and technology.
Cheluvarayaswamy will take charge of major and medium irrigation. Madhu Bangarappa has been assigned primary and secondary education, while Basavaraj Raya Reddy will handle higher education.
Shivalinge Gowda has been given excise, which has been transferred out of the finance department. Puttaranga Shetty will oversee animal husbandry and sericulture departments, while Vijayanand Kashappanavar has been assigned small-scale industries and public enterprises.
Santosh Lad will handle labour and employment. KS Basavanthappa has been given muzrai, fisheries, ports and inland water, while S.S. Mallikarjun will oversee the mines, geology and horticulture departments.
Narendra Swamy will handle agriculture, HC Balakrishna municipal administration and B Nagendra, the minister of planning and statistics.

headline: President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi will resolve the issue arising out of the threat of U.S. tariffs on India’s purchase of Russian oil, a senior White House adviser said on Tuesday.
full_text:
President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi will resolve the issue arising out of the threat of U.S. tariffs on India’s purchase of Russian oil, a senior White House adviser said on Tuesday.
The remarks by White House Trade Adviser Peter Navarro came days after the U.S. Senate passed a Bill authorising the U.S. President to impose 100% tariffs on the top five purchasers of Russian oil, contending that such business directly financed the Ukraine war.
Mr. Navarro said India was not involved in the oil trade with Russia before the Ukraine war broke out in 2022, but got involved later.
“Prior to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, India was not involved in the oil trade with Russia, but afterwards it got heavily involved and was selling a lot of refined products on behalf of Russia, which helped feed the war machine,” Mr. Navarro told reporters at the White House.
The U.S. official said the issue had since been resolved and claimed credit for weaning India off the oil trade with Russia.
“Maybe, I had a little bit to do with that with that op-ed,” Mr. Navarro said, referring to the article he had penned in The Financial Times recently.
“The President and your Prime Minister have a very good working relationship. They are going to work that out amongst themselves, and it is not for me to get between,” Mr. Navarro said.

Deepti Gaur Mukherjee is a 1993-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Madhya Pradesh cadre.
Senior bureaucrat Deepti Gaur Mukherjee on Wednesday officially took charge as the secretary of the department of higher education under the education ministry.
Mukherjee, a 1993-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Madhya Pradesh cadre, moves into the position after serving as secretary in the ministry of corporate affairs.
What the role entails
The department of higher education looks after the government’s policies and programmes related to universities, colleges and other higher education institutions.

It oversees areas such as funding, quality and access to higher education, student and teacher-related issues, research and major education reforms, while also coordinating with bodies such as the UGC and centrally funded institutions.
As secretary, Mukherjee will be the department’s top bureaucrat and will oversee the implementation of these policies and programmes.

Mukerjee has held several senior administrative positions during her career, including important assignments in Madhya Pradesh. Her work in the state included senior roles in the school education department and the state education mission.

headline: China says border situation with India 'generally stable' amid Arunachal tensions
full_text:
China says border situation with India 'generally stable' amid Arunachal tensions
This came after India's external affairs ministry said that the state of border affairs has ramifications for overall India-China ties.
China on Wednesday sought to play down reports of a military standoff with India in the Arunachal Pradesh sector of the Line of Actual Control (LAC), with a foreign ministry spokesperson saying the “border situation is generally stable”.
The comments by Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun came a day after the external affairs ministry said that the state of border affairs has ramifications for overall India-China ties, and that the two sides have agreed to use diplomatic and military mechanisms to “avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation” along the border.
The Indian side has officially offered no clarity on the current status of the standoff in Arunachal Pradesh sector, though people familiar with the situation said on condition of anonymity that problems first emerged in the remote Taksing area of Upper Subansiri district in early July and there had been several face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops.
Deep Dive
“The China-India border situation is generally stable at the moment. China and India held the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on China-India Border Affairs (WMCC) last week,” Guo told a media briefing without going into details.
Guo, who was responding to questions on videos on Indian social media claiming stepped-up Chinese military activity in Arunachal Pradesh, did not deny the reported standoff in the region.
The questions also referred to a recent military incident with India and increased Chinese military activity near Arunachal Pradesh.
Guo said India and China have “agreed to maintain communication via diplomatic and military channels and jointly uphold peace and tranquillity in the border areas”.
These remarks echoed comments by external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal at a media briefing in New Delhi on Tuesday.

India says Bangladesh's request to extradite Sheikh Hasina is being examined
India said it is examining Bangladesh's request to extradite former prime minister Sheikh Hasina. She, 78, has been living in India since fleeing Dhaka after the collapse of her government in August 2024 amid a massive anti-government agitation.
India on Tuesday said it is examining the Bangladesh government's request for the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina in line with established procedures. The response came a day after Dhaka renewed its call for Hasina's extradition during a meeting between Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi and Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Hasina, 78, has been living in India since fleeing Dhaka after the collapse of her government in August 2024 amid a massive anti-government agitation. Bangladesh has been seeking her return in connection with cases linked to the crackdown on student-led protests in 2024.
At his bi-weekly media briefing, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, "We have made it very clear that this issue is being examined in line with established processes on the Indian side. We will give you an update when there is one."
The previous government led by Muhammad Yunus had also asked India to extradite Hasina, arguing that she was convicted of "crimes against humanity" for the brutal crackdown on the student-led protests. Hasina and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal were handed the death penalty by the International Crimes Tribunal, a domestic war crimes court, last year after being convicted of crimes against humanity during the crackdown on the anti-government protests in 2024.
Replying to another question, Jaiswal said two separate invitations had been extended to Prime Minister Rahman to visit India — one for a bilateral trip and another to attend the outreach session of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi in September. India is hosting the annual BRICS Summit on September 12 and 13, and the meeting is expected to deliberate extensively on several pressing global challenges, including the economic consequences of the West Asia crisis.
New Delhi invited Rahman to the outreach session of the BRICS Summit in his capacity as the current chair of BIMSTEC. The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation comprises India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan.
On Bangladesh's request for the handing over of two Bangladeshi nationals arrested in West Bengal earlier this year on suspicion of involvement in the killing of Bangladeshi political leader Sharif Osman Hadi, Jaiswal said, "This is a legal matter, in which investigations are ongoing." Overall, India said Hasina's extradition request is under process, while also confirming that invitations have been sent to Rahman for a bilateral visit and the BRICS outreach session.

headline: Cash row: Justice Yashwant Varma inquiry report to be tabled in Parliament today
full_text:
Cash row: Justice Yashwant Varma inquiry report to be tabled in Parliament today
The enquiry report into allegations against former judge Justice Yashwant Varma will be tabled in both Houses of Parliament on Wednesday. The move sharpens the constitutional question of whether removal proceedings can continue after his resignation.
The enquiry report into allegations against former Allahabad High Court judge Justice Yashwant Varma will be tabled in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, bringing a controversial case involving the alleged discovery of burnt currency at his official residence to a crucial stage.
The three-member enquiry committee, constituted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, investigated allegations against Justice Varma following the discovery of burnt currency notes at his official residence in Delhi in March 2025.
Following the incident, Justice Varma was transferred from the Delhi High Court to the Allahabad High Court, and his judicial work was withdrawn pending an in-house enquiry. He resigned from the Allahabad High Court on April 9, 2026, while the parliamentary inquiry was underway.
The resignation has raised a key legal and constitutional question over whether Parliament can continue with removal proceedings against a judge who has resigned while the process is pending.
The parliamentary inquiry committee submitted its report to Speaker Om Birla on May 18. The committee was reconstituted in February and comprises Supreme Court Justice Aravind Kumar, Bombay High Court Chief Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and senior advocate B V Acharya.
The proceedings originated after a removal motion signed by 146 MPs was submitted to the Lok Sabha Speaker in July 2025.
WHAT IS THE ALLEGATION AGAINST JUSTICE VARMA?
The controversy dates back to March 2025, when a fire broke out at Justice Varma's official residence in Delhi. During firefighting operations, burnt currency notes were allegedly found at the site.
Justice Varma has denied the allegations and maintained that no cash was recovered from his residence. He was not present at the residence when the fire broke out and subsequently questioned the basis for holding him responsible for what happened at the premises.
Following the incident, then Chief Justice of India Sanjiv Khanna ordered an in-house inquiry. The panel reportedly found prima facie that Justice Varma and his family had control over the room where the cash was allegedly found.
PARLIAMENTARY ENQUIRY
In August 2025, Speaker Om Birla constituted a three-member committee under the Judges (Inquiry) Act to examine the allegations. Justice Varma later challenged the validity of the parliamentary inquiry before the Supreme Court. The proceedings were ultimately allowed to continue.
The committee completed its proceedings after Justice Varma resigned on April 9 and subsequently submitted its report to the Speaker on May 18.
The report will now be placed before Parliament. Its findings could determine what further parliamentary action is considered in the case.
CAN PARLIAMENT REMOVE A JUDGE AFTER RESIGNATION?
This is the central constitutional question surrounding the case.
Under Articles 124 and 217 of the Constitution, a High Court judge can be removed on grounds of "proved misbehaviour" or "incapacity". The removal process requires an address by each House of Parliament supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by at least two-thirds of members present and voting, followed by an order of the President.
Justice Varma's resignation, however, has created an unusual situation because the parliamentary removal process was already underway when he stepped down.

headline: New Delhi: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee on Wednesday, amid the Opposition demanding that the Bill be withdrawn entirely.
full_text:
New Delhi: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee on Wednesday, amid the Opposition demanding that the Bill be withdrawn entirely.
The resolution, introduced by MoS Home Affairs Nityanand Rai, said that the Bill would be referred to a Joint Committee of the Houses consisting of 21 Members of the Lok Sabha to be nominated by the Speaker, and 10 Members of the Rajya Sabha to be nominated by Chairman, Rajya Sabha. It said that to constitute a sitting of the Joint Committee, the quorum shall be, as near as may be, one-third of the total number of Members of the Joint Committee.
This Committee would submit a report to the Lok Sabha by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session 2026.
In response, Congress MP KC Venugopal asked for withdrawal of the bill, saying, “This legislation is clearly for targeting NGOs and minority institutions, those that are doing good work. On one side, the RSS is getting complete donations from foreign countries, on the other side the Government is trying to target the minorities and NGOs.”
In response, Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju said that the Opposition has been demanding that the Bill be referred to a Parliamentary Committee.
“If KC Venugopal ji or any other member has any objections with the Bill, they can raise it with the JPC. The JPC will get enough time and more people can be heard…I thought they would welcome this…Instead of welcoming this, they are opposing it. This isn’t to target any minority community. This is for the security of the entire country,” he said.
Samajwadi Party MP Akhilesh Yadav also spoke against the reference of the Bill to the JPC, saying, “All of us in Opposition are against the FCRA. The Minister is saying that this Bill isn’t against the Minority. He should answer which Bill they have brought which isn’t against the Minority?” he asked.
In response, Rijiju shot back, challenging Yadav to point out any provision that is against any minority.
“Lies are being spread in the country…Do you want foreign funds to come into India without any law and be spent here. This country is not a banana republic. There should be rules and regulations as per the spirit of the Constitution. There is not a single provision in the proposed FCRA to target minority institutions. There is a campaign to mislead certain communities. I take full responsibility to ensure that not a single provision is against any minority community. This is for the well being and security of every community in India,” Rijiju asserted.
The resolution was then passed amid sloganeering and ruckus.
(Edited by Nivedita Patil)
