headline: Examining implications for national security: MEA on Pak-Saudi-Turkey defence pact
full_text:
Examining implications for national security: MEA on Pak-Saudi-Turkey defence pact
India said it is assessing the implications of the new defence pact among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The ministry said the review will focus on national security, regional stability and wider developments in West Asia.
The Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday said India is assessing the implications of a new defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, including its potential impact on New Delhi's national security and regional stability.
The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7 after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan held talks.
External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India was closely examining the agreement.
"As far as this agreement is concerned, we are examining its implications both from the perspective of India's national security and considerations of regional peace and stability," Jaiswal said at his bi-weekly media briefing.
"India remains fully committed to safeguarding its national interests and will take all necessary measures in this regard," he added.
PACT PLEDGES COLLECTIVE DEFENCE
A joint statement issued by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey said the agreement was based on shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation among the three countries.
"The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all," the statement said.
"It further provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation among the three states," it added.
India said its assessment would focus both on the direct security implications and the wider impact on peace and stability in the region. Jaiswal also said New Delhi continued to closely monitor developments linked to the conflict in West Asia.
"India continues to closely follow all developments in the West Asia conflict," he said.
INDIA SLAMS PAKISTAN OVER POK
He also addressed questions about events held in different parts of the world to mark the "independence" of Pakistan's Balochistan province. He also referred to violent protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK).
"We continue to follow developments across the world. At the same time, I would like to highlight that we have seen the kind of human rights violations that were committed in POK and other parts of that country," Jaiswal said.
"We call on the international community to hold Pakistan accountable for its misdeeds, abuses and flagrant violation of human rights, including of all its people," he added.
Jaiswal said large-scale protests in POK had resulted in a situation where "public discontent was answered with bullets, blackouts, repression and oppression".
He also reiterated India's position on Pakistan and cross-border terrorism.
"We are where we were earlier. I need not emphasise which country is responsible for cross-border terrorism and which is the epicentre of terrorism, and where the action lies for stopping cross-border terrorism," he said.

headline: 7,000 tonnes of garbage: Haridwar readies for 'mega clean-up' after Kanwariyas depart
full_text:
7,000 tonnes of garbage: Haridwar readies for 'mega clean-up' after Kanwariyas depart
Experts have called for quick disposal of garbage as spectre of worsening pollution, disease looms over Haridwar, a popular pilgrimage for millions
The holy city of Haridwar is scrambling to dispose of over 7000 tonnes of garbage generated during the two-week ‘Kanwar Yatra’ when nearly 48 million pilgrims descended on it, the highest number on record.
Experts have called for quick disposal of the garbage as the spectre of worsening pollution and disease looms over Haridwar, a popular pilgrimage for millions through the year.
Heaps of garbage comprising plastic, clothes, ‘Kanwars,’ and non-degradable polythene waste remain strewn across the city, municipal officials said on Wednesday. The areas worst affected by the unregulated dumping of waste are the numerous ‘ghats’ on the Ganga river, markets where pilgrims stopped to rest and eat, access roads winding into the city from the national highways and the designated parking areas for vehicles that formed part of the processions.
Also Read | Record 48 million Kanwariyas visit Haridwar in 2026 Kanwar fair: Officials
Hundreds of workers have been deployed to clean the mess since the last pilgrims left the city, leaving a thick trail of garbage behind. It will take days for the waste to collected, transported to garbage collection centres and disposed.
“…approximately 7000 tonnes of garbage was generated during the two weeks of Kanwar yatra. It is being cleared since Tuesday evening, as Kanwariyas started leaving the city for their respective destinations after the Shravan Shivratri Ganga Aarti. Sanitation workers have been deployed in groups around Har-ki-Pauri and the Mela,” Nandan Kumar, municipal corporation town commissioner, said.
Also Read | 5 days on, Kanwar rush, heavy rain, traffic brings Delhi to standstill
“Waste collection and disposal is also being carried out in city markets, lanes, roads and parking lots on a war footing,” Kumar added,
Officials said discarded clothes left behind by the Kanwariyas alone amounted to several metric tonnes and would be recycled.
Haridwar will need a “mega cleanliness” drive
The Haridwar district administration has launched a mega cleanliness drive from August 12 to 18 to restore cleanliness in the district to pre-Kanwar fair levels.
“Heaps of garbage and waste are lying at Ganga ghats, in the Kanwar Mela zone, along the Kanwar patri and throughout the pedestrian routes used by Kanwariyas to travel, rest and camp, as well as at vehicle parking areas,” Lalit Narayan Mishra, chief development officer, said.
“While civic agencies are already involved in the clearance, it is vital that local residents, the saint community, religious organisations, educational institutions, volunteers and traders also participate,” Mishra said.
Mishra further said municipal corporations, local authorities including district and village panchayats were working round the clock on waste collection and disposal. The work is being monitored on site and online by senior officials to ensure time-bound clearance of waste, he said.
Also Read | Kanwariyas form human chain to let Muslim man's funeral procession cross highway
Sanitation worker deployment
Civic authorities have deployed over 1000 sanitation personnel and 100 outsourced workers for the drive, along with 80 garbage collection, transportation and disposal vehicles.
The city’s seer community has extended support to the district administration’s initiative to involve stakeholders and local residents in the post-Kanwar cleanliness drive.
The Akhil Bharatiya Akhara Parishad, the apex body of recognised akhadas, has informed the district administration that monks and office-bearers of various akhadas would participate in the cleanliness drive.
“Kanwar pilgrimage is an ancient tradition and in recent years the number of Kanwariyas has crossed the four-crore mark, so waste generation is bound to increase manifold. We fully support the administration’s initiative to seek voluntary participation from individuals. By participating in this post-Kanwar cleanliness drive, people will also derive spiritual satisfaction as they will indirectly be helping clean Ganga and reduce pollution,” said Akhara Parishad president Mahant Ravindra Puri of Niranjani Akhada.
What environmentalists say
Environmentalists, however, said pollution levels in the Ganga could rise if the waste was not removed in time and rain washed it into the river.
“Such a large floating population of Kanwariyas certainly has a bearing on pollution levels in the Ganga. Bacterial content increases when garbage, sewage, plastic, polythene and human waste enter the river. The risk of microplastics being absorbed also remains a major concern. The use of plastic sheets, bottles and cans and the dumping of clothes and bamboo in the Ganga should either be discouraged or prohibited,” said Gagan Matta, assistant professor, department of environmental science, Gurukula Kangri University.
The saint community also expressed concern over waste, plastic, polythene and used clothes being left at Ganga ghats.
“Kanwariyas, pilgrims, tourists and local people should be sensitised against littering and leaving waste, garbage, polythene bags and clothes at Ganga ghats. We regard Ganga as a deity and mother, but through such acts, knowingly or unknowingly, we pollute the sacred river,” said Mahamandaleshwar Swami Harichetnanand of Bada Udasin Akhada.
Ganga Sabha, which manages the affairs of Brahmakund Har-ki-Pauri, has started a cleanliness drive to ensure pilgrims do not face inconvenience while taking a dip in the Ganga river or during evening “Ganga Aarti” ritual.
“Through public address systems, we have been regularly urging kanwariyas and devotees to maintain cleanliness and ensure that they do not pollute the Ganga. Ganga Sabha ensures that garbage is collected and cleared by civic agencies in time. Our volunteers also clear garbage at Har-ki-Pauri, ensuring that the ghat is clean before the evening Ganga Aarti so devotees can sit on the steps,” said Ganga Sabha teerth purohit Ujjwal Pundit.

headline: Kanwar Yatra ends, 7,000 tonnes of garbage leave Haridwar reeling
full_text:
Kanwar Yatra ends, 7,000 tonnes of garbage leave Haridwar reeling
Around 4.8 crore Kanwar pilgrims visited Haridwar during the festival to collect Ganga water before returning to their destinations, according to civic officials.
Haridwar is carrying out a large-scale cleanup after this year’s Kanwar Yatra generated around 7,000 metric tonnes of waste, including nearly 2,000 metric tonnes in the final two days alone.
Around 4.8 crore Kanwar pilgrims visited Haridwar during the festival to collect Ganga water before returning to their destinations, according to civic officials.
Given the scale of the gathering, the Haridwar Municipal Corporation deployed around 1,000 additional outsourced workers and more than 80 vehicles for sanitation, garbage collection, transportation and waste disposal.
With the annual yatra now over, the civic body has launched a special cleanup drive across major ghats, Kanwar routes, markets and other crowded areas.
7,000 TONNES OF WASTE COLLECTED
Officials said around 7,000 metric tonnes of garbage was collected during the entire Kanwar Yatra.
Nearly 2,000 metric tonnes was collected in the last two days of the event alone.
More than 80 vehicles have been deployed to clear waste from major ghats, Kanwar routes, market areas and other public spaces.
The special post-mela sanitation drive will continue for another two days, with teams focusing on ghats, main roads, the Kanwar track, markets and other heavily used areas.
DRONES USED TO MONITOR CLEANUP
For the first time, the Municipal Corporation also used drones to monitor sanitation during the pilgrimage season.
Drone surveillance was used to track cleanliness along major Kanwar routes, crowded areas and other important locations.
The civic body also deployed sanitation volunteers at major ghats.
As part of efforts to introduce technology into waste management, solar sensor dustbins were also tested during the festival.
‘CLEANUP DOESN’T END WITH YATRA’
Haridwar Municipal Commissioner Nandan Kumar said the scale of the pilgrimage required extensive arrangements for solid waste management.
He said additional workers, vehicles, drone monitoring, green checkpoints, sanitation volunteers and technology-based measures were used to maintain cleanliness during the annual festival.
Kumar said the end of the yatra did not mean the sanitation work was over and that the civic body would continue clearing waste generated during the pilgrimage until Haridwar’s ghats and public spaces were restored.
He also praised municipal officials, sanitation workers, outsourced staff and drivers for working through challenging conditions during the festival.

headline: 90 porn videos found on ex-JDS MP Prajwal Revanna's phone seized from prison cell
full_text:
90 porn videos found on ex-JDS MP Prajwal Revanna's phone seized from prison cell
A fresh FIR has been filed after a phone allegedly used by Prajwal Revanna was seized from his prison cell. The recovery has widened scrutiny of prison security even as his conviction and legal challenges continue.
Former Janata Dal (Secular) MP Prajwal Revanna, currently lodged in Bengaluru’s Parappana Agrahara Central Prison in a rape case, has come under fresh scrutiny after investigators allegedly found dozens of pornographic videos on a mobile phone recovered from his jail cell during a recent search operation, Central Crime Branch (CCB) sources told India Today.
Sources said the phone was seized during a raid conducted inside the prison as part of a drive targeting high-profile inmates.
During the subsequent examination of the device, investigators reportedly found between 80 and 90 downloaded pornographic videos.
Most of the content was allegedly Indian pornographic material. Police sources also said that newspaper clippings featuring women in revealing clothes were stored on the phone.
The recovered phone is now being subjected to detailed forensic analysis. Investigators are examining all video files, images and other digital data stored on the device to determine their origin, date of download and possible relevance to ongoing criminal proceedings involving Revanna.
The seizure has already led to administrative action within the prison. The Assistant Superintendent of the jail has been suspended, while a show-cause notice has been issued to the Superintendent of Bengaluru Central Prison.
Besides the mobile phone, officials recovered a pen drive and a charger from the cell. Authorities said no other prohibited items were found during the four-to-five-hour search operation.
Following the recovery, a fresh FIR has been registered. An undertrial prisoner, identified as Pratap Rai, who was lodged in the same prison, has also been named in the case.
The development comes days after the Karnataka High Court rejected Revanna’s plea seeking suspension of his life sentence and interim bail in the first rape case registered against him in Hassan district.
The High Court observed that the gravity of the offence and the pendency of multiple sexual abuse cases weighed against granting him relief. The court also expressed concern that his release could affect witnesses and pending trials.
REVANNA SENTENCED FOR LIFE
Revanna was convicted in August 2025 by a special court and sentenced to life imprisonment for repeated sexual assault, voyeurism and destruction of evidence.
The case had drawn national attention after explicit videos allegedly involving him surfaced ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Revanna has consistently denied the allegations and has claimed that the videos were morphed.
His legal team has since approached the Supreme Court seeking transfer of one of the cases to another judge, alleging bias, while his appeal against conviction remains pending before the Karnataka High Court.
With the latest recovery from the prison cell, investigators are expected to focus on the source and use of the mobile phone, the digital material found on it and any possible violations of prison rules.
The forensic examination is likely to play a key role in determining the next course of action in the fresh case registered against Revanna.

headline: 4 Domino's outlets sealed in Maharashtra over food safety violations after FDA raids
full_text:
4 Domino's outlets sealed in Maharashtra over food safety violations after FDA raids
The FDA inspected a total of 104 establishments belonging to brands including Domino's Pizza, KFC, Pizza Hut, McDonald's, Subway, Burger King, Starbucks and Monginis. During the drive, operations at two establishments were halted immediately, while 95 improvement notices were issued and five food business licences were suspended with immediate effect.
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the food business licences of four Domino’s Pizza outlets after finding multiple food safety and hygiene violations during a special inspection drive across the state.
Three of the affected Domino’s outlets are located in Mumbai, while the fourth is in Satara district. The inspections were carried out on August 11 as part of a statewide drive targeting establishments operated by major restaurant chains.
The FDA inspected a total of 104 establishments belonging to brands including Domino’s Pizza, KFC, Pizza Hut, McDonald’s, Subway, Burger King, Starbucks and Monginis. During the drive, operations at two establishments were halted immediately, while 95 improvement notices were issued and five food business licences were suspended with immediate effect.
In Mumbai, the licence of the Domino’s outlet operated by Jubilant FoodWorks Ltd at Vile Parle West was suspended after inspectors found violations of Schedule 4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011.
The FDA flagged deficiencies related to the display of the FSSAI licence, potable water testing, food storage, pest control and hygiene facilities. The outlet was also directed to ensure proper temperature storage and monitoring of frozen and other food products.
Inspectors also found issues with the segregation and disposal of food and non-food items. Repairs were required to the kitchen back door, flooring and chilling room, while measures were ordered to prevent the entry of rodents and other pests.
The FDA further directed the outlet to provide adequate facilities for food preparation, equipment sanitisation and hand-washing and hygiene for food handlers.
Another Domino’s outlet in Borivali West was also found non-compliant, with the inspection report assigning it a 54 per cent compliance score. The FDA cited deficiencies involving food storage, temperature monitoring, food testing, hygiene and pest control.
The outlet was directed to maintain proper segregation between raw and cooked food as well as vegetarian and non-vegetarian food. Raw materials and non-food items must also be stored separately.
Inspectors additionally found a need for better cleaning and sanitisation of equipment and utensils, with oily residue and food scraps in the pizza preparation area required to be removed immediately. Improvements were also ordered in flooring, lighting and overall cleanliness, along with effective pest-control measures.
The third Mumbai Domino’s outlet, located at R-City Mall in Ghatkopar West, also had its licence suspended.
According to the FDA, the establishment lacked proper hygiene and sanitation arrangements and did not maintain a cleaning and sanitation schedule. Inspectors also reported pest infestation and inadequate pest-control measures and records.
The Satara outlet, on the other hand, was found to have a compliance score of 47 per cent.
The FDA cited deficiencies in infrastructure, equipment, cleanliness and pest control. The establishment was directed to introduce proper rack and storage systems for raw food items and conduct laboratory testing of food products while maintaining the required records.
The latest action comes a day after the FDA's crackdown on a Blinkit store in Mumbai's Malad West highlighted serious hygiene and food-storage violations.
During an inspection of the quick-commerce company's facility on August 7, FDA officials found a large number of cockroaches on fruit and vegetable stock. Food items were allegedly being stored directly on the floor, while some racks were rusty and cold-storage areas were poorly maintained.
The inspection also found inadequate pest- and rodent-control measures, expired food products and damaged or apparently tampered-with packages. The store was also not properly following FIFO (First In, First Out) and FEFO (First Expiry, First Out) systems for food storage.
Officials further flagged poor waste management and shortcomings in the personal hygiene of food handlers, including inadequate medical examination and health records and insufficient personal protective equipment.
Following the inspection, the FDA suspended the food licence of Blink Commerce Private Limited under Section 32(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The order directed the establishment to keep its food business operations suspended until further instructions.
The Blinkit action was part of a broader food-safety enforcement drive in Maharashtra. Between May 25 and July 31, the FDA inspected 3,137 hotels, restaurants, eateries and other food establishments across Mumbai, issuing 764 improvement notices and suspending 165 licences. The department also seized or destroyed food products weighing 28.66 lakh kg and valued at Rs 55.72 crore, according to FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe.

headline: RSS wing seeks bans, boycott of US firms for tariffs over Russian oil purchase
full_text:
RSS wing seeks bans, boycott of US firms for tariffs over Russian oil purchase
The SJM’s statement came weeks ahead of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s visit to the US and Canada as part of an international outreach
Swadeshi Jagaran Manch (SJM), the economic wing of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)’s ideological fount, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), criticised the US Senate legislation authorising US President Donald Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries making significant purchases of Russian oil and urged the Indian government to stand firm on purchasing it. It asked people to boycott US companies and the government to “impose a unilateral ban” on US tech and social media firms.
India was named as one of five target economies by the bill’s sponsors as the US Senate on Friday approved by 86 votes to 11 the bill. The bill spares US allies in Europe for similar purchases of Russian oil, gas and other exports.
The SJM’s statement came weeks ahead of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s visit to the US and Canada as part of the organisation’s international outreach. “India has time and again made it clear that our sovereign right to purchase energy from legitimate international markets cannot be dictated by any third country…” said SJM national co-convener Ashwani Mahajan in the statement.
Deep Dive
He added that India’s decision to buy crude oil from Russia is based on considerations of energy security, availability, price, diversification of supplies and the interests of Indian consumers. He added that if the US has differences with Russia, it is entitled to pursue its own foreign-policy objectives. “However, those objectives should not be converted into unilateral economic coercion against sovereign countries such as India; and tariffs cannot become an instrument of geopolitical coercion,” he said.
The statement said that while US legislation has yet to complete the full process and that tariffs would not be imposed automatically, it clearly poses a serious threat to the principles of free and fair international trade and to the sovereign right of nations to determine their energy policies.
The SJM, which has campaigned for indigenisation and opposed foreign direct investment in key sectors and strategic disinvestment, pointed out that this is not the first time there have been threats to impose unfair tariffs. It added that such threats have persisted since the beginning of Trump’s second term.
Steep tariffs on Indian goods entering the US will significantly impact exports. India is among the largest buyers of Russian oil, and the quantum of purchase has increased since the Iran-US war.
SJM referred to the previous tariffs and said they have been labelled in various ways, ranging from reciprocal tariffs and national security tariffs to Section 301 tariffs, Section 232 tariffs, punitive tariffs (for purchasing Russian oil), trade deficit tariffs, and forced labour tariffs. It said the list is never-ending. “India has clearly stated that its purchase of crude oil from Russia is based on considerations of energy security, availability, pricing, supply diversification, and the interests of Indian consumers.”
SJM expressed concern over what is described as unethical use of tariffs as an instrument of foreign policy. It labelled the Russia-Ukraine war as nothing but a power tussle between NATO, a bloc of western countries, and the Commonwealth of Independent States, an intergovernmental association formed in 1991 after the dissolution of the USSR. SJM added that Western nations are trying to push Ukraine to join NATO. It said sanctions on oil purchases from Russia are only a pressure tactic being used to give effect to its designs.
SJM called on India to remain uncompromising on the issue of energy security. “India’s energy policy must therefore be determined by India’s national interest, and not by external political pressure.”
“The US India trade negotiations cannot be conducted on gunpoint…The latest US legislation assumes particular significance because India and the United States are simultaneously engaged in negotiations on a bilateral trade agreement. The SJM believes that trade negotiations between two sovereign countries must take place on the basis of mutual respect, reciprocity and equality, and not through threats of punitive tariffs,” Mahajan said.
SJM urged the government to withdraw the notification allowing FDI in e-commerce entities, such as Amazon, Flipkart-Walmart, and to hold inventories for exports. It sought the withholding of the bill passed in the Lok Sabha, permitting banks and other electronic service providers to impose Merchant Discount Rate.
SJM demanded that Visa and Mastercard be forbidden to regain a foothold in India and unequivocally rejected any attempt to use US tariffs to dictate India’s oil purchases.

headline: Trump aide says he got ‘firebombed’ by India over remarks against its Russian oil purchases: ‘Don't do that’
full_text:
Trump aide says he got ‘firebombed’ by India over remarks against its Russian oil purchases: ‘Don't do that’
Navarro has repeatedly criticised India, even calling it the “Maharaja of tariffs,” while defending US tariffs in response to India's purchase of Russian oil.
White House trade adviser Peter Navarro on Tuesday responded to criticism in India over his comments about New Delhi and its trade policies, telling his critics not to attack him as he said such an approach is not how problems are resolved in America.
“I actually got firebombed by the Indian continent on the internet with all sorts of nasty little attacks. And all I would say is, don't do that. That's not how we resolve problems here in America,” he told reporters at the White House.
Notably, Navarro has repeatedly criticised India, even calling it the “Maharaja of tariffs,” while defending US retaliatory tariffs in response to India's purchase of Russian oil.
Trump aide on India's Russian oil purchases
Navarro, who advises US President Donald Trump on trade and manufacturing matters, said India was not involved in the Russian oil trade before the Ukraine war began in 2022. He said India's involvement increased after the war started.
"Prior to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, India was not involved in the oil trade with Russia, but afterwards it got heavily involved and was selling a lot of refined products on behalf of Russia, which helped feed the war machine," he said.
The US official said the issue has now been resolved and claimed that he played a role in reducing India's oil trade with Russia.
"Maybe, I had a little bit to do with that with that op-ed," Navarro said, referring to an article he wrote for The Financial Times.
‘Got firebombed by India’: Navarro
He said he was “firebombed” by India over his comments about the country and its trade policies involving Russia.
The US official also urged his critics to stop making “nasty little attacks”, saying such criticism is not how problems are resolved in America.
Peter Navarro’s tirade against India
Navarro has been a vocal critic of India's trade policies involving Russia and has previously accused the country of helping fund Russia's "war machine" in Ukraine.
In his opinion piece for the Financial Times, he described India's oil trade with Russia as “opportunistic” and “corrosive” to international efforts to isolate the Russian economy.
“As Russia continues to hammer Ukraine, helped by India’s financial support, American (and European) taxpayers are then forced to spend tens of billions more to help Ukraine’s defence. Meanwhile, India keeps slamming the door on American exports through high tariffs and trade barriers. More than 300,000 soldiers and civilians have been killed, while Nato’s eastern flank grows more exposed and the west foots the bill for India’s oil laundering,” wrote Navarro.
A few days later, he stepped up his criticism of India, calling the country a "laundromat for the Kremlin".
He has also referred to the Russia-Ukraine conflict as "Modi's war", claiming that the money Moscow earns through oil sales is used to fund "its war machine" in Ukraine.
India on Navarro’s remarks
In September last year, India dismissed Navarro’s comments about its purchases of Russian oil as “inaccurate and misleading”.
“We have seen the inaccurate and misleading statements made by Mr Navarro and obviously reject them,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.

headline: Youth protests being hijacked: Mayawati urges Gen Z to resist BJP, Congress
full_text:
Youth protests being hijacked: Mayawati urges Gen Z to resist BJP, Congress
BSP chief Mayawati accused the BJP and Congress of trying to take over youth protests in Delhi and Ranchi. She urged students to keep the focus on jobs, reservation and concrete solutions.
BSP supremo Mayawati on Tuesday urged students and Gen Z to stay away from what she described as "conspiracies" by ruling and opposition parties, accusing the BJP and Congress of attempting to hijack youth protests for political and electoral gains.
Addressing select media, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said students and young people across the country were deeply concerned about unemployment and other issues, but alleged that neither the BJP nor the Congress was genuinely committed to resolving their problems.
Mayawati's remarks came a day after BSP national coordinator and her nephew Akash Anand made a strong outreach to Gen Z and young people at a party rally in Hathras.
Referring to student and youth protests in Delhi and Ranchi, Mayawati alleged that political parties had sought to take control of movements that were initially focused on genuine concerns.
She claimed the protest at Jantar Mantar was initially launched by what she called the "Cockroach Janata Party" (CGP), but was later "hijacked" by the Congress and its allies. She made a similar allegation about the ongoing youth movement in Ranchi, claiming it had subsequently been taken over by the BJP and its allies.
"Delhi's Jantar Mantar student and youth movement and now the movement in Ranchi... we are seeing more politics in their garb," Mayawati said.
She alleged that disruptions in Parliament over various issues could either be the result of "internal collusion" between the ruling and opposition parties to divert attention from governance shortcomings or attempts to gain political power.
Mayawati appealed to Gen Z to remain cautious and use their protests to press for solutions rather than allowing political parties to exploit them for electoral purposes.
The BSP chief also attacked the BJP over the reservation system, alleging that quota provisions for Dalits, tribals and other backward classes had been weakened.
"We are not against the private sector, but reservation should be available in the private sector in the same way as it is available in government jobs," she said.
She alleged that public-sector institutions were being weakened while the private sector was being promoted in ways that benefited large industrialists and left poor, unemployed and disadvantaged sections further behind.
Mayawati also claimed that reservation for disadvantaged communities in government employment had become "almost negligible" and alleged that RSS members were working to make the system ineffective.
Defending the record of previous BSP governments in Uttar Pradesh, she claimed that recruitment freezes had been removed and "lakhs and lakhs" of people had been provided livelihood opportunities. She also claimed that new posts were created in the police and other departments.
Mayawati said the inability of governments at the Centre and in states to provide adequate employment opportunities after education and training was fuelling "tremendous anger" among students and young people.
With Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab set to hold assembly elections in the future, Mayawati appealed to students, youth, Dalits, tribals, backward classes, Muslims and other minorities, farmers, labourers, traders and employees to strengthen the BSP.
She described the party as "the only pro-Ambedkarite party" and urged disadvantaged sections to unite behind it and bring the BSP back to power.
Mayawati concluded her address with the slogans "Jai Bhim" and "Jai Bharat".

headline: Bengaluru: When DK Shivakumar faced his first legislature session as the chief minister of Karnataka on Thursday, there was no woman member in his 33-member cabinet. People aware of the development say different factions of the ruling Congress have b...
full_text:
Bengaluru: When DK Shivakumar faced his first legislature session as the chief minister of Karnataka on Thursday, there was no woman member in his 33-member cabinet. People aware of the development say different factions of the ruling Congress have been jostling to push their own candidate for the lone ministerial vacancy.
Shivakumar took over the charge of the state from his party colleague on 3 June, with 13 ministers taking oath alongside him. The cabinet expansion took place on 3 August, when 19 new ministers took oath out of 20 initially cleared. Gayatri Shanthegowda did not take oath. Later, it was said her inclusion in the list was a “typing error”.
Shivakumar has stated that the cabinet berth is reserved for a woman.
Although the All India Congress Committee (AICC) was able to reach a consensus on portfolio allocations for the 19 newly inducted ministers, a decision has not yet been reached on which woman legislator will fill the lone remaining seat in Shivakumar cabinet.
“It will take its own time. Now that the (legislature) session is on, we will take a decision after this,” said a senior Congress leader, requesting anonymity.
The Monsoon Session of the state legislature will continue till 27 August.
The leader added that appointing a woman Cabinet member without holding more deliberations will “create more problems”. Every leader, he said, is “naturally pushing for their own candidates”.
Another member, considered close to the chief minister, said there was “no urgency” in filling up the spot.
One of the reasons for the deadlock, it is learnt, is that Shivakumar, Siddaramaiah and national Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge are each pushing for their own candidate to fill the lone vacant cabinet berth.
Meanwhile, Shivakumar’s two-month-old government has come under sharp criticism over the issue.
Nayana Motamma (46), a first-time Congress legislator and MLA from Mudigere in Chikmagaluru district, said the delay in appointing a woman minister is sending out the wrong message.
“Even though I am a legislator who can be considered as an aspirant, I believe that the issue is bigger than me. From a larger picture about women empowerment, reservation, I think it’s really unfortunate and I hope that they (high command) do something about this as soon as possible. Otherwise, this reflects very badly on the party and the message it is giving out,” she told ThePrint.
Data shows that women significantly backed the Congress in the 2023 assembly elections, and the Congress centered its flagship programmes around them—Gruha Lakshmi (Rs 2,000 per month for woman head of household), Gruha Shakthi (free power), Shakthi (free public bus rides for women), Anna Bhagya (free rice scheme), and Yuva Nidhi (financial assistance to job seekers).
The Congress under Rahul Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi have supported reservation for women in state and national assemblies, as well as policies to empower women.
Also Read: Tirupathi board member opposes Karnataka CM Shivakumar’s proposal to amend ‘Nithya Aarthi’ protocols
‘All-male cabinet’
Siddaramaiah has been pushing for the nomination of Basavaraj Neelappa Shivannanavar for the lone remaining berth in the Cabinet, according to people aware of the development.
“We do not have any (woman) candidate. Our demand was to induct Shivannanavar,” said one person from the Siddaramaiah camp, requesting anonymity.
It is believed that earlier Siddaramaiah backed Shanthegowda, who, like himself and Shivakumar, comes from the Kuruba community.
Congress leaders ThePrint spoke to said if some leaders have their way, it could remain an “all-male cabinet”.
Shivakumar backs former women & child development minister Lakshmi Hebbalkar, while some other candidates have been trying to get the attention of the high-command, and the leaders of the respective warring factions.
Apart from facing criticism over no woman member in the Cabinet, the Shivakumar government is also battling public expression of dissent by several leaders, including M. Krishnappa, Tanveer Sait, H.C.Mahadevappa, M.C.Sudhakar, Narayanswamy and several others.
A.S. Ponnanna, the first-time MLA from Virajpet in Kodagu, was nominated as deputy speaker of the assembly, but was later appointed the political secretary to the chief minister. He has served as legal advisor to Siddaramaiah.
Certain communities have also aired their angst over the Cabinet expansion.
Brahmins, for instance, are protesting their exclusion for the first time in the state’s history. Several other smaller communities remain conspicuously absent when it comes to political representation.
When Siddaramaiah was the chief minister, he doled out nearly 150 cabinet ranks to Congress legislators and others to placate dissenting voices. Shivakumar appears to be following suit.
Veteran Congress leader R.V.Deshpande has been appointed the chairman of the reforms committee. Deshpande has been accorded a cabinet rank, as has Ponnanna.
‘Shrinking space for women in cabinet’
The situation is no different in other political parties and in states.
According to an analysis by Business Standard, only one in 10 ministers across Indian states is a woman, reflecting the stark reality of political parties whose platforms–elections and policy–are centred around women empowerment. Out of 608 ministers in 28 states and three Union Territories, only 30 are women.
In Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 72-member council of ministers, only two of
28 cabinet ministers are women: Nirmala Sitharaman and Annapurna Devi.
Out of the 39 ministers who hold minister of state rank, only five are women.
In most states, women are often allocated the Women and Child Development portfolio, with notable exceptions like Vangalapudi Anitha who holds Andhra Pradesh’s home department while S. Keerthana and Santana Chakma, who hold the industries portfolio in Tamil Nadu and Tripura respectively. Gupta and Kumari head the finance departments of their respective states.
According to Business Standard, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Puducherry and Karnataka have no women representation in the Cabinet.
Even within the Congress in Karnataka, most of the front-runners—Lakshmi Hebbalkar, Nayana Motamma, Kaneez Fathima from Kalaburagi, and Annapurana Tukaram—are dynasts, ThePrint reported earlier.
The party has four women legislators—Umashree, Aarthi Krishna, Bilkis Banu and Gayatri Shanthegowda–in the upper house of the state legislature.
Umashree, who was nominated as the deputy chairperson of the legislative council, has made it clear that she prefers a Cabinet role instead.
(Edited by Ajeet Tiwari)

headline: Seven workers killed, 14 injured after landslide, water seepage in Chamoli tunnel
full_text:
Seven workers killed, 14 injured after landslide, water seepage in Chamoli tunnel
The incident occurred around 7 pm inside a tunnel of the Tehri Hydro Development Corporation (THDC)-owned Vishnugad-Pipalkoti Hydroelectric Project.
Dehradun: Seven workers were killed and 14 others injured after a landslide and heavy water seepage triggered a partial collapse inside an under-construction THDC tunnel at Mayapur near Pipalkoti in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district on Thursday evening.
The incident occurred around 7 pm inside a tunnel of the Tehri Hydro Development Corporation (THDC)-owned Vishnugad-Pipalkoti Hydroelectric Project, where construction work was being carried out by HCC, according to officials.
According to State Emergency Operations Centre (SEOC) officials, 22 workers were trapped inside the tunnel following the sudden landslide and water seepage.
A large-scale multi-agency rescue operation was launched immediately. By 11 pm, 21 workers were evacuated from the tunnel. Seven of them were declared dead, while 14 others were injured and shifted for medical treatment, officials said.
The rescue operation is being undertaken by 57 personnel from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), 42 from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), 21 from the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), 22 from local police stations and outposts, nine fire service personnel and four personnel from the District Disaster Response Force (DDRF).
Senior officials are at the site and supervising the relief and rescue operation. HCC machinery and specialised equipment were also deployed to clear debris and assist the rescue teams.
The injured workers were initially taken to the district hospital in Gopeshwar for treatment. The administration also placed Base Hospital Srinagar and AIIMS Rishikesh on alert to deal with any critically injured workers who might require advanced medical care.
Officials said the rescue and relief operation was continuing and the administration was monitoring the situation closely.

headline: 7 killed, 14 injured after tunnel collapse in Uttarakhand's Chamoli; 1 trapped
full_text:
7 killed, 14 injured after tunnel collapse in Uttarakhand's Chamoli; 1 trapped
A tunnel under construction at the THDC project in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district collapsed, trapping several workers after debris and water entered the site.
Seven workers have died and 14 others were injured after debris and water entered an under-construction hydro tunnel at the THDC project in Mayapur (Pipalkoti) in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Thursday evening. One worker remain trapped inside the tunnel, while 21 of the 22 workers who were inside have been accounted for.
The incident occurred around 6.45 pm when a large volume of debris and water suddenly entered the tunnel being constructed by HCC. Workers from the shift on duty were trapped inside.
Rescue operations were launched immediately after the accident, with teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and other agencies deployed at the site.
Rescue teams are continuing efforts to reach the worker still trapped inside. Machinery is being used to clear debris and drain water from the tunnel.
The injured workers were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment. Officials said those with serious injuries would be shifted to higher medical centres, while others were being treated at Gopeshwar.
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami is monitoring the rescue operation. Earlier, he said several workers had been rescued and that all available resources were being deployed to evacuate those still trapped. He also said he had spoken to the Chief Ministers of Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh regarding the incident.
Chamoli District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar said the incident occurred at the under-construction tunnel of a THDC hydropower project and that rescue teams were working to evacuate the remaining workers.
The administration has mobilised all available machinery and personnel at the site as the rescue operation continues.
RESCUE OPERATION STARTED
A search and rescue operation was launched immediately after the incident.
Rescue teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) are using improvised drum boats to reach them, as the workers are stranded due to debris and water that entered the tunnel. Rescue operations are continuing.
Previously, Chamoli District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar said that 16 workers had been rescued safely until 9 PM, while efforts were continuing to evacuate the remaining people trapped inside the tunnel.
"This is a tunnel under construction for a hydropower project belonging to THDC. Around 6:30 or 6:45 PM, a large volume of debris and water surged into the tunnel. Workers from the shift on duty got trapped inside. NDRF and SDRF teams, along with all our machinery, are currently engaged in operations for the remaining individuals, and we are hopeful that we will be able to rescue everyone within the next few hours," said Kumar.
Given the seriousness of the situation, teams of the Army, Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) were rushed to the site.
Rescue operations are currently being carried out by personnel from the District Incident Response Force (DIRF), local police and the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF).
UTTARAKHAND CM OVERSEES RESCUE ACT
Following the incident, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami had expressed concern and directed authorities to carry out rescue operations on a war footing.
In a statement, the Chief Minister said teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) had been rushed to the site in view of the seriousness of the incident.
He also instructed the district administration and all concerned departments to work in coordination to ensure a swift rescue operation.
Dhami said he was personally monitoring the situation and remained in constant touch with senior officials, receiving regular updates on the rescue efforts.
"The government's top priority is to ensure the safe evacuation of every person trapped inside the tunnel. All necessary resources have been deployed for the rescue operation," the Chief Minister said.
He also directed officials to ensure there was no delay or lapse in the ongoing rescue work and asked the administration to extend all possible assistance to the affected workers and their families.
Authorities are yet to ascertain the cause of the collapse.

headline: UP teen uses AI-generated image to fake kidnapping, demands ₹2 lakh from father to pay off gaming debt
full_text:
UP teen uses AI-generated image to fake kidnapping, demands ₹2 lakh from father to pay off gaming debt
The ransom message to his father, a cloth merchant, read that the 16-year-old would be killed if the money was not transferred.
A 16-year-old boy in Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur allegedly staged his own kidnapping after losing nearly ₹3 lakh in online games and sent his father an AI-generated image to make the abduction appear genuine, police said on Thursday.
The Class 11 student reportedly had his Delhi-based girlfriend help him to make the abduction appear genuine. Using artificial intelligence, they created an image showing the teen with blood smeared across his face and tape covering his mouth, PTI reported.
Fake kidnapping, ransom demand
The student then sent the photograph to his father on WhatsApp along with a message demanding ₹1 lakh. The message also said that he would be killed if the money was not transferred.
ALSO READ | Four held for kidnapping Mohali youth, demanding ₹1 lakh ransom
When his father said he was unable to arrange the amount, the teenager allegedly changed the demand and asked him to bring ₹2 lakh in cash.
Concerned about his son's safety, the father contacted the police. This led to an immediate investigation.
Police trace teenager to friend's house
Police said the teenager, whose father is a cloth merchant in Sant Kabir Nagar, borrowed money from friends and others to fund his online gaming. When they began asking him to repay the money, he allegedly planned the fake kidnapping to get cash from his family.
On Tuesday evening, he left home telling his family that he was going to Sikriganj and put his phone on flight mode. He later connected the device to a friend's Wi-Fi network and sent the ransom message.
Police placed the mobile number under surveillance and traced its location to Sikriganj. A police team reached the area at around 2 am and found the teenager at a friend's house.
READ ALSO | ‘Arrange ₹15 lakh’: MP teen fakes kidnap, writes ransom note, breaks piggy bank for money to live alone
Student admits to fabricating abduction story
The teenager admitted to staging the kidnapping to raise money and repay his online gaming debts, Additional SP South Dinesh Kumar Puri said on Wednesday evening.
Police are now investigating the involvement of other people who may have helped him in carrying out the plan.
Similar case
Last year, a 13-year-old girl in Madhya Pradesh's Jabalpur allegedly staged her own kidnapping after being scolded by her mother over using her mobile phone, talking to friends and wearing lipstick. She left a ₹15 lakh ransom note and ran away, but police found her within hours in the Sadar area.
The girl later admitted that she had planned the fake abduction to escape restrictions at home. She had even broken open her piggy bank to rent a room where she planned to live alone for a month. Police reunited her with her family after confirming that she had written the ransom note herself.

headline: The Congress, the Trinamool Congress, and the Samajwadi Party boycotted the customary tea party hosted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Thursday after the House was adjourned sine die.
full_text:
The Congress, the Trinamool Congress, and the Samajwadi Party boycotted the customary tea party hosted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Thursday after the House was adjourned sine die.
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader Kanimozhi attended the traditional get-together though, sources said.
In the Rajya Sabha, opposition leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and former party chief Sonia Gandhi, attended the tea party hosted by Chairman C P Radhakrishnan.
According to sources, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, and several other senior leaders and ministers were present at the tea party in the Lok Sabha Speaker's chamber.
A senior Congress leader stated that leaders from the Congress, SP, TMC, and various other INDIA bloc parties did not participate in the event.
A tea party is hosted by the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman in their chambers after the proceedings of the two Houses are adjourned sine die.

In the Lok Sabha, 11 bills were passed without discussion, while one underwent discussion... In the Rajya Sabha, the bill was fully discussed. Only the main opposition, the Congress Party, and some others walked out, while other opposition parties participated: Kiren Rijiju
BJP MP Jagdambika Pal's remarks, made while he was presiding over the Lok Sabha proceedings, were expunged by Speaker Om Birla on Wednesday, the second time in the Monsoon Session currently underway.
The expunged remarks referred to Chotelal, Samajwadi Party MP from Robertsganj.
As the House re-assembled at 2 pm on Wednesday after an adjournment, Pal was trying to get the House in order, telling opposition MPs to get back in their place, and made a comment referring to Chotelal.
Earlier, in a rare decision on August 5, Birla expunged remarks made by Pal while he was presiding over the proceedings ahead of the passage of the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026.
Pal had made certain observations about Samajwadi Party MP Ruchi Vira and Congress MP KC Venugopal, who were protesting against the police action on students during their march to Parliament on July 20.
The BJP leader made the remarks against the SP's Moradabad MP in an admonishment for disrupting the proceedings. The expunged remarks against Venugopal were also made in the same context.
Congress MP Manish Tewari has given an Adjournment Motion notice in the Lok Sabha seeking a discussion on a possible new Anti-Defection Law.
Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Ram Gopal Yadav on Thursday hit out at Union Home Minister Amit Shah's proposal of submitting 'written questions' before answering them in Parliament, questioning if the House is now expected to "function like a press conference."
Speaking to reporters, Yadav said, "The Honorable home minister gave a statement yesterday, saying that questions should be submitted in writing to the Speaker first, and then he will answer. You all know--it has never been like this. There is no such tradition. The conventions and established practices have always been that ministers give a statement or an answer, and MPs from all parties ask for clarifications within a set time limit. That is the correct procedure."
"It's not about 'submit your questions first.' This is a practice followed in press conferences where questions are given in advance. Will the House now also function like a press conference?" he questioned.
Yadav asserted that the opposition would not accept new conditions that deviate from democratic norms. "The opposition can never accept this, no matter how much the ruling party claims 'the opposition is running away.' If you keep breaking traditions every day, we will not be a party to it," he added.
Describing the ongoing Monsoon Session, the senior MP further alleged, "Due to the government's stubbornness, several bills were passed forcibly amidst the din of the house throughout the session. Ideally, according to the rules, no bill should be passed in such a manner. The rule dictates that bills passed in such a way are not constitutional."

headline: Sonam Wangchuk's pitch for India's '2nd Independence movement' to 'reform political system'
full_text:
Sonam Wangchuk's pitch for India's '2nd Independence movement' to 'reform political system'
Sonam Wangchuk has called for India's second independence movement to bring about changes in how India chooses its leaders
Scientist and activist Sonam Wangchuk has called for “India’s second Independence movement” to bring about changes in how the country chooses its leaders, urging citizens to suggest “selfless, fearless” people of character and substance who can help shape India’s future.
In a post on X on Thursday, Wangchuk said India needs a “peaceful revolution”, particularly in the way political leaders are chosen, if the country is to remain a “respectable nation” by 2047.
He highlighted the criminal cases against elected representatives, saying that close to half of India’s MPs have criminal cases against them, while a third face serious charges such as murder, rape and kidnapping. He said this was contributing to a growing “trust deficit” in the country.
Also read | Sonam Wangchuk speaks to student leader on hunger strike in Jharkhand, urges him to end fast
Wangchuk said he wanted to consult some of the “best minds” across India to brainstorm about what needs to change and how such changes could be brought about. However, he stressed that the conversation should not be limited to intellectuals.
Instead, he called for the involvement of “selfless, fearless men and women of character and substance” who could contribute meaningfully to the effort to reform the political system.
Wangchuk, who is based in Ladakh, acknowledged that he did not know where such people could be found across the country and sought the public’s help in identifying them. He asked people to propose at least one such person from India as well as from their own region.
“Together, can we start India’s 2nd Independence movement?” he asked, framing the initiative as a collective effort to rethink the country’s political system and leadership ahead of 2047, the centenary of India’s Independence.
Wangchuk backs student protests in Jharkhand
Earlier, Wangchuk had extended his support to student leader Devendra Nath Mahato, who is on an indefinite hunger strike in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in the JPSC, JSSC CGL and other competitive examinations.
During their conversation, Mahato said Wangchuk assured him of continued support for the students’ agitation in Jharkhand. Following the assurance, Mahato agreed to consume water and salt but said he would continue his indefinite hunger strike.
Wangchuk’s intervention came weeks after he emerged as a prominent face of a student-led protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations. He joined the protest in June and began an indefinite hunger strike, demanding accountability over concerns surrounding the examination system.

headline: Rahul Gandhi hugs Congress leader, calls it PM's foreign policy. Then Meloni jibe follows
full_text:
Rahul Gandhi hugs Congress leader, calls it PM's foreign policy. Then Meloni jibe follows
A row erupted after Congress MP Rahul Gandhi hugged party leader Sandeep Dikshit at an event and mocked Prime Minister Narendra Modi's hugs with foreign leaders, including Italian PM Giorgia Meloni. The Congress defended Rahul Gandhi, saying he did not mention Meloni's name, while the BJP called the incident deplorable.
Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Thursday took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi's hugs with foreign leaders, including Italian PM Giorgia Meloni, by hugging Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit on stage.
Speaking at the Rachnatmak Congress national convention, Rahul Gandhi said, "I don't know where he (PM Modi) got this idea from. Strange ideas get into people's heads. He thinks this is foreign policy," before giving Dikshit a big hug.
Dikshit quipped, "You weren't hugging me thinking I was Meloni?" Rahul Gandhi then replied, "I haven't reached that stage yet," drawing laughter from the gathering.
The hug triggered a political row, with the BJP accusing Rahul Gandhi of making an "immature" remark, while the Congress defended Gandhi scion and said he had not even mentioned Meloni by name.
BJP spokesperson Sanju Verma told India Today TV that Rahul Gandhi's "remark was deplorable, despicable" and "certainly not becoming" of a Leader of Opposition or someone aspiring to be Prime Minister.
Congress spokesperson Shama Mohamed, however, said Rahul Gandhi had made no jibe at Meloni. "Rahul Gandhi has not used the word Meloni. Rahul Gandhi gave him (Sandeep Dikshit) a hug. There is nothing wrong," she told India Today TV.
Shama also criticised PM Modi's interactions with foreign leaders, saying she was "appalled" by his frequent hugs. "I am married to a foreigner. They don't like to be hugged. They like hands to be shaken. When they are familiar with you, they do a hug or a kiss," she said.
RAHUL GANDHI CALLS BJP, RSS 'BUNCH OF JOKERS'
At the event, Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on the BJP and RSS, calling them a "bunch of jokers" and "clowns" who, he claimed, have no understanding of India's history, culture or present-day reality.
He said the BJP-RSS's political philosophy was to impose an order on India that benefits them and certain other people, while the Congress wanted to allow the country to "express itself".
"If you look at what was happening at Jantar Mantar, the students wanted to express themselves, but the government stated that 'we want order and you cannot express yourselves'," he said.
He said the political battle was between those who wanted to impose an order on others and those who wanted people to express themselves.
'RSS NOW AN INSTRUMENT OF LARGE CAPITAL'
The Raebareli MP claimed that the RSS had lost its original character and had been "captured and utilised by large capital", naming industrialists Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani.
"The RSS as an original force is dead, they are gone. Now the RSS is an instrument of large capital. They are servants of Mr Adani, just like Mr Modi is a servant of Mr Adani," he alleged.
He asserted that the RSS had originally represented sections of India's small businessmen but that its character had changed over the years.
The Leader of Opposition also linked the change to demonetisation, alleging that the RSS had contributed to policies that hurt small businesses.
'WE WILL KEEP PM, AMIT SHAH AWAKE'
Rahul Gandhi vowed to continue putting pressure on the government and said PM Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah would not be allowed to "sleep" until they resigned.
"Till the day PM Modi and Amit Shah don't give their resignations, they will not be able to sleep. We will keep them awake," he said.
He stressed that the Congress would continue its campaign without violence or hatred. "We will do it without hate, violence. We are fighting for our culture. Our country is not about hate but about love, brotherhood and ahimsa (non-violence)," he said.
Rahul Gandhi claimed that the RSS had stopped being an original force and no longer represented the India it once sought to engage with.
"You cannot understand India 3,000 years ago, you have to understand India today. To understand it today, you have to understand its expression," he said.
He further said that even if the RSS sought to create its own "little order", it would eventually be challenged and broken by India's expression.

headline: New Delhi: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s foreign policy Thursday at the Rachnatmak Congress Organising National Convention in New Delhi, using a mock hug with party leader Sandeep Dikshit to poke fun at M...
full_text:
New Delhi: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s foreign policy Thursday at the Rachnatmak Congress Organising National Convention in New Delhi, using a mock hug with party leader Sandeep Dikshit to poke fun at Modi’s interactions with foreign leaders.
Gandhi told the gathering he would show what foreign policy meant for Modi. He then stretched out his arms and walked towards Dikshit for a hug.
“I don’t know where he (Modi) got this idea from. Strange ideas get into people’s heads. He thinks this is foreign policy,” Gandhi said. Dikshit then played along, bringing Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni into the joke. “You weren’t hugging me thinking I was Meloni?” he said, prompting laughter from the crowd.
Gandhi replied: “I haven’t reached that stage yet.”
The exchange was a reference to Modi’s public interactions with foreign leaders, including Meloni, with whom he shared a viral ‘Melody’ moment.
Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, used the gesture to mock what he portrayed as the Prime Minister’s approach to diplomacy, with the physical act of hugging becoming the central punchline of his attack.
Criticising Gandhi for mocking the Prime Minister in this manner, BJP MP Nishikant Dubey shared a video of the Congress event with the caption: “Do you think Rahul Gandhi’s mental state is sound?”
Referring to the remark about the Italian Prime Minister, BJP’s Bandi Sanjay Kumar wrote on X: “Targeting Prime Ministers with such cheap language isn’t politics. It is gutter-level behaviour that brings shame to Indian political discourse.”
The moment was followed by a broader criticism of the government’s handling of foreign policy. Gandhi questioned India’s position amid the West Asia war, arguing that the situation presented New Delhi with an opportunity to use its relationships with major powers to broker peace.
“War broke out in Iran. For India, had it recognized its own strength and had its leader been someone like Indira Gandhi, this presented the greatest opportunity in the world. What kind of opportunity? Iran was our old friend, America was our friend, and Russia was our friend. We could have stepped up, become relevant, and leveraged these friendships. But what actually happened? Nothing of the sort. Instead, Pakistan stepped in and took our place; Pakistan became the mediator, while India and Modi-ji simply looked on,” he said.
He then turned his criticism towards the India-China border, specifically referring to Arunachal Pradesh and areas where Indian and Chinese forces carry out border patrols.
Speaking about China, Rahul said, “I receive information directly from Modi ji’s office these days; there is a full-blown revolt going on inside. In our patrolling areas, specifically in Arunachal, China blocked us from patrolling. They essentially said, ‘Look, all that is fine—it is indeed your land—but you cannot patrol here’.”
(Edited by Amrtansh Arora)

headline: Kerala govt may order probe into previous LDF's Messi, Argentina visit proposal
full_text:
Kerala govt may order probe into previous LDF's Messi, Argentina visit proposal
Kerala ministers have accused the previous government of procedural lapses in the failed Messi event plan. The row has widened into questions over public spending, sponsor selection and misuse of official machinery.
The UDF government in Kerala is likely to order a probe into alleged irregularities and procedural lapses in the previous Left government's attempt to bring football legend Lionel Messi and the Argentina team to the state. Sports Minister O J Janeesh on Wednesday rejected former minister V Abdurahiman's defence of the proposal and alleged that official machinery was used to help a private individual make financial gains.
Later in the day, Health and Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan also said the government would order an investigation into the campaign around Messi's proposed visit and the renovation of a stadium in its name. The remarks came a day after Janeesh said the Sports Department had submitted its inquiry report on the controversy to the government for further action.
Janeesh said there was no substance in Abdurahiman's claim that the government had not suffered any financial loss in connection with the proposed event. He alleged that official procedures were not followed from the start and that there was no transparency in selecting the sponsor and handling the proposal.
"The government machinery was misused for a private event management company. From the Chief Secretary to the district collector, police and Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA), the administrative machinery was used for a private individual," Janeesh alleged while speaking to reporters. He said this created an opportunity for a private party to make substantial financial gains and, therefore, it was meaningless to argue that the government had suffered no loss.
The minister said the first email proposing the event was received by the then sports minister from an advertising company that had been registered only about 20 days earlier. He said the company had a capital of only Rs 1 lakh and questioned whether its background, financial capacity and experience to organise an event involving Messi and the Argentina team had been examined.
Janeesh alleged that the proposal was not handled according to the prescribed Rules of Procedure. He said the communication remained outside the official file system for nearly two years without being registered or given a file number. "It is clear that there were individual interests. The former sports minister's action in this regard amounts to a serious violation of the oath of office," he alleged, adding that official procedures for correspondence with private individuals and institutions should have been followed.
He also questioned the purpose of Abdurahiman's trip to Spain in connection with the proposal and said there should be greater clarity on that visit as well as on the selection of the sponsor. Janeesh alleged that the previous minister had communicated with private parties through his personal email for nearly two years before bringing the matter into official files, and said the government had a legal and constitutional responsibility in dealing with such matters.
The minister said around Rs 14 lakh of government money had been spent, including on the Spain visit, and that this should also be treated as a loss. He also referred to reports that Rs 126 crore provided by the sponsor had been lost and said clarity was needed on where that money went. Janeesh further questioned former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan's earlier statement assuring Kerala that Messi would come to the state, asking whether he was aware of the developments that had now come to light.
Muraleedharan said the government would act over the matter. "We will definitely bring before the law those who spent crores in the name of Messi, who never came. There is no doubt about it. We will bring out the truth, including the alleged corruption in the stadium renovation, for which Rs 75 crore was spent," he told reporters. He said the facts would come out and the government would not be deterred by false propaganda, adding that the then chief minister would also have to answer questions on the issue.
Janeesh had said the inquiry report was prepared by the Sports Department Special Secretary after examining files available with the department and had been handed over to the government.
Abdurahiman, however, has rejected the allegations and said the LDF government followed all prescribed procedures while trying to bring the Argentina team to Kerala for a friendly match. In a detailed statement, he said the state government did not suffer even a single rupee of loss because the agreement for the match was between the Argentina Football Association and the sponsor and imposed no financial liability on the government.

headline: The Swadeshi Jagaran Manch (SJM), the economic wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsewak Sangh (RSS), urged the Central Government on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) to remain firm on India’s energy policy and reject all attempts by the United States to use tari...
full_text:
The Swadeshi Jagaran Manch (SJM), the economic wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsewak Sangh (RSS), urged the Central Government on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) to remain firm on India’s energy policy and reject all attempts by the United States to use tariffs as leverage over New Delhi’s purchase of Russian crude oil.
The organisation was reacting to recent U.S. Senate legislation that would authorise the U.S. President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries making significant purchases of Russian oil.
“SJM fully supports the Government of India’s stand on the issue that India’s purchase of Russian crude oil is based on considerations of energy security, availability, price, diversification of supplies and the interests of Indian consumers. India has time and again made it clear that our sovereign right to purchase energy from legitimate international markets cannot be dictated by any third country,” said SJM National Co Convener, Ashwani Mahajan.
Threat to free trade
He added that the unilateral tariffs could undermine free and fair international trade and create uncertainty for exporters, importers, investors and consumers. He also argued that Russian crude has helped diversify India’s oil supplies and contain energy costs.
The organisation linked the proposed tariff measures to ongoing India-U.S. trade negotiations, arguing that discussions between the two countries should be based on equality, reciprocity and mutual respect rather than the threat of punitive duties.
“If one powerful country is allowed to impose punitive tariffs on another country for buying goods from a third country, the principle of sovereign economic decision-making itself comes under threat,” said Mr. Mahajan.
He also criticised recent policy changes concerning foreign investment in e-commerce and the proposed framework allowing banks and payment providers to levy merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions. He claimed the measures could benefit U.S.-based companies and weaken Indian businesses and digital-payment platforms.
Calling for a stronger response to Washington’s actions, SJM urged the government to reconsider the e-commerce policy change, withhold the MDR-related legislation, and reject any demand affecting India’s agriculture, dairy sector, energy security or strategic autonomy.
The organisation also called for a boycott of American products and services.
“Boycott products like Pepsi and Coke, social media firms, and e-Commerce platforms belonging to U.S. companies, to start with. If the U.S. continues to act against India’s interests, this boycott can be extended to services of other U.S. giants as well,” said Mr. Mahajan.

headline: Parliament Monsoon Session ends amid disruptions; Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die
full_text:
Parliament Monsoon Session ends amid disruptions; Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 13, 2026, 12:40 IST

File photo: Proceedings in the Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament, in New Delhi.
NEW DELHI: The Monsoon Session of Parliament ended on Thursday with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die amid repeated disruptions and political confrontations between the government and Opposition.The session, which began on July 20, witnessed protests inside and outside the Houses over several issues, while Parliament also passed a number of legislations.
Rijiju says session successful in business, but debate fell short
Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the Monsoon Session was successful in terms of legislative business but fell short on debate and discussion. He said Parliament passed 12 Bills during the session, but productivity remained low amid repeated disruptions.
"In terms of business, it was a very successful session; we passed a total of 12 bills. However, from the perspective of debate and discussion, it was not as successful," Rijiju said.He said the Lok Sabha recorded 19 per cent productivity against the total time allotted, while productivity in the Rajya Sabha stood at 39 per cent. Rijiju attributed the lower productivity largely to disruptions by Opposition parties, while noting that NDA members and MPs from some Opposition parties participated in debates.
Rijiju said only one Bill in the Lok Sabha â the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, dealing with paper leaks and unfair means in examinations â underwent a full discussion. The legislation was also discussed in the Rajya Sabha.He criticised the Opposition for not allowing debates to proceed, saying the government was ready to provide answers to questions raised by Opposition MPs. "This is not healthy for the parliamentary democracy," Rijiju said.
He also accused Congress MPs of focusing on slogans, placards and protests instead of parliamentary debate, and said he hoped there would be a change before the Winter Session."In the Lok Sabha, 11 bills were passed without discussion, while one underwent discussion," Rijiju said, adding that the concerned Bill was fully discussed in the Rajya Sabha.
Rajya Sabha skips question hour, passes Mines and Minerals Bill
The Rajya Sabha was adjourned sine die after chairman C P Radhakrishnan highlighted the performance of the House during the session.Deviating from the normal pre-lunch schedule on the final day, the Upper House dispensed with the Zero Hour and Question Hour and took up the Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill. The legislation was subsequently passed by a voice vote.The Rajya Sabha had witnessed repeated disruptions during the session over issues including police action against students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak and allegations concerning the theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.The House also witnessed a confrontation between leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge and the government over an alleged 'Shuddhikaran' or purification ritual at a stage in Haldwani after Kharge addressed a Congress rally there on August 8.Kharge raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha, saying he had spoken about people's problems and had not mentioned any community or religion during his speech.âBut after my speech, people associated with the BJP carried out a 'purification' ritual of that stage,â Kharge said, questioning whether such an incident was appropriate in a democracy.Leader of the House JP Nadda said the BJP did not support such activities and assured the House that the allegation would be investigated.âWhat Kharge ji has said is truly a matter of concernânot just for the Congress party, but for all of us,â Nadda said. âI want to make it absolutely clear that the BJP does not subscribe to such activities.âChairman C P Radhakrishnan said untouchability was condemned by all members and asked the government to investigate the allegation and punish those responsible if it was found to be true.
Lok Sabha ends amid opposition protests
The Lok Sabha was also adjourned sine die soon after proceedings began on the final day, following the traditional playing of Vande Mataram.Proceedings were disrupted by Opposition MPs amid sloganeering, with political tensions also spilling into the Parliament complex.BJP and opposition held counter-protests at the Makar Dwar steps, with the BJP protesting against Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi over the Congress' position on the ongoing protests in Jharkhand.Opposition MPs, meanwhile, raised demands for the Union Home Minister to make a statement in the House and for the Prime Minister to respond to issues raised by them.Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi accused the ruling party of preventing Parliament from functioning.
âIt is the ruling party itself that is preventing Parliament from functioning,â he said, arguing that the Opposition had been seeking discussions and responses from the government on issues including the Public Examinations Amendment Act.Union minister Manohar Lal Khattar rejected the opposition's allegations and said Parliament could not function without discussion.âThe Lok Sabha is a forum for discussion. There is no point in proceeding without discussion,â Khattar said. He added that the House was a platform for representatives from across the country and âdoes not belong to any single individualâ.The session ended after weeks of political confrontation, with disruptions remaining a prominent feature of proceedings in both Houses.
