headline: With hours left, Parliament heads for a tense Monsoon Session finish
full_text:
With hours left, Parliament heads for a tense Monsoon Session finish
Amit Shah offered a marathon debate on the student protests, but Rahul Gandhi demanded a direct answer on who ordered the police action, leaving Parliament deadlocked as the Monsoon Session entered its final day.
Parliament’s Monsoon Session will enter its final day on Thursday with the government and Opposition still locked in a standoff over the student protests, after Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s offer of an extended debate failed to break the deadlock in the Lok Sabha.
Shah offered to participate in a detailed discussion on the protests and allegations of police action against students. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, however, rejected the proposal, saying the Opposition wanted a direct answer on who ordered the use of pellet guns and force against protesters rather than a “lecture” from the Home Minister.
The Lok Sabha was eventually adjourned for the day amid sloganeering despite repeated appeals from the government to allow the discussion.
AMIT SHAH OFFERS EXTENDED DEBATE
The confrontation began soon after the Lok Sabha assembled at 11 am on Wednesday.
Shah said the government was ready to discuss all issues concerning the student protests and asked the Opposition to submit a written request to Speaker Om Birla.
He offered to begin the discussion at 3 pm on Wednesday and continue it until 3 pm on Thursday.
“Even today, I say that they should submit a letter to the Speaker by 2 pm. We are ready for all kinds of discussions from 3 pm today until 3 pm tomorrow,” Shah said.
He later wrote to the Speaker, saying he was prepared to remain present throughout the debate and respond to questions raised by the Opposition.
Shah said dialogue and discussion were the only ways to resolve issues in a democracy and maintained that the government had nothing to hide.
The Opposition, however, did not accept the offer.
‘IF HE ORDERED IT, HE SHOULD RESIGN’
Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition was not interested in listening to what he described as Shah’s “imagination” or a lengthy lecture.
He said young people wanted to know who ordered the use of pellet guns, lathi charges and other force against protesting students.
“If Mr Amit Shah gave the order to shoot our children, he should resign because he is culpable, and if he did not, he should resign because he is incompetent,” Gandhi said.
He argued that the Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force come under the Home Ministry and questioned Shah’s responsibility for the alleged police action.
Gandhi later posted a video of his remarks on X, saying Shah’s silence amounted to a “confession”.
Congress deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi also questioned why the Home Minister had not participated in an earlier proposed discussion on education and student protests.
He said Shah should make a statement in Parliament on the police action against protesters and allegations surrounding the use of AK-47s in Bihar.
GOVERNMENT ACCUSES OPPOSITION OF AVOIDING DEBATE
The government, in turn, accused the Opposition of refusing the very discussion it had been demanding.
When the Lok Sabha met again at 3 pm after two adjournments, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the government was ready to begin the debate immediately and pointed out that Shah had already written to the Speaker.
He urged the Opposition not to “run away” when the Home Minister was prepared to answer its questions.
Presiding officer Jagdambika Pal also repeatedly appealed to Opposition members to allow proceedings to continue, but protests and sloganeering persisted.
The House was eventually adjourned for the day.
Rijiju later called it “unthinkable and incomprehensible” that the Opposition was refusing a discussion when the government had agreed to one.
WHY THE STUDENT ROW HAS DOMINATED THE SESSION
The student protests have emerged as one of the main flashpoints of the Monsoon Session.
The Opposition has demanded accountability over police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak, including allegations of pellet gun use, lathi charges and tear gas at Jantar Mantar.
Congress has also repeatedly sought statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Shah.
The government has maintained that it is willing to discuss the issue, but disagreement over the scope and nature of the debate has repeatedly disrupted proceedings.
With the session ending on Thursday, there has been no breakthrough so far.
FCRA BILL SENT TO JPC
Even as the student row kept Parliament on edge, the government managed to move ahead on several pieces of legislative business.
The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday adopted a motion referring the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee. The Lok Sabha had already approved the referral.
The JPC will comprise 21 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha and has been asked to submit its report by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session.
Introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25, the Bill proposes tighter oversight of foreign contributions received by NGOs and other organisations. It also provides for a designated authority to manage and dispose of assets if an organisation loses its FCRA licence.
The Opposition has opposed the legislation, alleging that some provisions could affect legitimate foreign funding for Christian NGOs and minority-run social welfare and educational institutions.
The government has rejected the charge, saying the Bill is not religion-specific and is aimed at regulating foreign contributions.
Congress MP KC Venugopal demanded that the legislation be withdrawn, while Rijiju pointed out that Opposition parties had themselves sought its examination by a parliamentary committee and urged them to raise their objections before the JPC.
KERALA TO BECOME KERALAM
Parliament also cleared legislation to officially change Kerala’s name to Keralam.
The Rajya Sabha passed the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, by voice vote on Wednesday, a day after it was cleared by the Lok Sabha.
The move follows a resolution passed by the Kerala Assembly in 2024 urging the Centre to change the state’s name.
The Bill provides for the alteration of the name and consequential amendments to the Constitution, including the First Schedule.
RAJYA SABHA CLEARS NCDC AMENDMENT BILL
The Rajya Sabha also passed the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, a day after it cleared the Lok Sabha.
The legislation expands the powers of the National Cooperative Development Corporation, allowing it to provide loans and grants directly to cooperative societies.
The NCDC, a statutory organisation under the Ministry of Cooperation, will also be allowed, with prior approval from the Centre, to participate in the share capital of cooperatives and other entities involved in cooperative development.
The changes are aimed at widening the channels through which financial assistance can reach the cooperative sector.
FINAL DAY, STUDENT PROTEST ROW STILL UNRESOLVED
The Monsoon Session began with the Opposition raising the NEET paper leak and alleged irregularities involving donations to the Ram temple in Ayodhya, before the political focus shifted sharply to police action against protesting students.
The issue has since dominated proceedings and contributed to repeated adjournments.
The government’s last-minute offer of an extended discussion on Wednesday failed to end the impasse.
The Lok Sabha will meet again at 11 am on Thursday for the final scheduled day of the session, leaving only a narrow window for the two sides to find common ground.
For now, the government says it is ready to debate. The Opposition says it first wants a direct answer on accountability. That divide remains unresolved as the Monsoon Session heads into its final day.

headline: Rape convict, ex-MP Prajwal Revanna's phone in Bengaluru jail had Netflix, WhatsApp, Insta, Prime Video
full_text:
Rape convict, ex-MP Prajwal Revanna's phone in Bengaluru jail had Netflix, WhatsApp, Insta, Prime Video
Prajwal Revanna's phone was accompanied by a white charger, a blue pocket notebook and a black SanDisk pen drive.
Netflix, Instagram, WhatsApp and Prime Video were among applications found on a mobile phone seized from former MP Prajwal Revanna during a Central Crime Branch raid at Parappana Agrahara Central Prison, where he is serving a life sentence.
The applications were installed on a light blue Redmi 5G handset recovered from Room 4 on the first floor of Security Section 3 during a search conducted between 2 pm and 9 pm on Tuesday. The apps were password protected, and both Revanna and fellow inmate Pratap Rai told the search team that they did not know the passwords, the FIR registered over the matter said.
The phone was accompanied by a white charger, a blue pocket notebook and a black SanDisk pen drive. The room was occupied by Revanna and Rai, an undertrial prisoner.
Also Read | Rebalancing act: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar allots portfolios to 19 ministers ahead of Assembly session
While the phone was recovered from Revannna, officials said Rai told them that the phone, charger and pen drive belonged to him and that he used the handset to speak to his relatives and lawyer. Revanna also told the team that he had used Rai’s phone to call his relatives and lawyer. He claimed the notebook belonged to him.
The CCB seized all four items and lodged a complaint against the two inmates under provisions of the Karnataka Prisons (Amendment) Act, 2022, and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The complaint alleges that prohibited articles were brought into the prison without authorisation and used by the inmates.
DGP Prison and Correctional Services Alok Kumar said the raid covered high profile prisoners and lasted about four to five hours. He said another mobile phone was found in Rai’s possession. “Yesterday (Tuesday) afternoon, a raid was conducted by CCB on all the high profile prisoners. An Android phone has been seized from Prajwal Revanna’s possession,” Kumar said.
Police are examining CCTV footage and collecting further information before issuing notices and taking additional action. “A detailed enquiry is being conducted into this incident,” Kumar said.
Kumar said the Assistant Superintendent concerned had been suspended following a report from the DIG, South, while a show cause notice was issued to the superintendent of Bengaluru Central Prison. “CCB has lodged the complaint with Parappana Agrahara Police Station, and registration of an FIR is in progress,” Kumar said.
The seizure has also led to action against prison officials. Assistant Superintendent Iranna Rangapur was suspended for alleged dereliction of duty, while the superintendent of Bengaluru Central Prison was served a show cause notice.
Home minister Priyank Kharge said he had visited Parappana Agrahara Central Prison two to three weeks earlier and noticed lapses during his inspection. He said he discussed them with regional officials before obtaining chief minister D K Shivakumar’s permission for the raid.
He said similar searches would be conducted across the state. “Whether it is Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Bengaluru or any other prison, we will take strict action. We will keep doing this,” said the minister.
He said officials continuing to follow “old practices” would be identified and face legal action. If any official was found involved in criminal activity, the government would consider dismissal from service.
Revanna, 36, represented Hassan in the Lok Sabha from 2019 to 2023. He was convicted in August 2025 by the Special Court for People’s Representatives for raping a dometic worker at a farmhouse in Holenarasipura, Hassan district.

headline: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) met Governor Gulab Chand Kataria and sought his intervention for granting parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara, a member of the banned terrorist outfit Babbar Khalsa terrorist, who is ...
full_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) met Governor Gulab Chand Kataria and sought his intervention for granting parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara, a member of the banned terrorist outfit Babbar Khalsa terrorist, who is serving a life sentence for the 1995 assassination of former Chief Minister Beant Singh.
Mr. Mann requested the Punjab Governor to consider granting 10 day-parole to Hawara on humanitarian grounds, saying that after 31 years, his ailing mother has a renewed hope of meeting her son. The Chief Minister said the matter requires the Governor’s recommendation as the case is being heard in Delhi, while assuring that the Punjab government will take full responsibility for ensuring that law and order is not affected if Hawara is granted parole.
“Jagtar Singh Hawara has been lodged in Jail for the last 31 years. His mother is old and suffering from age-related health issues and is currently semi-conscious. In view of her deteriorating health condition, I have requested the Governor to kindly consider granting 10 days’ parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara at the earliest so that he can meet his mother,” he said.
The Punjab and Haryana High Court, last month had directed Mandoli prison authorities in Delhi, where Hawara is currently lodged, to seek recommendations from the Chandigarh Administration and decide his parole application within a stipulated time frame. In 2007, Hawara was sentenced to death, but in 2010 it was commuted by the High Court. Hawara is serving imprisonment for the rest of his life in connection with the August 31, 1995, blast at the Civil Secretariat in Chandigarh, which killed Beant Singh and 16 others.
Interestingly, in March this year, the Punjab government had written to the Tihar Jail authorities recommending the rejection of the parole application of Hawara.

headline: Karnataka says releasing 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu difficult
full_text:
Karnataka says releasing 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu difficult
Karnataka has said it will be difficult to release 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water daily to Tamil Nadu. The state will place its objections before the Supreme Court as protests gather pace.
Karnataka Minister Ramalinga Reddy on Wednesday said the state would find it difficult to release 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water a day to Tamil Nadu, as directed by the Cauvery Water Management Authority.
He said the state government would decide its next course of action after a Supreme Court hearing on Thursday on Tamil Nadu's petition, and added that it would ensure that no injustice was done to Karnataka.
The Cauvery Water Regulation Committee, which met in New Delhi on Tuesday, directed Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days from August 12. The Cauvery Water Management Authority later upheld the decision.
Reddy said discussions had been held with Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and officials. “I have held discussions with the Chief Minister (D K Shivakumar) and officials. The CM spoke to our Advocate General and advocates in Delhi. Tamil Nadu's petition is coming up before the Supreme Court tomorrow; it has been listed. We will have an opportunity there, and our advocates will file our objections. Let's see what the Supreme Court says. Thereafter, we will have further options,” he said.
Speaking to reporters, the State Water Resources Minister said the government's future course of action would depend on the outcome of the hearing. “Tamil Nadu has filed a petition, and we have been served a notice. We will have an opportunity to present our case there. Based on the outcome, we will decide whether further legal action is required. This is based on the suggestions given by the advocates,” he added.
The Tamil Nadu government had earlier this month moved the Supreme Court over the Cauvery dispute with Karnataka, saying that the quantum of water directed by the CWRC, as well as the water released by Karnataka, was insufficient.
Earlier, on July 28, the CWRC had directed Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. Karnataka had initially said it could not release water because of poor storage in its reservoirs. However, after heavy rain in the Cauvery catchment areas in the state, it began releasing water under the earlier 3,500-cusec direction.
Reddy said Karnataka had complied with that earlier order and had, in fact, released more water to Tamil Nadu. “When the Kabini dam filled due to rains in the catchment area, the water flowed downstream as there was no scope to store it further. About 10 TMC of water has flown,” he said.
He said Karnataka had about 76 TMC of water in its reservoirs, of which 36 TMC would be needed every year for drinking water, apart from losses due to evaporation and the requirement for rivers and crops. “We have about 76 TMC of water (in our dams), out of which we will need 36 TMC a year for drinking water. There will also be evaporation, and we will have to release water to rivers and for crops. Asking Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs for 15 days is inappropriate,” he said.
Reddy said the earlier direction to release 3,500 cusecs a day was somewhat acceptable, but the latest order to release 12,000 cusecs daily for 15 days, amounting to about 16 TMC, was “too costly” for Karnataka. He said the state would not have faced difficulty if it had been asked to release a smaller quantity. “This is too high a quantity,” he said.
He also said the monsoon had not been satisfactory in Karnataka's old Mysuru region and claimed that Tamil Nadu had enough water in its reservoirs. He said Tamil Nadu receives most of its rainfall during the northeast monsoon from October to December and has a better water table than Karnataka. “Our water table is too low here. Even if we go 800-1,000 feet, we don't get water, while they get water at much higher levels. Despite our Additional Chief Secretary, advocates, and experts effectively putting forward our case with all these facts, the order has come. It will be difficult for us to release 16 TMC of water in 15 days. We have discussed it. We will decide what to do,” he said.
“The CM has spoken to advocates in New Delhi and experts. We will ensure that no injustice happens to the state,” he added.
Meanwhile, farmers have staged sporadic protests in Cauvery basin districts, including Mandya and Mysuru, against the water release order. Some pro-Kannada organisations have called for a Karnataka bandh on Thursday in protest against the directive, while others have opposed the bandh call. Overall, the state government has said it will place its objections before the Supreme Court and decide its next steps after the hearing.

headline: Ex-TMC MLA Nirmal Ghosh arrested for ‘hastily cremating’ RG Kar rape-murder victim
full_text:
Ex-TMC MLA Nirmal Ghosh arrested for ‘hastily cremating’ RG Kar rape-murder victim
West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari had ordered the Barrackpore Police Commissioner to conduct a fresh probe into the alleged hasty cremation.
Former Trinamool Congress (TMC) legislator Nirmal Ghosh was arrested on Thursday over the alleged hasty cremation of the junior doctor, who was raped and murdered at Kolkata’s RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in 2024.
The arrest on charges of destruction of evidence, criminal conspiracy, and forcing someone to act against their will came four days after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari ordered an inquiry. Three TMC leaders, including Ghosh, were named in the case that was subsequently filed.
A police officer said that Ghosh had been absconding since July 11. He added that his son, Tirthankar, was arrested in another criminal case in which he is a prime accused last month.
Police said Ghosh was arrested in Odisha and is being brought to Kolkata by road. He will be produced before a court on Friday.
TMC leader Kunal Ghosh said Nirmal Ghosh should be punished if he is guilty of anything. “But it must also be taken into account that political leaders do a lot of things to help people in distress.”
Adhikari ordered the inquiry into the cremation on the day two-minute silence was observed across all hospitals on the second anniversary of the 2024 incident, which triggered protests and national outrage.
Bengal CM ordered fresh probe
On August 10, Adhikari said the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is probing the main crime and the alleged corruption at RG Kar Hospital on the Calcutta high court’s orders. “I cannot do anything there. But I have found one aspect that the police can probe. It is the cremation at the obscure Nataghat crematorium,” Adhikari said at an event in memory of the doctor.
The doctor’s body was found on August 9, 2024. Her post-mortem examination was completed within hours, and the body was cremated by evening.
Adhikari directed the Barrackpore police commissioner to register a new case and take appropriate action. “In the cremation schedule, it was the third body on the list that day, but the number was changed from three to one. According to rules, relatives of a deceased person have to pay a cremation fee and sign documents, but the victim’s family did neither,” Adhikari said on August 10.
He added that Nirmal Ghosh and local TMC leaders Somnath Dey and Sanjib Mukherjee did this and must be punished.
Ratna Debnath, the doctor’s mother, defeated Nirmal Ghosh’s son from the Panihati assembly seat in May on a Bharatiya Janata Party ticket.
The fresh case was filed on a complaint by the doctor’s father. In the complaint, the father alleged that Dey arranged a green corridor to bring the body from Kolkata to Panihati after the post-mortem examination instead of handing it to the family. He accused Nirmal Ghosh, Dey, Mukherjee and TMC workers of forcibly entering their home, threatening them to take the body for cremation fast. “They forcibly took the body to the crematorium without allowing us to follow any social norms,” the complaint said.
It added that the cremation was done against the family’s wishes and the TMC leaders forcibly stopped them from signing the cremation papers.
Ghosh, Dey and Mukherjee have denied these allegations over the past two years, saying they merely tried to help the family.
On Thursday, Chhanda, Nirmal Ghosh’s daughter, said her father cooperated with the investigating officers and responded to three summons during the first probe two years ago. “The state police made all the arrangements to bring the body to Panihati for cremation. We will seek legal help since my father has been arrested. If the chief minister is concerned about one family, then he should be concerned about us as well.”
In May, the Calcutta high court ordered the formation of a three-member CBI special investigation team for a second investigation.
The first CBI probe, ordered days after the crime, reached the same conclusion as the Kolkata police, which resulted in the life sentence of former Kolkata police civic volunteer Sanjay Roy.
On May 15, Adhikari suspended former Kolkata police commissioner Vineet Goyal and two other officers, Indira Mukherjee and Abhisek Gupta, on charges of mishandling the rape and murder case and offering money to the doctor’s parents.

headline: FCRA bill sent to JPC amid Opposition uproar, Amit Shah’s debate offer rejected: 'We are ready vs man lacks courage'
full_text:
FCRA bill sent to JPC amid Opposition uproar, Amit Shah’s debate offer rejected: 'We are ready vs man lacks courage'
The FCRA amendment bill was referred to a 31-member JPC amid Opposition protests, while Amit Shah’s offer to discuss student protests was rejected.
A bill proposing controversial amendments to India’s foreign contribution law was referred to a 31-member joint committee of Parliament on Wednesday amid a standoff between the government and the Opposition and repeated disruptions in the House.
The penultimate day of the monsoon session began with Union home minister Amit Shah saying he was ready for a discussion on students’ protests and police action, only for the Opposition – which has been demanding his statement in the House and another debate on the Ram Temple donation row – to rebuff the offer.
“Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led NDA government is ready for discussions. The House should be allowed to run, the Opposition should submit a letter to the speaker by 2pm today. We are ready to start discussion at 3pm today,” Shah said in a rare media interaction outside Parliament.
Deep Dive
Also read: FCRA amendments: What the new bill proposes, and why it has sparked pushback
Opposition rejects Shah’s offer for Parliament debate
Shah also wrote to Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla conveying the government’s readiness to participate in the discussion, only for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to call it a “last-minute attempt” and say that the Opposition was not interested in listening to Shah’s lecture.
The monsoon session is set to end on Thursday. The government indicated that it will not be extended and added that the Opposition’s views will be sought.
Introduced in the previous session but held back at the time, the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill triggered major controversy with the Opposition, several church delegations and three chief ministers of Christian-majority states raising concerns.
31-member panel to examine contentious amendments
Minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai and not Shah, as originally listed in the supplementary list of business introduced a resolution in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday afternoon to form the 31-member JPC with 21 Lok Sabha members and 10 Rajya Sabha members. A Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) member is expected to lead the panel.
The Opposition, which tried to pressurise the government to scrap the bill said it will join the JPC. “Even in the JPC, we will continue to strongly oppose this bill and will not allow these unconstitutional and coercive provisions to become law,” said Congress general secretary KC Venugopal.
“On one side, the RSS is getting donations from foreign countries, while on the other side, the government is trying to target minorities and NGOs. The government should withdraw this bill,” he added.
Also read: Centre eyes consensus on sending foreign funding bill to JPC amid demands for complete withdrawal
Rijiju defends JPC move, accuses Opposition of avoiding debate
Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju hit back, saying that the Congress and others had been demanding for days that the bill be referred to a JPC.
“Yet, even when we are referring such an important bill (to a panel), these people have objections. If KC Venugopal or a member of any other party finds anything objectionable in this bill, or if there is any point they wish to oppose, they can present their views in the JPC. The JPC will have sufficient time; hearings will be held, and other people will also be invited to participate. Instead of being pleased about this, they are speaking against it.”
The minister denied any pressure on the government to refer the contentious bill to a House panel and argued that the decision was taken to allow extensive discussion.
Later in the day, he attacked the Opposition.
Also read: FCRA bill may impact Christian groups, Nagaland CM tells Amit Shah
Shah, Gandhi trade sharp remarks over student protests
“I am totally frustrated. For the first time in my life, I am witnessing a scenario where the government wants a discussion in Parliament, yet the Opposition is running away from it. It is hard to imagine this, because in a parliamentary democracy, it is the Opposition that demands a discussion while the government provides the answers,” Rijiju told reporters.
“We are saying that if the Congress states even tomorrow morning at 11:00am that they are ready for the discussion, we will extend the time. You should ask Congress why they got scared and why they fled,” he added.
He also referred to Shah’s letter to Birla, where the home minister said that Rijiju – on behalf of the government during the business advisory committee meeting – gave consent for a discussion in Parliament on student protests.
“I would also like to mention that earlier, at the request of the Opposition, a discussion has already taken place in the current session of Parliament on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, in which no honourable Member of Parliament from the Opposition expressed any views in the House regarding the NEET examination. Despite this, the government is ready to discuss this issue once again,” Shah said in the letter written in Hindi.
The minister has asserted that he wanted to be present in the House during the scheduled time to participate in the discussion and was ready to answer all questions. “Solutions emerge only through discussion and dialogue in a democracy. I have unwavering faith in democracy and democratic institutions, and it is my belief that this House is meant precisely for discussion and dialogue,” he wrote.
But the Opposition dismissed the offer. Gandhi alleged that Shah lacked the courage to come to Parliament, reiterating the demand that Shah come to the House and speak on police excesses at Jantar Mantar.
“The Opposition has clearly said that we are not interested in Amit Shah giving us a lecture. When I say ‘we’, I mean the younger generation of this country. Who shot the students? Who gave the order to beat up the students with lathis with nails? Did Amit Shah give this order to shoot our children? If he did, then he should resign. For the last 20 days, Amit Shah has been missing. The home minister of India has no courage; he cannot come to the House,” Gandhi said.
“When a man lacks the courage to speak the truth, his silence speaks for him. Amit Shah’s silence is his confession,” he added.
Formed to review a bill, a joint committee of Parliament initially gets three months’ time but is allowed extensions. Currently, Parliament has 18 such panels.
The bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in the previous session but was not brought for passage after protests by the Opposition and controversy in then poll-bound Kerala. The bill had evoked sharp reactions from Opposition leaders, particularly Kerala lawmakers, as Christian groups alleged they might be targeted under the new law.
Also read: Nagaland CM urges Shah to reconsider FCRA amendments, seeks parliamentary panel review
Bill proposes wider government control over NGO assets
The amendments establish a designated authority for “a comprehensive framework for vesting, supervision, management and disposal of foreign contribution and assets, including provisional and permanent vesting.” A provision stated that the government can appoint a “designated authority” to take over, manage, or sell assets created from foreign funds by a non-governmental organisation whose licence under FCRA was cancelled, suspended, or simply not renewed.
The bill plans to do away with section 15 of the current act that limits the scope of the authority to manage the activities of the organisation, utilise foreign contribution or dispose of the assets created out of it, in case adequate funds are not available for running such an activity.
In the meeting of opposition parties on Wednesday morning, it was decided that the parties will participate in the JPC panel and not repeat their boycott of the panel on the set of bills to automatically remove ministers if arrested for 30 days. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said he told the opposition leaders, “We can’t repeat the same mistake”.

headline: Bengal revokes BJP MP Anant Maharaj’s Banga Bibhushan after Netaji remarks
full_text:
Bengal revokes BJP MP Anant Maharaj’s Banga Bibhushan after Netaji remarks
The decision came a day after CM Suvendu Adhikari warned of strict action against those making derogatory comments against the iconic freedom fighter
The West Bengal government on Thursday withdrew the Banga Bibhushan award conferred five months ago on Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Ray, popularly known as Anant Maharaj, following widespread outrage over his controversial remarks about Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
“The state government issued an order withdrawing and annulling the Banga Bibhushan conferred upon Anant Maharaj on February 21, this year,” said a senior official of the state information and cultural affairs department.
Also Read | Suvendu Adhikari's helicopter makes emergency landing in Bengal's Kolaghat due to inclement weather
Why the decision?
The decision to withdraw the state’s highest civilian award came a day after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari warned of strict action against those making derogatory comments against the iconic freedom fighter, and ordered the police to register cases and arrest the accused.
Anant Maharaj, a prominent Rajbanshi leader from north Bengal, described Netaji as a “war criminal” at a public meeting in Siliguri on August 9, and questioned his leadership and the role of the Azad Hind Fauj in India’s freedom struggle.
A government order said, “The competent authority is satisfied that the continued retention of the Banga Bibhushan by Nagendra Ray is inconsistent with the dignity, prestige and purpose of the honour. Ray shall cease to be entitled to represent himself as a recipient of the Banga Bibhushan and shall not hereafter use, claim or derive any recognition, privilege or benefit specifically arising from such conferment”.

headline: New Delhi: At least half of the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) office-bearers, including those in its national working committee, have had some past association with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). Asked by ThePrint about his past association with the AAP...
full_text:
New Delhi: At least half of the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) office-bearers, including those in its national working committee, have had some past association with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). Asked by ThePrint about his past association with the AAP, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said he was a part of the party but has no connection with it anymore.
Dipke’s AAP link has now come back into focus after the CJP released the list of its national working committee. Of the 12 members inducted into the CJP’s core team, six were either directly associated with the AAP or supported it publicly.
AAP spokesperson Sanjeev Jha acknowledged that some of those associated with the CJP had links with the party in the past, but maintained that they had since moved on, and there had been no recent contact. “Yes, there was a link, but no more. They were with the AAP, but recently there was no contact. They went their own ways to find jobs or study.”
ThePrint tracks the CJP core team’s past association with the AAP.
Also Read: Abhijeet Dipke launches new CJP campaign—‘School Thik Karo’ for ‘neglected’ govt schools
Abhijeet Dipke (CJP founder): In 2020, Dipke joined the Aam Aadmi Party’s social media team, where he said he developed a style of political messaging built around memes, humour and satire.
His experience with the AAP also gave Dipke early grounding in using social media as a political communication tool—something that later became central to the CJP.
In 2023, Dipke moved to the United States to pursue a master’s degree in public relations in Boston, but continued to follow Indian politics closely. He launched the CJP in May this year and returned to India.
The familiarity between Arvind Kejriwal and Dipke was visible when the former Delhi chief minister visited the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar. The two hugged when they met. AAP sources, however, said the party had extended support to the CJP agitation beyond what was publicly visible, including through volunteers, food and other basic amenities.
Ashutosh Ranka (CJP co-convener): Ranka was an AAP volunteer in Rajasthan. He wrote opinion pieces, participated in TV debates wearing the AAP cap. He has maintained that he was never officially a spokesperson of the party, but said he was volunteering for the AAP and had communicated to the party that he was no longer associated with it.
He met Deepak Baliyan, another member of the CJP’s national working committee, while the latter was organising a protest in Jaipur. In March 2026, Ranka wrote an editorial for ThePrint titled ‘AAP liquor case points to what is missing in India: Accountability’.
Ajinkya Shinde (CJP organisation in-charge): Shinde’s appointment as the CJP’s organisation in-charge raised questions, as his social media pages continue to carry his past affiliation with the AAP, listing him as ‘Ex-Convener – AAP Youth Wing (AYW), Maharashtra’ and ‘Sah Prabhari AAP, Goa’.
His Instagram profile, @ajinkyashinde_aap, is now unavailable. His Facebook page has also been deactivated.
BJP leader Amit Malviya also took a swipe at Shinde’s appointment, posting his photograph with Kejriwal.
Vijay Reddy Malangi (media lead and South zone head): In an interview with local YouTube channel Kranthi TV in November 2025, Malangi was introduced as a spokesperson and leader of the Aam Aadmi Party from Telangana. When ThePrint went through his Facebook profile, it found several posts shared by him in support of the AAP.
In some of them, he was seen wearing the AAP sash and the ‘Anna topi (cap)’.
Malangi also shared a statement criticising Raghav Chadha and the other six AAP parliamentarians who switched to the BJP. He did not comment on his affiliation when reached out via call and text message.
Ankit Bhardwaj (in charge, East and Northeast zones): A 12 May 2017 report in the Hindustan Times identified Bhardwaj as an AAP volunteer associated with the party since 2014, and that he had put his chartered accountancy work on the backburner to work for the party. According to news reports from 2017, he had allegedly attacked Kapil Mishra while the politician, by then sacked as a minister by Kejriwal, was sitting on dharna.
A video available on YouTube, titled “Ankit Bhardwaj ke 2 shabd Kapil Mishra jaise dokhebaazon ke liye (Ankit Bhardwaj’s comments on traitors like Kapil Mishra)”, shows him speaking in support of the Aam Aadmi Party. In the video, he addresses AAP volunteers and says: “Main apne Aam Aadmi Party ke saathiyon ko ek baat kehna chahta hoon; niraash mat hona, hum aaj bhi vohi party hai jo 3 saal pehle thi, ye party bauhat aage jaayegi.”
(I want to tell my fellow Aam Aadmi Party members one thing: do not be disappointed. We are still the same party that we were three years ago, and this party will go very far.)
According to the Delhi Police, as reported by Hindustan Times, Bhardwaj had gone to meet Mishra to question him over his criticism of the AAP and Arvind Kejriwal. Mishra and his supporters alleged that Bhardwaj had attacked him. Bhardwaj, however, told the police that he had only been gesturing with his hands during the argument and denied hitting Mishra.
Saurav Das (co-convener): Das is an investigative journalist who frequently tweeted and retweeted content in support of the Aam Aadmi Party and its leaders.
His admiration for Arvind Kejriwal and several AAP leaders was visible through his social media activity, leading to questions about his political leanings.
Also Read: Abhijeet Dipke launches new CJP campaign—‘School Thik Karo’ for ‘neglected’ govt schools
What does the overlap mean
As of now, the CJP calls itself a pressure group and has continued to reiterate that it does not intend to enter electoral politics.
Political analyst and Delhi University professor of political science Chandrachud Singh told ThePrint that the overlap between the two organisations was not surprising given the similarity in their style of politics and Dipke’s own past association with the AAP.
“The fact of the matter is that the Aam Aadmi Party is also kind of something which does this kind of educational politics, right? And agitation politics and the politics of the street, in the way that was done during the Anna movement. AAP is known for this,” he said.
Adding, “The fact that Dipke himself came from that party means that he must be having some connects and some contacts in the party. So there would be people who might be sulking in the AAP or may not be in the mainstream of its organisation. Therefore, Dipke will offer them some chances, and they will be happy to grab those opportunities.”
Singh also said, “It is very clear that the CJP did get support, and you would see that some of the early political leaders who went and met him, I think Kejriwal was one of those, isn’t it? And not only Kejriwal, but I think other members of his party were also there.”
“The bonhomie between the Aam Aadmi Party and the leadership of CJP — the CJP in itself, the organisational part, is quite closer to the AAP and therefore there would be a movement to and fro. I don’t see that not happening,” he added.
Former AAP spokesperson Ashutosh, meanwhile, said the members who had previously been associated with the party should be seen as having made a break with it.
“Since they have decided to form CJP and become its office-bearers, that means they are having a clean break from the AAP and are not happy with the way the AAP is working. They may have had some idealism and hope in the AAP, but over a period of time they felt disillusioned with the party and the political establishment. However, it would be wrong to understand CJP as being launched or propelled by the AAP,” he told ThePrint.
AAP spokesperson Sanjeev Jha, too, acknowledged that some CJP members had previously been associated with the party, but said they had since moved on.
“Yes, there was a link, but no more. They were with the AAP, but recently there was no contact. They went their own ways to find jobs or study,” Jha said.
Who are the others?
The other members of the CJP’s 12-member core team come from varied professional and activist backgrounds.
Deepak Baliyan (organisation co-in charge and North zone head): A political science post-graduate from Alwar, Rajasthan, and has been involved in agrarian movements. He was also involved in organising the CJP’s Jaipur protest and had met Ashutosh Ranka while organising a protest in the city.
Aafreen Nawaz (national secretary): A Bengaluru-based entrepreneur with an MBA who left the corporate sector to work on issues concerning students and young people.
Ratna Singh (legal affairs): A lawyer from Lucknow who has been one of the CJP’s more visible faces, particularly on legal issues involving protesters.
Vaishnavi Gaur (research & policy lead): A lawyer from Dehradun who has emerged as one of the CJP’s prominent spokespersons, regularly speaking about the organisation’s demands and responding to criticism of the movement.
Rohan Deshpande (technology lead): Based in Mumbai, he has a background in hotel management from IHM Mumbai. He has also written on political and social issues.
(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)

headline: Air India to screen all pilots for drug abuse after turbulent flight's captain found 'high'
full_text:
Air India to screen all pilots for drug abuse after turbulent flight's captain found 'high'
Air India stressed the need to go beyond regulations prescribed by the DGCA “ to uphold the highest standards of safety and professionalism".
Air India and Air India Express will begin screening of all their pilots psychoactive substance from Thursday after the commander of a Phuket-Delhi flight that lost altitude sharply last week tested positive for marijuana, even as the Centre is planning to amend rules to enforce stricter action against pilots testing positive for drugs, people familiar with the matter said.
“We have decided to undertake a full screening of all Group pilots for any substances or medications that are not permitted under prevailing regulations. This testing is mandatory and will start today, 13 August 2026,” Manish Uppal, head of flight operations, Air India, wrote in an email to all pilots of the group. HT has seen the email.
“It will be conducted concurrently with training at the Gurugram academy, post flight at our Flight Briefing Centres / Air India Offices, or at locations provided by your respective bases,” the internal communication added.
Full pilot screening begins across Air India group
Air India and Air India Express together have around 5,000 pilots.
The move follows an August 4 incident involving Air India flight AI2379, an Airbus A320neo flying from Phuket to Delhi, which suddenly lost about 300 feet in altitude during cruise. While the case is being investigated by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), the pilot-in-command tested positive for marijuana in an initial, and a second confirmatory, test early this week. A preliminary defect report prepared by the pilots suggested the incident was preceded by multiple technical glitches, including an autopilot disconnection.
Also read: Air India pilot who tested positive for marijuana slept 30-35 minutes during Phuket-Delhi flight
Government weighs stricter drug-testing rules
Meanwhile, people aware of the matter said the government is planning to amend the drug-testing rules for aviation personnel. “The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) will review the existing civil aviation requirements (CAR) on testing for psychoactive substances, with a possible increase in random testing and stronger penalties under the revised framework,” one of the people said, requesting anonymity.
The current CAR, effective since January 2022, requires scheduled commercial airlines, air traffic controllers, flight training organisations and air navigation service providers to conduct random drug tests covering at least 10% of employees annually. The rules also provide for removal from safety-sensitive duties following a non-negative screening result.
India mandates pilots to undergo breath analyser test for alcohol before and after the flight. “The government may look at similar rules for drug testing. The random testing module can also be increased,” a second person said. “While the discussions have just begun, the amendments to the CAR may also look at placing greater responsibility on airlines for ensuring compliance with drug-testing requirements.”

headline: New Delhi: A shuddhikaran (purification) ceremony held at the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani after a rally addressed by Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge on 8 August has created a political stir in Uttarakhand, with both the Congress and Bha...
full_text:
New Delhi: A shuddhikaran (purification) ceremony held at the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani after a rally addressed by Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge on 8 August has created a political stir in Uttarakhand, with both the Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) training their guns at each other.
Speaking to ThePrint, Uttarakhand Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal claimed that the group—Shri Ram Sena—that performed the ceremony was associated with the BJP, a charge that the ruling party has denied. Godiyal went on to ask why no action has been taken so far. The Congress has posted Godiyal’s statement on its official X handle.
Godiyal said it was “deeply distressing and condemnable” that the very stage from which the Congress president addressed the public at the Haldwani rally was the venue of a “purification” ritual by individuals associated with the BJP. “This incident reflects caste-based discrimination and a narrow mindset. The Congress believes in humanity, equality, and brotherhood, whereas such incidents foster animosity and division in society. We urge the Senior Superintendent of Police of Nainital to take cognisance of this matter, conduct an impartial investigation, and ensure appropriate action is taken against the guilty if the law has been violated,” he said in a post on X.
He further said that there is no place for discrimination and untouchability in modern democratic India. “We vehemently oppose such a mindset through democratic and constitutional means. Mahatma Gandhi had said, ‘Untouchability is a crime against God.’ Humanity and equality constitute the supreme religion,” he added.
हल्द्वानी में कांग्रेस की रैली में माननीय राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष श्री मल्लिकार्जुन खड़गे जी ने जिस मंच से जनता को संबोधित किया, उसी मंच का भाजपा से जुड़े लोगों द्वारा ‘शुद्धिकरण’ किया जाना बेहद आहत करने वाला और निंदनीय है। यह घटना जातिगत भेदभाव और संकीर्ण मानसिकता को दर्शाती है।… pic.twitter.com/bAWZyKVTHI
— Ganesh Godiyal (@UKGaneshGodiyal) August 12, 2026
A video of the ‘purification’ ceremony has gone viral on social media, with one of the organisers claiming that a political programme was held there and certain slogans were raised which should not have happened. “This place has been made to conduct Hindu programmes and functions. To use this platform for conducting a political programme and then to give a platform to a person who in the past has spoken about Hinduvadi organisations being like a snake and has appealed to Muslims to kill them, such things hurts the sentiments of the Hindu community. It also violates the sanctity of the place,” said one of the organisers in the viral video defending the purification drive.
Ahead of the Assam elections earlier this year, Kharge had allegedly compared the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and BJP to a poisonous snake, prompting Sangh’s Assam unit to file a police complaint against him for alleged hate speech.
Reacting to the Haldwani incident, Congress leader Salman Soz urged the prime minister to condemn the incident. “This is outrageous and I am so angry! These people are an affront to our society, to our country. They have not only committed a hate crime against my party’s leader and the Leader of the Opposition but against a respected senior member of the Dalit community. We have normalized such hate crimes. It is time to put an end to this nonsense,” he wrote on X.
“[I] call on PM @narendramodi to condemn this incident and direct the Home Minister, the Chief Minister of Uttarakhand and @uttarakhandcops to arrest the perpetrators of this vile act and to hold them accountable under applicable hate crime laws. If Kharge ji has to suffer such indignities, imagine the plight of hundreds of millions of our fellow citizens from marginalized communities who have little or no voice. Let us act together to fight this scourge. Please!”
The incident received flak from other Opposition parties too, including the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD). “The very spot in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, where Mallikarjun Kharge ji delivered a speech on 8 August was subjected to a “purification” ritual! The barbaric progeny of Manu simply cannot stomach the fact that a Dalit is one of the country’s foremost leaders. Does the BJP nurture such casteist bigots? They ought to be banished from the country!” said RJD spokesperson Priyanka Bharti.
A statement issued by the Uttarakhand BJP denied any connection with the organisation that conducted the ceremony. “BJP has no connection with the organisation that conducted the rituals; Congress’s allegations are a diversionary tactic. The Sanatani community is deeply hurt by the objectionable slogans raised by a specific religious group at a ground of great religious significance,” said Khajan Das, BJP Cabinet minister in Uttarakhand and spokesperson. Das said the people of Devbhoomi, as Uttarakhand is called, are furious over the objectionable slogans raised by a specific religious group at the sacred Ramlila Ground.
“The Congress is resorting to caste-based politics and attempts to divide the Sanatan community merely to divert attention from the issue,” he added.
Das claimed that the Congress is making “baseless attempts” to link the BJP with the Shri Ram Sena, the organisation that performed the purification and worship rituals in Haldwani. Das also expressed objection to the fact that slogans specific to a particular religion were raised during the Haldwani rally on 11 August.
“The site where this incident occurred is the sacred Ramlila Ground, which holds immense religious significance in Sanatan Dharma. Raising slogans associated with other religions at such a holy site cannot be accepted or justified under any circumstances. This is a direct insult to the faith of crores of Sanatanis,” he added.
Das said that insulting Dalits has always been the Congress’s nature. “It is not Mallikarjun Kharge who needs purification, but the Congress party’s own tainted mindset,” he added.
“The Congress humiliated figures ranging from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar to its own Dalit national president, Sitaram Kesri—whom they assaulted, tore the clothes off, and drove out of the party office. Babu Jagjivan Ram was also subjected to disrespect by the Congress party. This mindset of the Congress can never be forgotten,” the minister said.

full_text:
Pew survey: What US, UK and others think about India at 80

At 80, India is increasingly a country the world has an opinion about.
As India completes 79 years of independence, its global standing presents a striking study in contrasts.A Pew Research Center survey conducted across 36 countries between February and May 2026 reveals an international community divided down the middle: a global median of 45% of respondents hold a favorable view of India, while 41% express an unfavorable opinion.Read more:80 years on, still enemy No. 1: What Indians and Pakistanis think of each otherBehind this median lies a complex tapestry of geopolitical shifts, historical rivalries, and evolving regional alliances.From enthusiasm in Western Europe and East Africa to frosty hostility in parts of the Middle East and South Asia, public perception of the worldâs most populous democracy depends heavily on where you ask.
Neighbourhood contrasts & global scorecard
Nowhere is this divergence more intense than in India's immediate backyard. While proximity can foster cooperation, in South Asia it has produced antithetical attitudes.Sri Lanka has the most favourable view of India, with 79% of adults expressing a positive opinion.Pakistan sits at the opposite end, with just 7% viewing India favourably. The gulf between the two countries reflects decades of conflict, political rivalry and competing national narratives.Turkey is another major outlier. Only 15% of Turks have a favourable opinion of India, while a majority hold an unfavourable view.
In the West Bank and East Jerusalem, just 18% express a positive opinion.Yet beyond these pockets of hostility, India finds considerable goodwill across much of the world.
as India enters its 80th year as an independent nation, what does the world think of it?
Kenya and the United Kingdom rank alongside Sri Lanka among the countries most positive towards India, with roughly seven in 10 adults expressing favourable views.Majorities in Germany, Israel, Italy, Sweden, Japan and Thailand also see India positively.In contrast, Latin American publics express mixed-to-negative views, alongside substantial shares of respondents who offer no opinion.The findings suggest that India's global image is not simply a reflection of its diplomatic alliances.Economic ties, strategic partnerships, cultural familiarity and perceptions of India's growing global role all appear to shape how people view the country.
India's image is changing
The bigger story is perhaps not where India stands today, but how its image has changed.In most countries surveyed, opinions have remained relatively stable since Pew last asked the question. But in 10 countries, the change has been statistically significant â and in seven of them, India's favourability has fallen.Turkey and Nigeria have recorded the sharpest declines since 2025, with the share of people expressing a favourable opinion of India falling by 10 percentage points in both countries.India has also lost ground in the United States, Indonesia, South Africa and Mexico.The decline is particularly striking in Bangladesh.Pew's previous survey there was conducted in 2024. Since then, the share of Bangladeshis with a favourable opinion of India has fallen by 15 percentage points, leaving fewer than half with a positive view.At the same time, the number of Bangladeshis who do not express an opinion has also fallen sharply, from 24% to just 7%. In other words, more Bangladeshis now appear to have a defined opinion of India â and that opinion has become considerably less favourable.The trend is not uniformly negative, however.India's image has improved significantly in Germany, Britain and Sri Lanka.The share of Britons with a favourable opinion of India has risen 11 points since 2025, while Germany has recorded a six-point increase. Sri Lanka has seen an even bigger jump, with favourability rising 14 points since 2024.Looking further back to 2023 reveals another interesting divide.Across several European countries, India's image has strengthened substantially since the first post-pandemic survey. In Germany, for example, only 47% had a favourable opinion of India in 2023. That figure has now climbed to 63%.France has followed a similar trajectory. India's favourability there has risen from 39% in 2023 to 50% today.Outside Europe, however, the picture is less encouraging.South Korea is one example. In 2023, 59% of South Koreans viewed India favourably. Today, that figure has dropped to 44%.Latin America also tends to lean more negative, although large numbers of people in several European and Latin American countries do not express an opinion at all.
Politics matters too
India's global image is also shaped by domestic political ideology in some countries.The United States and Canada show a striking pattern: people on the political left are more likely than conservatives to view India favourably.In the US, 54% of liberals express a positive opinion of India, compared with 40% of conservatives. In Canada, the corresponding figures are 58% and 45%.Israel presents almost the exact opposite picture.There, 68% of people on the political right view India favourably, compared with just 46% on the left.The ideological divide underlines how perceptions of India can be tied not only to India's own policies, but also to how different political constituencies interpret its role in the world.
A mixed but largely positive global image
So, as India enters its 80th year as an independent nation, what does the world think of it?The answer is neither uniformly celebratory nor overwhelmingly negative.Pakistan and Turkey may give India the stink eye, but they represent the more hostile end of a much broader spectrum.From Sri Lanka and Kenya to Britain, Germany and Israel, India enjoys strong positive sentiment in several strategically important countries.
At the same time, the declines in Bangladesh, the US, South Korea, Turkey, Nigeria and other countries show that India's global image cannot be taken for granted.India's international reputation is therefore becoming more consequential â and more contested.As New Delhi seeks a larger role in global affairs, its challenge will not simply be to build economic and military power, but also to shape how that power is perceived abroad.At 80, India is increasingly a country the world has an opinion about.

headline: Maharashtra FDA suspends licences of multiple facilities linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart over food safety violations

Maharashtra FDA suspends licences of multiple facilities linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart over food safety violations
The regulator directed food business operators selling and delivering food through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed standards.
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the licences of muiltiple food business establishments linked to online platforms including Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after a state-wide inspection drive found multiple food safety and hygiene violations, officials said on Friday.
The FDA inspected 86 establishments across Maharashtra on August 13 that sell and deliver food through online platforms. It issued 60 improvement notices and ordered the temporary stoppage of operations at one facility. No licence was cancelled during the drive, the state regulator said, according to a PTI report.
The FDA also suspended multiple food business licences with immediate effect, including five each linked to Blinkit and Zepto, and two linked to Instamart.
Also Read | Maharashtra FDA action against food outlets continues
Why the suspended licences?
The inspections examined storage and temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, personal hygiene of food handlers, compliance with FIFO/FEFO (First In, First Out/First Expired, First Out) practices, food safety records and the display of licences. The FDA said licences were suspended where serious non-compliance was found.
In Pune, the FDA suspended the licence of a Zepto outlet in Lohegaon after finding several violations. Some food products were stored beyond their declared "Use By" dates, while inspectors also found that FIFO/FEFO practices were not being followed.
The regulator reported unhygienic storage conditions, inadequate pest control and serious deficiencies in the personal hygiene of food handlers.
The quick commerce firm's response during the hearing was found unsatisfactory, the FDA said.
Also Read | HC slams FDA for ‘displaying powers’, revokes stop-sale order against Cadila Pharma
Blinkit and Zepto facilities in radar
At a Blinkit facility in Malad (West), Mumbai, inspectors found the chiller room temperature at 6 degrees Celsius, above the required level.
Around 40 food handlers had also not undergone medical examinations, and records related to the examinations were unavailable, the FDA said.
Several handlers were found without headgear, aprons and gloves. Inspectors also reported disorganised storage, damaged or rusted racks, inadequate segregation of vegetarian, non-vegetarian, cooked and dairy products, and shortcomings in training and food safety supervision.
Inadequate drainage, waste-disposal arrangements
At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, Mumbai, inspectors found inadequate drainage and waste-disposal arrangements, temperature-control issues for frozen products, unprotected lighting fixtures in an unpacked-food storage area and poor housekeeping.
The establishment scored 34 out of 74, or 46 per cent, and was recorded as non-compliant, according to the FDA.
The FDA also inspected Zepto facilities in Mumbai. At its Mulund establishment, inspectors found inadequate waste-disposal facilities, shortcomings in temperature control, lighting and separate storage arrangements, unsatisfactory cleanliness and failure to prominently display the FSSAI licence. The establishment scored 81 out of 180, or 45 per cent, and was recorded as non-compliant.
A reinspection of Zepto's Gola Unit in Goregaon found deficiencies in temperature control, lighting, food storage, personal hygiene facilities and cleanliness. The unit scored 98 out of 142, or 70 per cent, but was still classified as non-compliant, the FDA said.
At an Instamart facility in Andheri, Mumbai, inspectors found some food packets stored directly on the floor. The FDA also reported inadequate storage space, congestion of food products and packaging material, temperature-control deficiencies and shortcomings in lighting, cleanliness and personal hygiene. The establishment scored 76 out of 140, or 55 per cent, and was recorded as non-compliant.
The inspection drive also covered delivery operations.
At a Blinkit store in Karad, Satara district, officials checked 125 two-wheeler delivery riders. They found that the riders did not have identity cards or medical fitness records. The principal food business's FSSAI licence was also not displayed on delivery carts, bags or boxes. The FDA directed the firm to stop business activity involving two-wheeler deliveries until the deficiencies were rectified.
The FDA said the action against establishments operated by quick commerce firms was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the rules and regulations framed under the legislation.
The regulator directed food business operators selling and delivering food through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed standards for food safety, hygiene and storage.

"Patriotism must never be reduced to compulsory conformity," the church council said, emphasising that a citizen's love for the nation cannot be measured solely by participation in a prescribed patriotic expression.
It also stressed that India's diversity of faiths, cultures, languages, traditions and convictions is a defining feature of the country, and urged the state and public institutions to exercise restraint and sensitivity when national symbols or practices carry different meanings for different communities.
The church council appealed to all stakeholders to remain peaceful and cautioned against hostility, intimidation, confrontation and actions that could deepen social or communal divisions.
According to the Nagaland Baptist Church Council, coercion may result in "outward compliance but cannot create genuine loyalty, conviction or a sense of belonging".
It called for dialogue, mutual understanding, accommodation and respect for conscientious objection.
The council appealed to the government and its authorities, educational institutions, student organisations, churches, civil society groups and the wider public to approach the issue with "wisdom, restraint and constitutional sensitivity."

headline: What have I done?: Jinnah reportedly struck his forehead after seeing refugees
full_text:
What have I done?: Jinnah reportedly struck his forehead after seeing refugees
Kuldip Nayar recounts a reported moment when Muhammad Ali Jinnah saw Partition's refugee columns from the air. The anecdote and Nayar's own memories highlight the scale of loss, fear and displacement in 1947.
As Partition tore through the subcontinent in 1947, millions were forced to flee across a newly drawn border amid communal violence, killings and looting. It was in this backdrop that Pakistan founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah, after reportedly seeing streams of people moving across a divided Punjab from the air, struck his forehead and said in despair, "What have I done?"
The episode is recounted by journalist and author Kuldip Nayar in his autobiography Beyond the Lines. Nayar also records his own memories of violence and fear while leaving his ancestral home in Sialkot for Delhi, offering another account of the upheaval that accompanied Partition.
Nayar writes that when Jinnah was in Lahore, Pakistan's rehabilitation minister Iftikhar-ud-din and Pakistan Times editor Mazhar Ali Khan flew him in a Dakota aircraft over the divided Punjab. "When he saw streams of people pouring into Pakistan or fleeing it, he struck his hand on the forehead and said despairingly: 'What have I done?'" Nayar wrote. According to the author, both Iftikhar and Mazhar had vowed not to repeat the remark. Nayar says Mazhar later confided in his wife Tahira, who in turn told Nayar about Jinnah's comment long after her husband's death.
Nayar says the remark came at a time when the scale of the human tragedy linked to Partition was becoming increasingly visible. He writes that Jinnah had initially not believed reports that thousands of people were migrating from both sides of the border. Both the Congress and the Muslim League had rejected the proposal for an exchange of population and had insisted that Muslims and non-Muslims remain in their homes. However, escalating violence led to a massive movement of people across the newly carved borders at Wagah and Attari.
Recalling his own journey, Nayar writes of the devastation he saw while approaching Wagah. "I saw corpses lying on both sides of the road and empty suitcases and bags which bore testimony to the looting that had taken place either before or after the killing," he says. He also remembered the fear as they neared the border, writing, "There was nervousness as we neared Wagah."
Together, the two accounts recorded by Nayar — Jinnah seeing displaced people from the air and Nayar witnessing bodies and abandoned belongings on the road — underline the scale of suffering during Partition. August 14 is observed in India as Partition Horrors Remembrance Day to remember the loss of lives, displacement and suffering caused by Partition and the communal violence that accompanied the division of the subcontinent.

headline: ‘What have I done?’: When Jinnah confronted Partition’s horrors from the skies over Punjab
full_text:
‘What have I done?’: When Jinnah confronted Partition’s horrors from the skies over Punjab
As India marks its 80th Independence Day, the story of Partition remains inseparable from the birth of India & Pakistan -- and the crores displaced by violence.
From thousands of feet above the fractured landscape of Punjab, Muhammad Ali Jinnah saw the human cost of Partition unfold beneath him. In August 1947, from the window of a Dakota aircraft, he reportedly watched endless columns of men, women and children making their way along dusty roads.
Some were fleeing west, others east. Along the routes lay unburied bodies, abandoned trunks, broken carts and the remains of homes destroyed in communal violence.
The sight deeply affected Jinnah, according to an account recorded by veteran journalist and author Kuldip Nayar in his autobiography Beyond the Lines. “What have I done?” the Pakistan founder reportedly struck his forehead and said in despair as he looked down at the streams of displaced people.
READ ALSO | ‘Beginning of another’: How Hindustan Times reported freedom on August 15, 1947
Nayar wrote that Jinnah was flown over divided Punjab by Pakistan's rehabilitation minister Iftikhar-ud-din and Pakistan Times editor Mazhar Ali Khan. Both reportedly decided not to repeat Jinnah's words. Mazhar later told his wife, Tahira, who eventually shared the account with Nayar.
“When he saw streams of people pouring into Pakistan or fleeing it, he struck his hand on the forehead and said despairingly: 'What have I done?'” Nayar wrote.
Estimates of those killed during Partition range from several lakh to around 10 lakh, while more than 1.5 crore people were displaced in one of the largest mass migrations in modern history.
‘There was nervousness’
Nayar himself was among those caught in the upheaval. Travelling from his ancestral home in Sialkot towards Delhi, he recalled seeing corpses along the road and abandoned luggage left behind after looting.
“I saw corpses lying on both sides of the road and empty suitcases and bags which bore testimony to the looting that had taken place either before or after the killing,” he wrote. “There was nervousness as we neared Wagah.”
How British-India broke into two
The Partition of British India was not caused by one decision or one leader. It followed decades of political disagreements, British policies, communal tensions and the growing rivalry between the Indian National Congress and the All-India Muslim League.
At the centre of the demand for Pakistan stood Jinnah, the leader of the Muslim League. But Jinnah had not always demanded a separate country. Jinnah initially supported Hindu-Muslim cooperation and worked with both Congress and the Muslim League.
The political environment, though, changed considerably during the first half of the 20th century. British constitutional reforms introduced separate electorates for different communities, helping institutionalise communal political representation. The Muslim League, founded in 1906, increasingly presented itself as the principal political organisation representing Muslim interests.
There were also periods of cooperation. The 1916 Lucknow Pact brought Congress and the Muslim League together on constitutional demands.
That did not last. The provincial elections of 1937 became an important turning point. Congress was the dominant political force in several provinces, while the Muslim League did not perform as strongly as Jinnah expected.
READ ALSO | Freedom the same night, but different dates: Why Pakistan marks its Independence Day on August 14
Jinnah increasingly feared that Muslims could become politically vulnerable in a united India dominated by a strong central government. By the 1940s, he moved towards the demand that Muslims be treated as a separate political nation.
The Pakistan demand
At its Lahore session in March 1940, the Muslim League adopted the Lahore Resolution, calling for independent political units in Muslim-majority areas of north-western and eastern India.
The resolution did not use the word “Pakistan”, but it turned the idea of a separate Muslim homeland into the League's central political demand.
The 1945-46 elections then gave support Jinnah's position. The Muslim League won most of the Muslim seats, allowing Jinnah to claim that the League had a mandate to speak for Muslim voters.
The last attempt to keep India united
Britain's Cabinet Mission arrived in 1946 with a plan to keep India united while giving provinces considerable autonomy.
Congress and the Muslim League initially accepted the proposal but disagreed over how the provinces would be grouped and how much power the central government would have.
The compromise collapsed and the political crisis soon spilled into the streets.
The Muslim League called August 16, 1946, Direct Action Day. Calcutta witnessed days of communal violence, followed by violence in Noakhali, Bihar and Punjab.
By 1947, the political dispute had become inseparable from communal violence.
ALSO READ | Independence Day 2026: Is it 79th or 80th Independence Day? Theme, significance and history explained
Britain chooses Partition
When Lord Louis Mountbatten became Viceroy in 1947, Britain decided to accelerate its withdrawal.
On June 3, Mountbatten announced a plan to transfer power to two new Dominions - India and Pakistan.
Punjab and Bengal, both divided between large Muslim and non-Muslim populations, would themselves be partitioned.
British lawyer Sir Cyril Radcliffe was given only weeks to draw the new boundaries. The Radcliffe Line divided Punjab and Bengal, but the borders were publicly announced only on August 17, two days after India's independence. For many people, independence came before they knew which country their homes would belong to.
August 1947
Pakistan became independent on August 14, 1947, with Jinnah as its first Governor-General.
India became independent on August 15, with Jawaharlal Nehru as its first Prime Minister.
But independence came with a massive humanitarian crisis. Millions of Hindus and Sikhs moved from areas that became Pakistan towards India, while millions of Muslims moved in the opposite direction. Villages were emptied, homes were abandoned and families were separated.
The violence included killings, looting, abductions and sexual violence. Estimates of the death toll vary, with some historical estimates reaching around 10 lakhs. The number of displaced people ran into crores.
Punjab suffered some of the worst violence. Refugee trains crossed the new border as people fled in search of safety.
Jinnah got Pakistan, but not the Pakistan he wanted
Jinnah achieved his primary objective: Pakistan was created. But the country was not formed as he had envisioned.
Punjab and Bengal were divided, despite Jinnah's opposition to their partition. Pakistan also then sorted itself into two geographically separate wings -- West Pakistan and East Pakistan, with over 2,000 km of Indian territory between them.
East Pakistan later became Bangladesh in 1971.

headline: India-Italy ties strong, remarks should be respectful: Govt on Congress' 'Meloni' jibe
full_text:
India-Italy ties strong, remarks should be respectful: Govt on Congress' 'Meloni' jibe
The MEA's response comes after a remark involving Giorgia Meloni triggered political criticism, as Rahul Gandhi's broader attack on PM Modi's foreign policy also drew a sharp BJP counterattack.
The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday called for mutual respect in diplomatic discourse after Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Sandeep Dikshit made a reference to Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni while taking a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s foreign policy.
MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India’s relationship with Italy had expanded and strengthened “in every way” in recent years, stressing that both sides must remain respectful of each other.
“We have strong ties with Italy. Our ties with Italy in recent years have expanded and strengthened in every way, and it’s important that, as part of diplomatic practice, we strengthen our ties, keeping in mind and being respectful of each other and this mutual understanding between the two sides,” Jaiswal said.
His comments came a day after Gandhi mocked Modi’s approach to foreign policy at the Rachnatmak Congress National Convention in New Delhi, saying he did not understand where the idea had come from that foreign policy was about “hugging leaders”.
Gandhi then hugged Dikshit on stage to demonstrate his point.
“Imagine the ignorance... where did he get the idea that foreign policy was about hugging leaders?” Gandhi said.
Dikshit then joined in, asking Gandhi: “Ek cheez pooch sakta hoon? Meloni samajh ke toh nahi pakda tha?”
Gandhi replied: “I have not reached there yet.”
The exchange referred to Meloni, who has maintained close diplomatic engagement with India and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
MEA STRESSES EXPANDING INDIA-ITALY TIES
Jaiswal’s response focused on the broader India-Italy relationship rather than directly commenting on the political exchange.
He said bilateral ties had grown and become stronger in recent years, making mutual respect and understanding an important part of diplomatic practice.
“We want to strengthen this relationship,” Jaiswal said, adding that the two countries should continue to deepen their ties while “being respectful of each other”.
The remarks come as the Congress’ criticism of Modi’s foreign policy has turned into a wider political row, with the BJP accusing Gandhi of crossing the limits of political discourse.
GANDHI ATTACKS MODI’S ‘HUG DIPLOMACY’
Gandhi had used the convention to question Modi’s approach to foreign policy and accused the Prime Minister of treating personal relationships with foreign leaders as diplomacy.
He also contrasted Modi’s approach with that of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, recalling her interactions with the US and arguing that India’s foreign policy should be driven by the country’s interests.
“From where, it has gone in PM (Modi’s) head that they (leaders) are my friend,” Gandhi said.
He also referred to the US-Iran conflict and argued that India could have played a role in mediating between the two countries.
“A US-Iran war broke out. In such a scenario, if there had been leadership like Indira Gandhi ji, we would have had the biggest opportunity. Because Iran is our old friend, America and Russia are also our friends, so we could have mediated friendship between them. But Pakistan stepped in and took our place, and Narendra Modi just stood by watching,” he said.
BJP ATTACKS GANDHI OVER REMARKS
The BJP has sharply criticised Gandhi over his comments, including his description of the BJP-RSS as a “bunch of jokers” and “clowns”.
BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi accused Gandhi of crossing the limits of political discourse, while other BJP leaders also criticised the reference involving Meloni.
The political row has now drawn a diplomatic response, with the MEA choosing to stress the importance of India’s relationship with Italy and the need for mutual respect as the two countries continue to strengthen their ties.

MEA on Congress’ ‘Meloni jibe’: India shares strong ties with Italy, based on mutual respect and understanding
