headline: Cockroaches, expired food: Maharashtra FDA suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart
full_text:
Cockroaches, expired food: Maharashtra FDA suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart

Inspections uncovered violations ranging from cockroach infestation and expired food to poor hygiene and storage practices.
NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 14 food business establishments linked to quick-commerce platforms Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after a statewide inspection drive uncovered multiple food safety and hygiene violations.The August 13 drive covered 86 establishments across Maharashtra involved in the storage, sale and delivery of food through online platforms. The FDA issued 60 improvement notices and ordered one facility to temporarily halt operations, news agency PTI reported.Of the 14 suspended licences, five were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto, two to Instamart, while one each belonged to Bhagwati Stores and Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd.The inspections focused on storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest management, personal hygiene of food handlers, food safety records, display of licences and compliance with inventory practices such as First In, First Out (FIFO) and First Expired, First Out (FEFO).In Pune, the FDA suspended the licence of a Zepto outlet in Lohegaon after inspectors found food items stored beyond their declared "use by" dates.
The regulator also flagged unhygienic storage conditions, inadequate pest control and lapses in personal hygiene, adding that the company's response during the hearing was unsatisfactory.Another Pune facility operated by Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd was found to have a cockroach infestation, inadequate cold-chain maintenance for frozen products and deficiencies in hygiene and pest-control practices.In Mumbai, a Blinkit facility in Malad (West) was found to be operating with chiller temperatures above the prescribed limit. Inspectors also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone mandatory medical examinations and that records were unavailable.The FDA said several workers were not using protective gear such as gloves, aprons and head coverings. Inspectors also found damaged storage racks, poor organisation and inadequate segregation of different categories of food products.At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, officials flagged shortcomings in drainage, waste disposal, temperature control and housekeeping. The outlet was classified as non-compliant after scoring 46 per cent during the inspection.Inspections at Zepto facilities in Mulund and Goregaon revealed deficiencies related to food storage, temperature management, cleanliness and licence display.
At an Instamart outlet in Andheri, inspectors found food packets stored directly on the floor. The FDA also reported inadequate storage space, overcrowding and deficiencies in hygiene and temperature control.The inspection drive also covered delivery operations.At a Blinkit store in Karad in Satara district, officials checked 125 delivery riders and found that they lacked identity cards and medical fitness records. The regulator also found that the outlet's FSSAI licence was not displayed on delivery bags and boxes.The FDA directed the company to suspend two-wheeler delivery operations at the outlet until the deficiencies were addressed.The regulator said the action was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and urged all food businesses operating through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed food safety, hygiene and storage standards.

headline: India hits back at Norway FM’s Kashmir remarks during Pakistan visit
full_text:
India hits back at Norway FM’s Kashmir remarks during Pakistan visit
India says Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of the country, while urging the world to focus on Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and cross-border terrorism.
India on Friday pushed back against Norwegian foreign minister Espen Barth Eide’s remarks on Kashmir during a visit to Islamabad, saying the world community should focus on Pakistan’s use of illegally occupied portions of the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir to back cross-border terrorism.
At a joint media briefing with Pakistan’s Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad on Thursday, Eide said his visit — the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade — was an opportunity to discuss regional issues ranging from Jammu and Kashmir to Afghanistan. Dar said he briefed Eide on the “long-standing unresolved” dispute over Kashmir and the new dimension added to the “volatile security situation” by India’s decision to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty.
“Let me say that the whole of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh are an integral and inalienable part of India,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a regular media briefing when he was asked about the Norwegian foreign minister’s comments.
“The issue that should concern the international community are the atrocities currently being perpetrated in the illegal Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and the use of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir for cross-border terrorism,” he said.
India has repeatedly criticised Pakistan’s handling of widespread protests over the cost of living and elections to the local assembly in PoK in recent weeks. Dozens of people have died in a crackdown by security forces on the protests led by the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).
Jaiswal responded to another question on Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s remarks criticising India’s decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance by saying that there had been no change in New Delhi’s position on the matter.
“You are aware of our position on the Indus Waters Treaty and there has been no change in that,” he said, referring to India’s decision to suspend the pact following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year.
Addressing an event in Islamabad on Thursday, Sharif said India had “proved itself an enemy of peace” by unilaterally suspending the Indus Waters Treaty. “I declare in clear terms that every drop of Pakistan’s water is our red line. If India does not come to its senses, it will be responded to directly.”

headline: India responds to White House report on Chinese goods transshipment
full_text:
India responds to White House report on Chinese goods transshipment
India says it is studying a White House report that flags the country among major hubs for transshipment of Chinese goods to evade US tariffs.
India on Friday said it is examining a White House report that places the country in the top tier of nations allegedly being used for transshipment of Chinese goods to evade US tariffs, while defending the national framework of laws and regulations to prevent such practices.
The report by the White House’s Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy, seen as part of efforts to prevent Chinese products from circumventing US tariffs through third countries, listed India among more than 40 countries that are perceived to be exposed to China-linked transshipment risks. The report listed India among “China’s biggest enablers”.
“We have seen some reports on this particular matter. We would like to study the findings and the methodology that has been adopted in detail,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a regular media briefing when he was asked about the White House report.
Deep Dive
“We have robust laws and procedures governing customs, rules of origin and exports, and any instances of violation that may be there are dealt with in accordance with law,” he said.
Jaiswal noted that the government had learnt of the US report on Friday morning and is still studying its findings and methodology. “Beyond that, I don’t have, at present, anything specific to add to what I’ve already said,” he said.
The report placed India, along with Canada, the European Union, Israel, Japan, Mexico, South Korea and Taiwan, in Tier 1 of “countries and trading blocs that account for large absolute volumes of China-linked goods while maintaining diversified industrial bases and major US-bound export platforms”.
The report contended that in these jurisdictions, “illegal transshipment risk is embedded within broad legitimate trade flows”.
“The countries that comprise China’s Shadow Transshipment Network include many of America’s largest trading partners. China’s biggest enablers range from Mexico and Canada on US land borders to the European Union, India, Japan and South Korea,” the report said.
The White House also estimated that “approximately $67 billion in US-bound goods were transshipped from China through the top hubs — Mexico, India and Vietnam — in 2025, producing an estimated $28 billion in lost tariff revenue”.
Jaiswal also dismissed speculation that the government referred a bill proposing changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) to a joint parliamentary committee because of pressure from the US.
“As I have informed you earlier and let me reiterate again that legislative matters concerning India are our own internal matters on which the Parliament of India is there to decide, and only the Parliament of India is there to decide,” he said in response to another question.
“I would also urge you that you should disregard mischievous and misleading reports on this particular issue,” he said.
Reports had suggested that US Vice President JD Vance had spoken on the phone with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US ambassador Sergio Gor had met Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval regarding the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 after several American lawmakers expressed concerns about its impact on Christian organisations and charities.

headline: CJI Surya Kant says remarks were misused, warns of social media misleading youth
full_text:
CJI Surya Kant says remarks were misused, warns of social media misleading youth
CJI Surya Kant said his Supreme Court remarks were taken out of context and circulated misleadingly online. He said transparency would continue, but misuse and monetisation of court clips must stop.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has said his oral remarks in a Supreme Court hearing were misquoted and misused with "malicious intent", as he voiced concern over clips of court proceedings being circulated on social media without adequate context. In an interview with DD News, he said such material was being used to mislead the youth of the country and urged responsible reporting of judicial proceedings.
He also said the judiciary was committed to transparency, including through live-streaming of Supreme Court proceedings, but stressed that such access should not lead to misuse or commercial exploitation of court footage. Referring to his recent order, he said unauthorised dissemination, reposting, uploading and monetisation of audio and video recordings of judicial proceedings on social media and other digital platforms should not be allowed.
On May 15, 2026, while hearing a case in the Supreme Court, the CJI had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees to "cockroaches" who become social media or RTI activists to attack the system. The remark triggered widespread youth backlash and inspired the satirical online movement "Cockroach Janta Party" or CJP.
CJI Kant said what happened afterwards was unfortunate and clarified that he could never imagine such things regarding the people involved. "My comment was misquoted and misused. What was not said is presented as though it was said. This is extremely unfortunate. Particularly, it is a major malicious attempt to mislead the youth of the country," he said.
Asking the media to report responsibly on judicial proceedings, he said every citizen had a duty to maintain harmony in society. "You are on social media, print media or any form of media or you are simply a citizen. All of us have rights and constitutional duty and responsibilities. When we speak of rights, we must also possess the capacity to fulfil our obligations. Therefore, I would urge them to keep their responsibilities in mind; we must all make tireless efforts to ensure that harmony prevails in society," he said.
The over-a-month-long CJP-led protests at Jantar Mantar against the NEET-UG paper leak later led to a clash between agitators and police on July 20, leaving several individuals on both sides injured. The protests also resulted in the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as the Union education minister.
The 53rd CJI said transparency in judicial proceedings was necessary, but it should not result in commercial exploitation. "We are committed to bringing transparency into the judiciary. There should be transparency. As a further step in this direction, we started live streaming in the Supreme Court. But live-streaming should not be misused. Particularly, it should not be misused commercially. People misuse small clips for their personal gain, for commercial gain. That should stop," he said.
In sum, the CJI said his remarks had been taken out of context, called for responsible handling of court proceedings in the media, and reiterated that while judicial transparency would continue, misuse and commercial use of court clips must be stopped.

headline: At least six people died and 14 others sustained injuries on Thursday (August 13, 2026) after water and debris entered a tunnel under construction at a hydroelectric project site in Chamoli district of Uttarakhand, officials said.
full_text:
At least six people died and 14 others sustained injuries on Thursday (August 13, 2026) after water and debris entered a tunnel under construction at a hydroelectric project site in Chamoli district of Uttarakhand, officials said.
According to preliminary information shared by the officials, 22 workers were trapped inside the tunnel. Twenty people have been brought out of the tunnel. Of them, six were declared dead, while 14 others have sustained injuries and are undergoing treatment at a nearby hospital. Information about the remaining two workers was not immediately available.
Earlier, officials said 16 workers were rescued after water and debris entered the under-construction tunnel in the Pipalkoti area of Chamoli.
According to the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the incident was reported around 7.05 p.m. Preliminary information suggested that 22 workers were inside the tunnel being built for a Tehri Hydro Development Corporation Limited (THDC) project when water and debris entered it.
Rescue operations were launched soon after the incident was reported. Teams from the Indian Army, Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and SDRF were rushed to the site and raced against time to locate and evacuate the trapped workers.
District-level rescue teams, the local police and Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel were also involved in the operation.
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami expressed concern over the incident and directed officials to carry out the rescue operation on a war footing. He said the government’s priority was to ensure the safe evacuation of every worker trapped inside the tunnel.
Chamoli district has witnessed heavy rainfall over the past several days. On Monday (August 10, 2026), a bridge in the Niti Valley region was swept away after rising water levels triggered a strong current in the river. A video of the incident showed a large volume of muddy water surging downstream and crashing into the metal bridge. The powerful current soon uprooted the structure and pushed it towards the riverbank.
(With PTI inputs)

headline: Amidst the controversy raging over making derogatory remarks at Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, the West Bengal government on Thursday (August 13, 2026) withdrew the Banga Bibhushan award conferred to Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Roy alias Ananta Maharaj, who...
full_text:
Amidst the controversy raging over making derogatory remarks at Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, the West Bengal government on Thursday (August 13, 2026) withdrew the Banga Bibhushan award conferred to Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Roy alias Ananta Maharaj, who allegedly made the comments.
Mr. Roy was conferred the award in February this year by the Trinamool Congress government. A leader from Cooch Behar, he was nominated to the Upper House from West Bengal in July 2023 as a candidate backed by the BJP.
A few days ago, the self-styled leader who is associated with regional Greater Coochbehar People Movement had called Netaji a “war criminal” and questioned his leadership and raised doubts over the role of the Azad Hind Fauj in India’s freedom struggle.
The order issued by the State’s Information and Cultural Affairs department stated that “subsequent to the conferment of the honour, certain facts and circumstances which have arisen/subsequently come to the notice of the Government.... to raise a question as to the continued retention of the aforesaid honour by Shri Nagendra Ray alias Ananta Maharaj and as to whether such continued retention is consistent with the dignity, prestige and purpose of the honour”.
The order stated that the competent authority is satisfied that the continued retention of the Banga Bibhushan by Ananta Maharaj is inconsistent with the dignity, prestige and purpose of the honour and added that consequently, he “shall cease to be entitled to represent himself as a recipient of the Banga Bibhushan”.
After the remarks gave a handle to the Opposition to target the BJP government, the West Bengal government started damage control. Former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee had also held protests against derogatory remarks at Netaji. Political observers say that both the BJP and the Trinamool tried to placate Nagendra Roy for the vote bank he brings along.
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) directed the police to take action against such remarks. “We will not allow this (remarks against Netaji) to be made from the soil of West Bengal. The police will take appropriate and strong action,” the Chief Minister said. One person was arrested in connection with posting derogatory messages on social media. Meanwhile, speaking to media persons in Delhi, Mr. Roy said that his remarks were based on official records.

headline: Sonam Wangchuk seeks 'peaceful revolution' to reshape India's politics
full_text:
Sonam Wangchuk seeks 'peaceful revolution' to reshape India's politics
Sonam Wangchuk has called for a peaceful revolution in how India chooses its political leaders. He said the shift is necessary if India is to emerge as a developed nation by 2047.
Climate activist and education reformer Sonam Wangchuk has called for a “peaceful revolution” in India, arguing that the country needs a fundamental change in the way it chooses its political leaders if it is to emerge as a developed nation by 2047.
In a video message posted ahead of Independence Day, Wangchuk said he had been reflecting on India’s future and was increasingly disappointed by India’s progress compared with several countries in the region.
“Fifty years ago, countries that were behind us or at par with us are today miles ahead of us,” he said, citing Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh in terms of per capita GDP.
Wangchuk warned that if the current trajectory continued, India could struggle to hold its place in the global economy by 2047, the centenary of its Independence.
He also praised people who had recently taken to the streets demanding change, saying their protests had already resulted in the resignation of the education minister. However, he said the appointment of a new education minister had not yet brought any visible transformation.
“As long as education remains backward, the future of the country will also remain backward,” Wangchuk said.
NOT ABOUT ANY ONE POLITICAL PARTY
Wangchuk said the problem extended beyond any particular political party. Referring to protests and government action in different states, he argued that governments across the political spectrum had been accused of silencing voices raised against injustice.
He recalled the anti-corruption movement of 2012-13, which led to a change in government in Delhi, but said corruption and injustice had returned in a different form.
“Now, 12 years later, corruption and injustice have changed their route, but are staring at us, frightening us, in a form two or three times bigger,” he said.
Wangchuk said India therefore needed a “very big change”, which he described as a “peaceful revolution”.
FOCUS ON HOW POLITICAL LEADERS ARE CHOSEN
The activist said the biggest weakness in India’s political system was the way leaders were selected.
“If the leaders are not right, the whole country goes in the wrong direction,” he said.
Wangchuk acknowledged that there were politicians who followed principles and worked with honesty, saying he saluted such leaders. But he questioned how India could become a developed country when many lawmakers face criminal cases.
He claimed that nearly half of India’s MPs face criminal cases and around a third face serious allegations, including murder, rape and kidnapping. He stressed that he was not targeting any particular party or the ruling or opposition camp, but was speaking about the country as a whole.
SEEKS NAMES OF SELFLESS INDIANS
Wangchuk said he now wanted to bring together some of the country’s “best minds” to seek ideas and advice on how India could move towards a new political system.
But he said he was not looking merely for intellectuals.
“I want to meet people who are selfless, who have character and who follow principles,” he said.
Wangchuk, who is currently in Ladakh, appealed to people across India to suggest names of individuals they believe possess these qualities and could help create a “new map” for the country’s future.
He also said he wanted to travel to different states and cities to seek suggestions directly from people.
Wangchuk ended his message by wishing people on Independence Day and appealing for their help in building what he described as a peaceful transformation of India.
“Give me the best gift this Independence Day by suggesting such names,” he said.

headline: Gorakhpur teen fakes own kidnapping, uses AI to extort father for online gaming
full_text:
Gorakhpur teen fakes own kidnapping, uses AI to extort father for online gaming
A Gorakhpur teenager allegedly staged his own kidnapping and sent AI-generated images to demand Rs 1 lakh from his father. Police said the false ransom plot was aimed at raising money for online gaming and involved no real kidnappers.
In a bizarre case from Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur district, a teenager allegedly staged his own kidnapping and used AI-generated images to demand Rs 1 lakh from his father to fund his online gaming activities.
The incident came to light in the Sikriganj police station area when a man informed the police that his nephew had left home and failed to return. Around the same time, several images were sent from the boy's mobile phone to his father's phone, accompanied by a demand for Rs 1 lakh.
Treating the matter as a suspected kidnapping, police immediately registered a case and launched an investigation.
Using call detail records (CDR) and CCTV footage, police teams traced the boy and recovered him safely within two hours. He was later handed over to his family.
During questioning, police uncovered an unexpected twist. According to investigators, the boy, who was allegedly addicted to online gaming, had fabricated the kidnapping story himself to obtain money for use in online games.
To make the plan appear genuine, he allegedly sent AI-generated images portraying himself as a kidnapping victim and demanded Rs 1 lakh from his father. Police said no actual kidnappers were involved and the ransom demand had been orchestrated by the boy himself.
According to information gathered during the probe, the AI-generated images were reportedly created with the help of the boy's girlfriend, who lives in Delhi.
Khajani Circle Officer Deepanshi Rathore said police acted immediately after receiving the complaint and traced the boy within two hours with the help of technical surveillance and CCTV footage.
She said the investigation revealed that the boy had staged the kidnapping and sent AI-generated photographs to support the false claim, with the sole aim of raising money for online gaming. Police confirmed that no third party had demanded money in the case.

headline: President Murmu approves 78 gallantry awards, 13 posthumous, on Independence Day eve
full_text:
President Murmu approves 78 gallantry awards, 13 posthumous, on Independence Day eve
President Droupadi Murmu has approved 78 gallantry awards, including 13 posthumous honours, for personnel of the Defence Forces and Central Armed Police Forces on the eve of the 80th Independence Day. The awards include nine Kirti Chakras, 19 Shaurya Chakras, 36 Sena Medals and honours for Navy and Air Force personnel.
President Droupadi Murmu on Friday approved 78 gallantry awards, including 13 posthumous honours, for personnel of the Defence Forces and Central Armed Police Forces on the eve of the 80th Independence Day.
The awards recognise acts of exceptional bravery across the Army, Navy, Air Force and forces under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The President also approved 89 Mention-in-Despatches for distinguished service.
The 78 gallantry awards comprise:
- 9 Kirti Chakras, including 7 posthumous
- 1 Bar to Shaurya Chakra
- 19 Shaurya Chakras, including 1 posthumous
- 5 Bars to Sena Medal (Gallantry)
- 36 Sena Medals (Gallantry), including 5 posthumous
- 3 Nao Sena Medals (Gallantry)

headline: Indians, Pakistanis see each other as greatest geopolitical threat: Pew survey
full_text:
Indians, Pakistanis see each other as greatest geopolitical threat: Pew survey
Despite some positive sentiments from Indian Muslims, mutual distrust persists between the nuclear-armed neighbours eight decades post-independence.
Most people in India and Pakistan view each other as their greatest geopolitical threat, a testimony to the "continued animosity" between the nuclear-armed neighbours nearly 80 years after their independence from British rule, according to a new survey by US-based think tank Pew Research Center.
Over half of Indians (54%) surveyed named Pakistan as their country’s greatest threat, while 43% of Pakistanis identified India.
Also Read | Indians three times more likely than Pakistanis to favour US: Pew
Majority Indians view Pakistan as threat
The report revealed that 78% of the Indians surveyed held an unfavourable view of Pakistan, including 65% with a very unfavourable opinion. "Muslims in the Hindu-majority country are somewhat more favourable toward Pakistan (21%) than Hindus are (6%)," the report said.
Sharing data on Pakistani's take on the issue, the report said, "Roughly nine-in-ten Pakistanis have an unfavourable view of India, with about three-quarters (73%) saying their view is very unfavourable. This sentiment is shared broadly across demographic groups in Pakistan."
India-Pakistan ties strained
Bilateral relations hit a new low after terrorists killed 26 Indians, mostly tourists, in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam on April 22 last year. India responded with Operation Sindoor, targeting terrorists deep inside Pakistan, and successfully thwarted Islamabad's drone attacks before hitting several Pakistani airbases.'
The government also put the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 in abeyance, saying Pakistan should "credibly and irrevocably" abjure its support for cross-border terrorism first. The move has far-reaching consequences for Pakistan, a country heavily dependent on the Indus river system for 80% of its 16 million hectares of agricultural land and 93% of its total water use.
Also Read | 80 years free, India’s biggest independence challenge is its bureaucracy with colonial mindset
'Skeptical of govts' commitment to maintain ties'
According to the Pew survey, respondents in both India and Pakistan—which have fought four major wars—"are skeptical of how committed the other country’s government and people are to good bilateral relations".
The report involved 3,566 people in India and 1,039 people in Pakistan, alongside respondents in other countries included in the surveys, which were conducted in India from February 8 to April 27, 2026, and in Pakistan from April 8 to May 7, 2026.
The survey found that a majority of Indian adults think the Indian people and government are committed to good bilateral relations. But a majority of Pakistani adults said the Indian people and government are not committed.
Similarly, a majority of Pakistani adults said "their country’s people and government are committed to good bilateral relations", even though Indians thought that the Pakistani people and government were not committed.
Also Read | Partition Horrors Remembrance Day: 7 Films Based On The Horrific Division of India and Pakistan
The report said there are differences in how Hindu and Muslim respondents view Pakistan, with Indian Muslims generally expressing more favourable opinions than Indian Hindus. Pew Research Center estimates from 2020 put the Muslim population in India at about 15%.
According to the survey, around one-third of Indian Muslims (34%) named Pakistan as their top threat, compared with 57% of Hindus.
China, Israel next big threats
Among the global players, Indians see China as a top threat (named by 21%). Pakistanis see Israel (24%) and the US (24%) as their next-greatest threats, according to the findings.

headline: 'Greatest threat': How India, Pakistan view each other; data lays bare deep animosity
full_text:
'Greatest threat': How India, Pakistan view each other; data lays bare deep animosity
Aashish Saxena / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 14, 2026, 19:53 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
A survey has revealed that a majority of adults in Pakistan and India view the other as their single greatest threat.
Nearly eight decades after the 1947 Partition of British India gave birth to two independent nations, deep-seated historical trauma, and territorial disputes that have led to multiple military confrontations continue to shape the mindset of citizens on both sides of the border.As the two countries celebrate their independence, a major survey by the Pew Research Center reveals that an overwhelming majority of adults in both nuclear-armed rivals view the other as their single greatest geopolitical threat.Conducted across South Asia between February and May 2026, the findings highlight a persistent, deep-rooted mutual hostility that shows little sign of thawing. These sentiments reflect not merely political disagreements, but deeply entrenched unfavourable opinions among general populations, extending into perceptions of global superpowers, regional allies, and the long-term prospects for bilateral peace.
'Greatest threat': India and Pakistan point at each other
The data paints a stark picture of two neighbours frozen in mutual distrust.In India, 54% of respondents named Pakistan as the greatest threat to their country.Conversely, 43% of Pakistanis identified India as their primary security threat.
The data paints a stark picture of two neighbours frozen in mutual distrust.
For Indians, China is the next most cited threat at 21%. For Pakistanis, Israel and the US each register at 24% as major threats â though still far below India.These threat perceptions align closely with how each public judges the otherâs commitment to peace.
Most Indians believe their own government and people are committed to good bilateral relations, but a majority say Pakistanâs government and people are not.Pakistanis mirror this: they express confidence in their own sideâs commitment but doubt Indiaâs.
Mutual hostility runs deep
The numbers on bilateral perceptions are stark.Nearly nine in 10 Pakistanis have an unfavourable view of India, with 73% describing their opinion as 'very unfavourable'. The sentiment cuts across demographic groups, suggesting that hostility toward India is not confined to any particular section of Pakistani society.The picture in India is similarly bleak. As many as 78% of Indians have an unfavourable view of Pakistan, including 65% who hold a very unfavourable opinion. There is, however, a notable internal divide in India. Indian Muslims are somewhat more favorable toward Pakistan (21%) than Indian Hindus (6%), and they are also less likely to name Pakistan as their top threat (34% vs 57% among Hindus).
The numbers on bilateral perceptions are stark.
Pew's polling also shows that this is not a temporary shift in sentiment.Indian views of Pakistan have remained overwhelmingly negative for more than a decade, with the share expressing a favourable opinion never rising above 20% since 2013.Historical Pew surveys also show that Pakistanis have long held predominantly negative views of India. Pakistani respondents expressing favourable views of India have generally ranged from single digits to around one-third.
Lack of trust
The survey further suggests that hostility is not simply about how Indians and Pakistanis perceive each other. It also extends to whether they believe the other side genuinely wants better relations.A clear pattern emerges: people tend to believe that their own government and population are committed to good bilateral relations, while doubting the intentions of the other side.
When asked whether the Indian and Pakistani governments and people are committed to good relations with each other, the clear pattern is that people only have faith in their own country
Pew Research report
A majority of Indians believe both the Indian government and Indian people are committed to maintaining good relations with Pakistan. But a majority of Pakistanis reject that assessment, saying the Indian government and people are not committed to good relations.The mirror image appears in Pakistan.
Beneath the geopolitical differences lies a more fundamental problem: the absence of trust.
A majority of Pakistanis say their government and people want good relations with India.Most Indians, however, believe Pakistan's government and people are not committed to improving ties. About a quarter of Indian respondents were unsure.This mutual lack of trust creates a difficult cycle: each side sees itself as willing to improve relations while viewing the other as unwilling to reciprocate.Indian Muslims again stand apart to some degree. Around a third say the Pakistani government and people are committed to good relations, significantly higher than the corresponding share among Indian Hindus.
How Bangladesh, Sri Lanka view the rivals
The Pew findings become even more revealing when India and Pakistan are placed alongside Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.Of the four South Asian countries surveyed, Sri Lanka is the only country that receives more positive than negative ratings from respondents in all three of the others.
The India-Pakistan divide extends beyond bilateral relations.
India, meanwhile, has the widest range of perceptions.Sri Lankans are overwhelmingly positive toward India, with 79% expressing a favourable opinion. In Bangladesh, 42% view India favourably. In Pakistan, however, the figure plunges to just 7%.India is also seen as Sri Lanka's most important ally by a clear majority: 63% of Sri Lankan respondents name India.The picture is very different in Bangladesh and Pakistan, where India is most often identified as the greatest threat.Views of Prime Minister Narendra Modi follow a broadly similar pattern. Seventy percent of Sri Lankans express confidence in PM Modi to do the right thing in world affairs, compared with 42% in Bangladesh and 4% in Pakistan.The survey also finds that Pakistan is not universally viewed negatively across South Asia.Fifty-seven percent of Sri Lankans and 54% of Bangladeshis have a favourable opinion of Pakistan, compared with only 8% of Indians.Bangladesh itself receives broadly positive views in Pakistan and Sri Lanka: 66% of Pakistanis and 56% of Sri Lankans express favourable opinions of Bangladesh. Only about a quarter of Indians do so.Sri Lanka emerges as the region's relative outlier. Around half or more of respondents in India, Pakistan and Bangladesh view the island nation positively, while significantly fewer hold negative views.
Divergent worldviews
The India-Pakistan divide extends beyond bilateral relations to the way each country views the global order.For Indians, Russia remains a particularly important and popular partner. Thirty-six percent identify Russia as India's most important ally, while 16% name the United States.Russia's favourable image in India is particularly striking. Fifty-eight percent of Indians have a favourable opinion of Russia, while 51% express confidence in Russian President Vladimir Putin.Pakistanis are considerably less positive: 39% have a favourable view of Russia and only 32% express confidence in Putin.India's relationship with the United States is also reflected in public opinion. Indians are substantially more favourable toward the US than Pakistanis are and are more likely to express confidence in US President Donald Trump.The picture is almost completely reversed when it comes to China.An overwhelming 90% of Pakistanis have a favourable view of China, while 83% express confidence in Chinese President Xi Jinping. Three-quarters of Pakistanis identify China as their country's most important ally.Saudi Arabia is a distant second, named by 12%.In India, however, only around a quarter of respondents view China or Xi positively. Even Indian Muslims, who are more favourable toward China than Indian Hindus, remain negative toward both China and its president on balance.
Nearly 80 years after Partition, the survey suggests that the India-Pakistan rivalry remains deeply embedded not only in government policy and military strategy, but also in public perceptions.The most striking finding may therefore not be that Indians and Pakistanis dislike each other. It is that both overwhelmingly believe the other side sees them as the problem.That mutual conviction â reinforced by decades of conflict, competing national narratives and geopolitical rivalry â remains one of the biggest barriers to changing the relationship between the two nuclear-armed neighbours.Yet beneath these geopolitical differences lies a more fundamental problem: the absence of trust.Both populations believe their own side is committed to better relations, while doubting the intentions of the other.

headline: Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian to travel to Delhi for BRICS Summit
full_text:
Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian to travel to Delhi for BRICS Summit
The visit assumes significance as India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit under its 2026 chairship.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will travel to New Delhi to attend the upcoming BRICS Summit, Iranian sources said on Friday.
Pezeshkian's participation in the summit is scheduled to be held in the national capital in September.
The visit assumes significance as India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit under its 2026 chairship. The summit will be held under India's theme of "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability". India assumed the BRICS chairship from Brazil at the beginning of 2026.
In October 2024, Pezeshkian met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia, where the two leaders discussed bilateral and regional issues.
Iran became a full member of BRICS in 2024, along with Egypt, Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates. Indonesia joined the grouping in 2025, taking the total number of full members to 11.
Earlier in June, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in India to attend the BRICS Foreign Ministers' Meeting.
Addressing a press conference in the national capital following the meeting, Araghchi highlighted New Delhi's growing influence as a global peacemaker and asserted that India can play a "greater role" in de-escalating the volatile situation in West Asia. Araghchi made it clear that Tehran sees no future in armed conflict.
He stated that there is no military solution to the current crisis and that a "negotiated settlement" remains the only viable path forward.
Underscoring Tehran's openness to Indian mediation, he remarked, "We will welcome any constructive role by India."
Araghchi also held talks with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar where he affirmed that friendly nations can rely on Iran for commercial security.
Araghchi clarified that Iran will always carry out its historical duty as protector of security in Hormuz.
In a post on X, he said, "In fruitful engagement with my host External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, discussed regional developments and clarified that Iran will always carry out historical duty as protector of security in Hormuz. Iran is a reliable partner of all friendly nations, who can rely on safety of commerce."
Meanwhile, the Iranian government said in a post on X, "FM Seyyed Abbas Araghchi delivers Iran's statement at the BRICS Foreign Ministers' Meeting in India. He highlighted the importance of breaking Western hegemony and ensuring that international institutions remain free from political manipulation."
The developments come as West Asia remains locked in a cold, precarious stalemate amid the ongoing hostilities following the eruption of conflict on February 28, which pitted the combined forces of the United States and Israel against Iran. (ANI)

headline: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Thursday (August 13, 2026) flagged concerns over the misuse of live-streamed court proceedings and the circulation of clips on social media without adequate context. He said that some of his oral remarks in ...
full_text:
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Thursday (August 13, 2026) flagged concerns over the misuse of live-streamed court proceedings and the circulation of clips on social media without adequate context. He said that some of his oral remarks in the court had been misquoted and misused with “malicious intent”.
The CJI’s reported reference to “cockroaches” while speaking about holders of fake law degrees during the hearing of a writ petition on May 15, 2026, had sparked a public furore. The remark led to the creation of the online outfit Cockroach Janta Party that spearheaded the recent student protests against examination leaks. The following day, the Chief Justice had issued a clarification stating that sections of the media had misquoted him and that he had the “greatest concern and respect” for the country’s youth.
Also Read | Supreme Court bars unauthorised recording, monetisation of court videos on social media
“My comment was misused… What was not said is presented as though it was said. This is extremely unfortunate. Particularly, it is a major malicious attempt to mislead the youth of the country,” the CJI said in an interview with DD News.
He urged the media to exercise responsibility while reporting on judicial proceedings to help maintain harmony in society. “You are in print media or any [form of media], or you are simply a citizen. Whoever you are, all of us have responsibilities. All of us should make tireless efforts to maintain harmony in society,” he said.
Also Read | News outlets can report courts, but cannot ‘utilise’ audio-video clips of proceedings: Supreme Court order
Referring to the Supreme Court’s July 24 interim order barring the unauthorised dissemination, reposting, uploading, and monetisation of audio and video recordings of judicial proceedings on social media and other digital platforms, the CJI said transparency in judicial proceedings was necessary but should not result in their commercial exploitation.
“We are committed to bringing transparency into the judiciary. There should be transparency. As a further step in this direction, we started live streaming in the Supreme Court. But live-streaming should not be misused. Particularly, it should not be misused commercially. People misuse small clips for their personal gain, for commercial gain. That should stop,” he said.
Also Read | Supreme Court moots protocol to access court’s livestream archives
‘Clips taken out of context’
The CJI expressed concern over short clips being circulated on social media without the context in which a judge’s remarks were made.
“Small clips and certain words of judges have been taken out without explaining the background.. in what atmosphere, in what context those words were used…. without even using the complete sentences, they have been misused. Such instances have come before us,” he added.
The top court had last month indicated that it would frame a protocol requiring users seeking to post or circulate live-streamed judicial proceedings from the Supreme Court and High Courts to access the audio-visual content only through the courts’ archives. The CJI had reiterated in open court that live-streamed proceedings could not be subjected to “misuse” or “commercial exploitation”.
However, activists have sought modification of the court’s July 24 interim order barring the circulation of live-streamed proceedings on social media and digital platforms. They have argued that open access to court proceedings promotes transparency, keeps the judicial process accountable to the public, and acts as a safeguard against arbitrariness.

headline: India and Bangladesh are in talks for an early bilateral visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to New Delhi, preferably before the end of this month or the first week of September, to help in full normalisation of relations. Officials hoped that the...
full_text:
India and Bangladesh are in talks for an early bilateral visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to New Delhi, preferably before the end of this month or the first week of September, to help in full normalisation of relations. Officials hoped that the early visit would pave the way for the renewal of the Ganga waters treaty, energy deals and removal of the trade restrictions that were imposed in May 2025 on Bangladesh.
Diplomatic sources expressed cautious optimism, saying that “positive developments” can take place quickly in the coming few days. Sources in Dhaka expressed satisfaction over the ongoing exchanges between the two sides but cautioned that continued activities by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina or her party Awami League from India have the potential to cast a shadow on fresh initiatives. Sources here also said normalisation will have to be achieved as soon as possible as the diplomatic window may close soon because of other visits and commitments that are being scheduled for the Indian leadership in the remaining four months of the year.
Also Read | Bangladesh urges India to expedite Sheikh Hasina’s extradition
The exchanges between the Indian and Bangladeshi sides began last Monday (August 10, 2026) when High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi called on Mr. Rahman at the Secretariat in Dhaka. The meeting took place against the backdrop of tension generated by the virtual press conference that was addressed by Ms. Hasina and her son Sajeeb Wazed Joy at the Foreign Correspondents Club in New Delhi on August 5, 2026. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bangladesh said it was “outraged” by Ms. Hasina’s press conference and described the event as an “afront” to the “sovereignty of Bangladesh”.
A day earlier on August 9, Bangladesh hosted a delegation led by Parag Jain, Secretary, Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW), the external intelligence wing of the Government of India. In response to Bangladesh’s remarks, the Ministry of External Affairs distanced itself from Ms. Hasina’s event and said India did not “endorse” the remarks that were made at the event against the “duly constituted government of Bangladesh”. The Ministry’s Official Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal further clarified that alongside the invite to Mr. Rahman for the BRICS meeting, India had extended an invite for a bilateral visit on February 17, 2026. This bilateral invite was further acknowledged by Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman on August 10, 2026 after Mr. Trivedi met Mr. Rahman.
Subsequently, Mr. Trivedi visited Delhi and briefed Prime Minister Narendra Modi during Tuesday evening. It has been learnt by The Hindu that the Indian side has conveyed that an “early bilateral visit preferably before the end of the month” will ensure full normalisation of India-Bangladesh ties, including “addressing the water-related issue, energy agreements, visa facilities, and lifting of restrictive measures that were imposed on the textile and food processing sectors of Bangladesh in May 2025”.
It was also communicated to the Rahman government that “if you get stuck with Hasina, you will miss the bus.” It is understood that there has been greater interest of Bangladesh in a bilateral visit for Mr. Rahman and not so much for a participation in the BRICS summit as Bangladesh is not a member of the BRICS and as a result, Mr. Rahman is unlikely to feature in the main round table meet of the leaders of the member countries. Diplomatic sources, however, cautioned that a fresh meeting by members of Ms. Hasina’s Awami League is also being planned by the end of this month in Delhi and suggested that it could hurt positive trend in the talks.
Bangladesh, one of the largest trading partners of India in the neighbourhood, has had a prolonged spell of cold relation with India since the fall of the Hasina government on August 5, 2024. The subsequent 15-month-long interim government led by Mohammed Yunus and his Council of Advisers did not hold important official discussions in areas such as water-sharing and strategic affairs.
India had reached out to Mr. Rahman on February 17 when he was sworn in after winning the February 12 election with a landslide majority. Subsequently, Mr. Rahman has remained occupied domestically with a worsening energy situation that coincided with the Gulf crisis, a measles crisis that has killed hundreds of infants, and tough challenge from the Jamaat-e-Islami that is leading the Opposition bloc in the Parliament in Dhaka. Bangladesh will elect a new President on August 20 and seniormost Cabinet member Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, the choice of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party, is expected to be the new President. Mr. Rahman is likely to have a few days after that during which a visit could be scheduled.

"The government is positive about visits to all countries. But it will depend on the PM's schedule and on how far discussions between the two countries progress," state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam said.
"The government is busy, and so is the prime minister. If everything fits together, of course there will be a visit to India, a visit to Japan; all the visits will happen," she said, referring to ongoing domestic programmes and upcoming constitutional activities.
In April, Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman visited India as part of efforts to mend strained bilateral ties following more than 18 months of heightened diplomatic tensions.
Bangladesh has also sought the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.
External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday that India has extended two separate invitations to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman â one for a bilateral visit and another to attend the outreach session of the Brics Summit in New Delhi in September.
"Brics is still a long way off. A lot can happen in a month,â Shama said.
Asked whether Rahmanâs visit to India could help ease tensions, Shama said direct communication between the leaders of the two governments could provide an opportunity to discuss and resolve outstanding issues.
"Whenever the heads of two countries talk, there is a chance of resolving many problems. That opportunity is there; it remains," she said.
Relations between India and Bangladesh deteriorated sharply after the interim government led by Muhammad Yunus came to power following the fall of Sheikh Hasinaâs government in August 2024.
Efforts to stabilise ties gained momentum after Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, accompanied by foreign secretary Vikram Misri, represented India at Tarique Rahmanâs swearing-in ceremony in Dhaka on February 17.
Rahman assumed office as prime minister after his party secured a landslide victory in the parliamentary elections.
Bangladeshâs current government, led by Rahmanâs Bangladesh Nationalist Party, has maintained that Sheikh Hasina must surrender and face the law if she returns to the country.

headline: A firing incident involving armed civilian members of the Village Defence Guards (VDG) left one dead and another injured in Jammu division’s Udhampur district on Friday (August 14, 2026).
full_text:
A firing incident involving armed civilian members of the Village Defence Guards (VDG) left one dead and another injured in Jammu division’s Udhampur district on Friday (August 14, 2026).
Preliminary reports suggest that a scuffle broke out among the VDG members, trained to fight against terrorists, in Udhampur’s hilly pocket of Pancheri area. Initial information suggests that one VDG member, Surjeet Singh, a resident of Sasri Damnot, fired upon two civilians.
One civilian, identified as Baldev Singh was left dead in the firing incident and another civilian, identified as Romesh Singh, was critically injured. The injured was shifted to a hospital in the district.
Officials said the firing incident was being investigated. A police team assessed the spot where the incident took place and “will prepare a report soon”, officials said. Initial investigation suggests that the firing could be the result of an “altercation”. However, the officials said the police were “still in the process of establishing the cause of the firing”. Meanwhile, the accused was on the run, officials said.
Second incident in two years
This is the second such incident in the past two years in the Jammu region. A woman was left dead in Kishtwar’s Chatroo area after a VDG opened fire in 2025. Two VDG members were kidnapped and killed by terrorists in Kishtwar in 2024.
Earlier known as Village Defence Committees, the civilian armed groups were first constituted in Jammu and Kashmir in 1995 in 10 districts of the Jammu region. The move was made after multiple terrorists carried out the killings of members of minority communities till 2006. Later, it was disbanded. However, after the Dangri attack in Rajouri in 2023, which left six civilians dead and injured 15 others, the Centre decided to revive these groups and renamed them as VDGs. Hundreds of locals in the Jammu region have been imparted armed training in automatic rifles by the security forces in the past three years.
Before 2006, around 26,567 locals were recruited into VDCs in the Jammu region. According to official figures, 160 criminal cases involving VDC members were filed in the Jammu region.

headline: CM Rekha Gupta says Delhi aims to become India's most dynamic urban economy
full_text:
CM Rekha Gupta says Delhi aims to become India's most dynamic urban economy
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta said at the Bhartiya Vyapar Mahotsav that Delhi must strengthen trade and business to support India's growth. She said digital transformation, startups and wider market access are reshaping the economy.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Friday said her government is working to make the national capital the most dynamic urban economy in the country, stressing the need for Delhi to keep pace with India’s rapid economic growth.
Speaking at the Bhartiya Vyapar Mahotsav at Bharat Mandapam, Gupta said trade and business would play a key role in advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat.
She said India, once largely viewed as a consumer economy, is now emerging as a trusted manufacturing hub and a reliable global supply chain, attributing the transformation to the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and policy reforms introduced since 2014.
Gupta also highlighted India’s expanding network of free trade agreements, saying these have helped domestic businesses and industrialists gain greater access to international markets.
She said the country was now moving beyond conventional economic growth towards economic transformation driven by digital technology.
Citing the rapid expansion of India’s startup ecosystem, Gupta said the number of startups had increased from around 100 before 2014 to more than 2.5 lakh.
She also pointed to the growth of digital initiatives such as the Unified Payments Interface and Direct Benefit Transfer, saying technology had fundamentally transformed the country’s economic landscape.
The chief minister said Delhi would need to play a larger role in this growth story by strengthening its trade, business and economic ecosystem.

headline: Cockroaches, expired food: Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart face Maharashtra FDA crackdown
full_text:
Cockroaches, expired food: Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart face Maharashtra FDA crackdown
Maharashtra's FDA has suspended 14 licences after statewide inspections found food safety lapses at quick-commerce facilities and other establishments. The drive also triggered notices, seizures, FIRs and a warning to food businesses to meet prescribed hygiene and storage standards.
Maharashtra’s Food and Drug Administration has launched a major crackdown on food businesses after a statewide inspection drive uncovered serious hygiene, storage and food safety violations at quick-commerce facilities, hotels, restaurants and other establishments.
The FDA inspected 86 establishments linked to online food delivery platforms on August 13, suspending 14 food business licences with immediate effect. Five licences were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto, two to Instamart, while one each belonged to Bhagwati Store and Swinsta ENT Pvt Ltd.
The action came after inspectors found expired food products, poor temperature control, pest infestations, unhygienic storage, inadequate waste disposal and serious lapses in personal hygiene at several facilities.
14 LICENCES SUSPENDED AFTER STATEWIDE INSPECTIONS
Alongside the licence suspensions, the FDA issued 60 improvement notices and ordered one establishment to immediately halt business operations.
The inspections examined storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, hygiene of food handlers, FIFO and FEFO practices, food safety records and the display of FSSAI licences.
Officials said suspension action was taken against establishments where serious non-compliance was detected.
EXPIRED FOOD, COCKROACHES AND COLD-CHAIN FAILURES
At a Zepto facility in Pune’s Lohegaon area, inspectors found food products stored beyond their declared “Use By” dates. The facility also failed to follow FIFO and FEFO practices and had unhygienic storage, inadequate pest control and serious personal hygiene deficiencies.
The FDA said the company’s response during the hearing was unsatisfactory.
At Swinsta ENT Pvt Ltd in Warje Jakat Naka, Pune, inspectors reported cockroach infestation, inadequate cold-chain maintenance for frozen products, temperature-control problems and serious hygiene and pest-control deficiencies.
BLINKIT FACILITIES FLAGGED IN MUMBAI
A Blinkit facility in Malad West was found operating with a chiller-room temperature of 6 degrees Celsius, above the prescribed level.
The FDA also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone medical examinations and that the required records were unavailable. Several workers were reportedly not wearing headgear, aprons or gloves.
Inspectors further flagged disorganised storage, damaged and rusted racks, inadequate segregation of vegetarian, non-vegetarian, cooked and dairy products, along with shortcomings in training and food safety supervision.
At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, inspectors found inadequate drainage and waste-disposal arrangements, poor temperature control for frozen products and unprotected lighting fixtures in an unpacked-food storage area.
The establishment scored just 34 out of 74 marks, or 46 per cent, and was declared non-compliant.
ZEPTO, INSTAMART UNITS ALSO FOUND NON-COMPLIANT
At Zepto’s Mulund facility, inspectors reported inadequate waste disposal, temperature-control failures, lighting problems, poor cleanliness and inadequate separate storage facilities. The FSSAI licence was also not prominently displayed.
The facility scored 81 out of 180 marks, or 45 per cent, and was declared non-compliant.
A reinspection of Zepto’s Gola Unit in Goregaon also found deficiencies in temperature control, lighting, food storage, personal hygiene facilities and cleanliness. Despite scoring 98 out of 142 marks, or 70 per cent, the unit was still classified as non-compliant.
At an Instamart facility in Andheri, food packets were found stored directly on the floor. Inspectors reported inadequate storage space, congestion, temperature-control deficiencies and problems with lighting, cleanliness and personal hygiene.
The facility scored 76 out of 140 marks, or 55 per cent, and was declared non-compliant.
At Zepto’s Lokhandwala facility, the FDA additionally found inadequate temperature control for perishable food, no ante-room for frozen products, poor warehouse layout and improper segregation of food, non-food items and hazardous substances. The facility scored 65 out of 140 marks, or 47 per cent.
DELIVERY RIDERS ALSO UNDER FDA SCANNER
The crackdown extended beyond warehouses and stores to delivery operations.
At a Blinkit store in Karad, Satara district, officials checked 125 two-wheeler delivery riders and found that they lacked identity cards and medical fitness records.
The FDA also found that the principal food business’s FSSAI licence was not displayed on delivery carts, bags or boxes. The firm was directed to stop business activity involving two-wheeler deliveries until the deficiencies were rectified.
MILK PRODUCTS, BAKERY ITEMS SEIZED
The statewide drive also resulted in significant seizures of food products.
The FDA seized 698 kg of milk and milk products valued at around Rs 34,302. Another 1,270 kg of food items, including milk products, bakery products and edible oil, valued at approximately Rs 1,29,762, was seized.
The regulator said the total value of seized goods involving other food items and banned products stood at around Rs 46,89,603.
The drive also led to 10 FIRs over the sale, distribution and transportation of banned products such as pan masala and gutkha. Nine people were arrested and banned stock worth Rs 46,76,631 was seized.
109 HOTELS, RESTAURANTS AND DHABAS INSPECTED
The FDA also inspected 109 hotels, restaurants and dhabas as part of the wider crackdown.
Officials issued 49 improvement notices and suspended four food establishment licences. A total of 15 raids were conducted during the special drive.
BOLLYWOOD CAFE FACES ACTION OVER HYGIENE LAPSES
The FDA also conducted a special inspection at Bollywood Cafe, Studio Number 13, located in Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari, Film City, Goregaon.
Inspectors found serious shortcomings in cleanliness and food safety standards. The condition of utensils and the premises was found unsatisfactory, while a large-scale fly infestation was reported.
The kitchen was found with dirty water, accumulated dirt and food residue. Officials also found food being prepared on rusty and unhygienic food-contact surfaces.
The department directed the cafe management to immediately rectify the violations and strictly comply with prescribed food safety and hygiene standards.
The FDA said penal action was being initiated under Section 69 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
FDA WARNS FOOD BUSINESSES
The Maharashtra FDA said the action against quick-commerce establishments and other food businesses was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the rules and regulations framed under it.
The regulator has warned food business operators involved in selling and delivering food through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed standards for food safety, hygiene, storage and handling.

headline: Former Trinamool Congress MLA Nirmal Ghosh was mobbed outside a police station on Friday (August 14, 2026). A day back, he was arrested from Odisha for his alleged involvement in the ‘hurried’ cremation of the RG Kar rape and murder victim’s dead bod...
full_text:
KOLKATA
Former Trinamool Congress MLA Nirmal Ghosh was mobbed outside a police station on Friday (August 14, 2026). A day back, he was arrested from Odisha for his alleged involvement in the ‘hurried’ cremation of the RG Kar rape and murder victim’s dead body.
Mr. Ghosh was attacked right outside the Khardah Police Station as he was being escorted by the police to produce him at the Barrackpore Court in North 24 Parganas. He was wearing a helmet, but he was still subjected to physical attack, some threw eggs and muck, sticks, bricks, some also threw kicks and slaps. Many protestors carried garlands made of shoes.
The police tried to cover his head with a helmet to avoid any injuries during the transit. Mr. Ghosh was mobbed with “chor, chor“ (thief, thief) slogans outside the Barrackpore Court.
He was sent to 8 days police custody. He has also been accused in another case for allegedly stealing lottery prize money.
“Police promptly arrested the accused from another State. I appreciate the CP Barrackpore for their work,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Friday (August 14, 2026).
Commenting on the attack, Trinamool MLA Kunal Ghosh condemned the incident. “This cannot happen. How can the police allow this? The arrested person has not been convicted,“ Mr. Kunal Ghosh said. He also accused the police of being complacent in the attacks.
Nirmal Ghosh aide attacked
A former Trinamool councillor, Sanjib Mukherjee, a neighbour of the RG Kar victim in Panihati area, was also subjected to similar treatment. He was also being taken to court because he was allegedly present during the cremation of the victim’s body and was also known to be a close aide of Mr Ghosh. Mr. Mukherjee was also arrested on Thursday (August 14, 2026).
Mr. Ghosh, a former MLA from Panihati, also served as the chief whip of the Mamata Banerjee government. His son, Tirthankar Ghosh had fought the Assembly polls from Panihati and lost to the mother of the RG Kar victim Ratna Debnath.
Series of attacks on leaders
The attack on Mr. Ghosh is among the series of attacks that many Trinamool leaders have been subjected to in the past three months. After the Trinamool’s loss in the 2026 Assembly elections to the BJP, many of their current and former leaders, MLAs, former Ministers, and Councillors have been mobbed. Angry masses have raised slogans against them, hurled eggs, bricks, many were heckled, and some were also thrashed in public since May 4.
Among the top leaders, Trinamool chairperson and former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, MLA Kunal Ghosh, and many others have come under attack. Mr. Abhishek Banerjee was one of the first leaders, who was showered with eggs and physically abused by the mob, after which the attacks have been consistent on the others.
Trinamool Congress leaders have repeatedly blamed the BJP for these attacks. However, BJP leadership has denied all such allegations.
The Calcutta High Court had also raised questions about the role of the State’s administration and the police for not being able to ensure the safety of the leaders.

headline: The Nagaland Baptist Church Council (NBCC) has opposed the Centre’s order to play or sing the revised version of Vande Mataram, the National Song, at official events to mark India’s 80th Independence Day.
full_text:
GUWAHATI
The Nagaland Baptist Church Council (NBCC) has opposed the Centre’s order to play or sing the revised version of Vande Mataram, the National Song, at official events to mark India’s 80th Independence Day.
The church body’s opposition follows the Naga Students’ Federation’s call to ensure that schools and other educational institutions do not send their students to participate in the Independence Day programmes. The students’ body also said students who decline to sing Vande Mataram “on grounds of conscience or religious beliefs” should not face disciplinary action or discrimination.
In a statement on Thursday (August 13, 2026) evening, the NBCC said it was against any directive or practice that seeks to compel citizens, particularly Christians, to sing Vande Mataram. It maintained that patriotism should arise from willing participation and a shared love for the nation rather than compulsion.
At the same time, the church body called upon all stakeholders to express their positions peacefully and constructively, cautioning that disagreement over national symbols or patriotic practices should not become a source of communal tension or social division.
The NBCC said it fully respects national symbols, patriotic sentiments, and the constitutional values of India. However, it insisted that matters concerning faith, conscience, religious conviction, and deeply held identity require “the highest degree of sensitivity, wisdom, and respect.”
“National unity cannot be strengthened by compelling citizens to participate in an expression that, for reasons of faith or conscience, they may not be able to embrace,” the NBCC said, reminding the Centre that India was a plural and diverse nation.
“India’s unity will be strongest when every citizen, irrespective of faith, community, culture, or conviction, can say with confidence that there is a rightful place for them in the nation and that their conscience will be respected,” it added.
